[Preference of some days and months over others]

Among this is His preferring some days and months over others. The best of days in the sight of Allah is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr), and it is the Greatest Day of Hajj (Yawm al-Hajj al-Akbar), as in the Sunan, from him (ﷺ) who said: "The best of days in the sight of Allah is the Day of Sacrifice, then the Day of Qarr."

It has been said that the Day of Arafah is better than it, and this is the well-known view among the companions of al-Shafi'i (Ashab al-Shafi'i). They said: because it is the Greatest Day of Hajj, its fasting expiates two years, there is no day on which Allah frees more slaves from the Fire than the Day of Arafah, and because He, glorified and exalted, draws near to His servants on it, then boasts of the people of the standing place (Ahl al-Mawqif) to His angels. The correct view is the first opinion, because the hadith indicating this is not opposed by anything that can stand against it. The correct view is also that the Greatest Day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice, due to His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the Day of the Greatest Hajj﴾

It is established in the two Sahihs that Abu Bakr and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, proclaimed this on the Day of Sacrifice, not on the Day of Arafah.

And in Sunan Abi Dawud, with the most authentic chain: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Greatest Day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice."

Likewise said Abu Hurayrah and a group of the Companions. The Day of Arafah is a prelude to the Day of Sacrifice that precedes it, for on it occur the standing (al-wuquf), supplication (al-tadarru'), repentance (al-tawbah), entreaty (al-ibtihal), and seeking pardon (al-istiqalah). Then on the Day of Sacrifice comes the delegation and the visit (al-wifadah wal-ziyarah). For this reason its circumambulation is called Tawaf al-Ziyarah (the Visiting Circumambulation), because they have been purified of their sins on the Day of Arafah, then their Lord permits them on the Day of Sacrifice to visit Him and to enter upon Him at His House. For this reason the sacrifice of offerings, the shaving of heads, the stoning of the jamarat, and most of the rites of Hajj take place on it, while the acts of the Day of Arafah, such as purification and ritual bathing, are performed before this day.

Likewise is the preference of the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah over other days, for its days are the best of days in the sight of Allah. It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"There are no days on which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days." They said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah?" He said: "Not even jihad in the way of Allah, except a man who goes out with his self and his wealth and does not return with anything of that."

These are the ten nights which Allah swore by in His Book, in His saying: ﴿By the dawn - and ten nights﴾

For this reason it is recommended to increase in them in glorifying (takbir), declaring the oneness of Allah (tahlil), and praising Allah (tahmid), as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So increase in them in takbir, tahlil and tahmid." Their relation to the days is like the relation of the places of the rites to the rest of the lands.

(Benefit)

The Prophet's ﷺ saying, when Qutaylah bint al-Harith recited to him her well-known poem lamenting her brother al-Nadr:

"Had I heard this before I killed him, I would not have killed him."

It does not express regret for killing him, for he had only killed him rightfully. Rather, he was merciful, accepting intercession and showing grace to the offender. So its meaning is: had she interceded with me by means of what she said before I killed him, I would have accepted her intercession and spared him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verses 7–12 (part 1 of 2):

[Section: The covenant of the People of Dhimma lasts only as long as they remain upright towards us]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can there be a covenant with the polytheists in the sight of Allah and in the sight of His Messenger?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 7] up to His saying: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths, so that they may desist﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12].

Allah negated that there could be a covenant for any polytheist from those with whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had made a covenant, except for a people whom He mentioned, for whom He made a covenant "as long as they remain upright towards us." It is thus known that a covenant does not remain for the polytheist except as long as he remains upright. It is well known that openly committing those great matters (of enmity) undermines uprightness, just as openly displaying uprightness in them would. Indeed, openly reviling our Lord, our Prophet and His Book, and burning our mosques and homes, is more grievous to us than openly waging war against us, if we are believers, for it is obligatory upon us to spend our lives and our wealth until the Word of Allah is supreme and nothing of the harm done to Allah and His Messenger is openly displayed among us. So if they are not upright towards us while disparaging the lesser of the two matters, how could they be upright towards us while disparaging the greater of them?

This is clarified by His saying: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you, they observe neither ties of kinship nor covenant towards you?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 8] That is: how could there be a covenant for them, when if they gained the upper hand over you they would not observe the ties of kinship between you and them, nor the covenant? It is thus known that whoever's condition is that, if he gains the upper hand, he does not observe the covenant between us and him, then there is no covenant for him. And whoever openly attacks our religion and reviles our Lord and our Prophet, that is among the strongest proofs that if he gained the upper hand over us he would not observe the covenant between us and him. For if this is his conduct while the covenant and humiliation exist, how would it be when he has power and dominion? This is in contrast to one who has not openly shown us any of that; he may be expected to keep the covenant with us even if he gains the upper hand.

If it is said: the verse only concerns the people of truce who reside in their own land. The answer is in two respects:
First: its wording is more general.
Second: if its meaning applies to the People of Dhimma residing in their own land, then its applying to the People of Dhimma residing in our land is more fitting and more applicable.

[Section: The covenant is annulled by their breaking of their oaths]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12].

Allah commanded fighting against one who breaks his oath, that is, his covenant by which he pledged to us to refrain from harming us and from reviling our religion. He made the cause of fighting him that, and He coupled reviling the religion with breaking the covenant and singled it out for mention, to make clear that it is among the strongest causes that necessitate fighting. For this reason, the punishment for its perpetrator is made severe. This was the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he would make lawful the blood of whoever harmed Allah and His Messenger and reviled the religion, while refraining from others.

If it is said: the verse indicates that whoever breaks his covenant and reviles the religion is to be fought; from where do you derive that whoever reviles the religion without breaking the covenant is not to be fought? It is known that a ruling tied to two attributes does not take effect except by the presence of one of them. The answer comes in several ways:

The first: this is a case of tying a ruling to two mutually entailing attributes, neither of which is separated from the other; whenever one of them is realised, the other is realised too. This is like His saying: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has chosen﴾ [al-Nisa: 115], and His saying: ﴿And do not mix truth with falsehood or conceal the truth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 42], and His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾ [al-Nisa: 14], and its counterparts are very numerous. Thus it is inconceivable that he remains upon the covenant while reviling our religion. Rather, his remaining upon the covenant while still holding to the religion is more likely than his remaining upon the covenant while openly reviling the religion. Indeed, if it is possible for him to remain upon the covenant while openly reviling the religion and the sunnah of Allah and His Messenger, it is possible for him to remain upon it while waging war with his hand and withholding payment of the jizya. This is clear and there is no obscurity in it.

The second answer: each of these two attributes must have its own bearing on the ruling as it is specified; otherwise an attribute with no effect would not be tied to a ruling, and it would not be correct to say: "Whoever eats and commits fornication is flogged." Moreover, each attribute may be independently effective if it stood alone, as when it is said: "This man is to be killed because he is an adulterer and an apostate." Sometimes the whole of the penalty is arranged upon the whole of the attributes, and each attribute has an effect on part of it, as Allah says: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].

These attributes may also be mutually entailing, each of which, if considered in isolation, would be effective independently; so it is mentioned to clarify and explain the cause of the ruling.

Sometimes some of them entail others without the converse, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ [Aal Imran: 21]. Whatever category this verse is taken to fall under, it serves as evidence; for at most it is said that breaking the covenant is what makes fighting lawful, and reviling the religion reinforces it and necessitates it. We say: if reviling makes fighting one with whom we have no covenant more severe and necessary, then it is all the more necessary to kill one with whom we have a dhimma, who is bound to submit to humiliation. For a muʿahid (treaty partner) may display in his own land whatever he wishes of his religion, whereas a dhimmi is not permitted to display anything of his false religion in the land of Islam.

The third answer: the mere breaking of oaths necessitates fighting even if it is stripped of reviling the religion, and its harm to us is greater than the harm of reviling the religion. So if the lesser of the two matters requires fighting, how much more so the greater of them?

The fourth answer: if a dhimmi openly reviles Allah and the Messenger or disparages Islam, he has broken his oath and reviled our religion. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that he is to be punished for this with what deters him and makes an example of him. It is thus known that this was not part of what we covenanted with him; for if it were a term of the covenant, his punishment for it would not be permissible, just as one is not punished for drinking wine or eating pork and the like. Since we made a covenant with him that he would not revile our religion, and he reviled it, then he has broken his oath after his covenant, and it is obligatory to kill him by the explicit text of the verse.

Our shaykh said: this is a very clear proof, because the opponent concedes to us that he is forbidden from that by the covenant between us and him, but he says: "Not everything he is forbidden from breaks his covenant, such as displaying wine and pork." But the difference is between one who does something the covenant forbids which does not clearly harm us, such as failing to wear the distinguishing belt, drinking wine, or displaying pork, and one who does something the covenant forbids which carries the utmost harm to the Muslims and to the religion. Equating one with the other is invalid.

This is further clarified by the fifth answer: breaking the covenant is violating the agreement. Whenever they violate something they were settled upon, it is a breaking (nakth), derived from the breaking of a rope, which is the undoing of its strands. The breaking of a rope occurs by the undoing of one strand just as it occurs by the undoing of all the strands; but some of its strength may remain by which the rope is still held, and sometimes it is wholly weakened. This violation by a treaty partner may completely nullify the covenant, making him an enemy combatant, or it may loosen the covenant so as to permit punishing them, just as the lack of some conditions in sale, marriage and other contracts may nullify them entirely, or may permit their annulment or continuation.

As for the one who says: "The covenant is broken by every violation," this is evident according to an opinion held by al-Qadi in al-Ta'liq.

Al-Qadi argued that if they displayed something abhorrent in the land of Islam, such as building churches and synagogues in the land of Islam, raising their voices with their books, striking the clappers, extending their buildings over the dwellings of the Muslims, and displaying wine and pork, and likewise what they were required to abandon of imitating the Muslims in their clothing, their mounts, their hairstyles and their kunyas.

He said: The answer is that among our companions are those who consider these things to break the covenant, and this is the apparent meaning of al-Kharaqi's words, for he said: "Whoever breaks the covenant by violating something they were settled upon becomes an enemy combatant." On this basis, we do not concede. And even if we concede it, these things are such that it is clear there is no harm to the Muslims in them; they were only forbidden from doing them because displaying them is abhorrent. This is not the case in our religion, because doing them harms the Muslims; thus the difference is evident. End of his words.

Our shaykh said: On either view, the contract requires that they not display anything of the defects of our religion; and whenever they display it, they have broken the covenant and reviled the religion, and so they fall within the general scope of the verse both in wording and in meaning. Such a general application reaches the level of an explicit text.

[Section: Everyone who reviles our religion is among the leaders of disbelief]

There is another proof in the verse from a different angle, namely His saying: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12]. They are those who broke their oaths after their covenant and reviled our religion. But the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun between the two, on the attribute by which they deserve fighting, like His saying: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾ [al-A'raf: 170] and its counterparts. This indicates that whoever breaks his oath and reviles our religion is among the leaders of disbelief, and a leader of disbelief is one who calls to it and is followed in it.

He became a leader in disbelief only because of the reviling; otherwise mere breaking of the oath would not necessitate that, and this is clear. For one who reviles the religion disparages it, condemns it and calls to opposing it, and this is the role of a leader. So when a dhimmi reviles the religion, he becomes a leader in disbelief, and it is obligatory to fight him.

His saying: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12] is another reason for fighting them. As for the reading with a kasra (innahum), the verse then contains the mention of what necessitates fighting, namely breaking the covenant and reviling the religion, and the statement that there is no preventive barrier to fighting, namely a protecting faith.

As for the reading with a fatha on the alif (aymanun, plural of yamin), and it is the better of the two readings, since His saying appeared earlier in the verse: ﴿and if they break their oaths﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12]; He informed of the cause of fighting, namely the breaking of oaths and the reviling of the religion, then informed that they have no oaths that would protect them from being killed, because they have broken them.

By "oaths" here are meant covenants, not swearing by Allah; for the Prophet (ﷺ) did not swear an oath to them by Allah at al-Hudaybiyya, but made a covenant with them, and the copy of the document is preserved and contains no oath. This is because each of the two parties to a covenant extends his right hand to the other, and then the mere speech of covenant came to be called a "yamin" (oath/right hand), even if no hand was extended.

It has also been said that the covenant was called a yamin because yamin means strength and firmness, as Allah says: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45]. And since an oath is tied and bound, it is called a yamin. Thus the term yamin encompasses the covenant between the servant and his Lord, even if it is a vow (nadhr), as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A vow is an oath." It also encompasses the covenant between created beings, as in His saying: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ [al-Nahl: 91]; so the prohibition is against breaking covenants even if no oath is sworn in them. And He said: ﴿And who fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 10], even though there is no oath there. And from this is His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [al-Nisa: 1].

Its meaning: they make a pact with one another and bind themselves by it. The point is that anyone who reviles our religion after we have made a covenant with him, a covenant that requires him not to do so, is a leader of disbelief (imam fi al-kufr) with no oath binding him. For that reason he must be killed, by the explicit text of the verse. This also clarifies the difference between him and the oath-breaker (nakith) who is not a leader of disbelief, meaning one who violates some term that was agreed upon in a treaty by doing something.

[Section: The intention to expel the Messenger makes fighting them obligatory]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 13]. Here He made their resolve to expel the Messenger a reason that makes fighting them obligatory, because of the harm it contains for him.

It is certain that reviling him is a far greater harm to him than merely expelling him from his land. For this reason, on the day of the Conquest (ʿam al-fath), he (ﷺ) pardoned those who had resolved to expel him, but he did not pardon the one who reviled him. Therefore, when a dhimmi (a non-Muslim under the protection of the Muslim state) openly reviles him, he has broken his covenant and done something greater than resolving to expel the Messenger, and he has begun the harm, so fighting him is obligatory.

[Section: The command to fight the oath-breakers who attack the religion]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people, and remove the rage from their hearts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14–15].

So He commanded the fighting of the oath-breakers who attack the religion, and He attached several results to that: their punishment through your hands, their humiliation, your victory over them, the healing of the believers' breasts, the removal of the rage in their hearts, and His turning (in mercy) to whomever He wills among others. The implication is: if you fight them, these things will come about.

Since these matters are attached to fighting the oath-breaker and the one who attacks the religion, and since they are desired matters, their cause which necessitates them is also desired by the Lawgiver, namely fighting. And since these matters are desired and are achieved through fighting, it is not permissible to suspend the fighting, which is their cause, while the reason for it exists on the part of those who are fought, namely oath-breaking and attacking the religion.

The healing of hearts that results from the pain of oath-breaking and attack on the religion, and the removal of the rage that arises in the believers' breasts because of it, are intended by the Lawgiver and are required to be achieved. There is no doubt that whoever among the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimma) openly reviles the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enrages and pains the believers far more than shedding the blood of some of them or seizing their property. This is because it stirs anger for the sake of Allah and zeal for Him and His Messenger.

This degree of rage does not stir in the heart of a believer any greater than this, and the upright believer does not become angry with such anger except for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. Allah, exalted is He, loves the healing of the believers' breasts and the removal of rage from their hearts, and this is achieved only by killing the reviler, for several reasons:

First: their ta'zir (discretionary punishment) and disciplining would remove the rage in their hearts if he insults one of the Muslims. If ta'zir and discipline removed their rage when he insults the Messenger, their rage at insulting their Prophet would be like their rage at insulting one of themselves. This is definitely false.

Second: insulting him is greater in their eyes than that some of them should shed the blood of others. Moreover, if one of them killed (the reviler), that would not heal their breasts except by his killing. So it is more fitting and more appropriate that their breasts be healed only by killing the reviler.

Third: Allah made their fighting the cause of achieving healing, and the default is the absence of any other cause that would bring it about. Therefore, killing must be what heals the believers' breasts from such a thing.

Fourth: when Mecca was conquered and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to heal the breasts of Khuza'a, who were the believing people, from Banu Bakr, who had fought them, he gave them power over them at midday or later, while he had granted safety (aman) to all the other people. If the healing of their breasts and the removal of rage from their hearts could have been achieved without killing those who had broken oaths or attacked, he would not have done that while granting safety to the people.

First: its wording is more general.

We say: if reviling makes fighting one with whom we have no covenant more severe and necessary, then it is all the more necessary to kill one with whom we have a dhimma, who is bound to submit to humiliation. For a muʿahid (treaty partner) may display in his own land whatever he wishes of his religion, whereas a dhimmi is not permitted to display anything of his false religion in the land of Islam.

They are those who broke their oaths after their covenant and reviled our religion. [Section: The command to fight the oath-breakers who attack the religion]

[Section: The covenant of the People of Dhimma lasts only as long as they remain upright towards us]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can there be a covenant with the polytheists in the sight of Allah and in the sight of His Messenger?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 7] up to His saying: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths, so that they may desist﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12].

Allah negated that there could be a covenant for any polytheist from those with whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had made a covenant, except for a people whom He mentioned, for whom He made a covenant "as long as they remain upright towards us." It is thus known that a covenant does not remain for the polytheist except as long as he remains upright. It is well known that openly committing those great matters (of enmity) undermines uprightness, just as openly displaying uprightness in them would. Indeed, openly reviling our Lord, our Prophet and His Book, and burning our mosques and homes, is more grievous to us than openly waging war against us, if we are believers, for it is obligatory upon us to spend our lives and our wealth until the Word of Allah is supreme and nothing of the harm done to Allah and His Messenger is openly displayed among us. So if they are not upright towards us while disparaging the lesser of the two matters, how could they be upright towards us while disparaging the greater of them?

This is clarified by His saying: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you, they observe neither ties of kinship nor covenant towards you?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 8] That is: how could there be a covenant for them, when if they gained the upper hand over you they would not observe the ties of kinship between you and them, nor the covenant? It is thus known that whoever's condition is that, if he gains the upper hand, he does not observe the covenant between us and him, then there is no covenant for him. And whoever openly attacks our religion and reviles our Lord and our Prophet, that is among the strongest proofs that if he gained the upper hand over us he would not observe the covenant between us and him. For if this is his conduct while the covenant and humiliation exist, how would it be when he has power and dominion? This is in contrast to one who has not openly shown us any of that; he may be expected to keep the covenant with us even if he gains the upper hand.

If it is said: the verse only concerns the people of truce who reside in their own land. The answer is in two respects:
First: its wording is more general.
Second: if its meaning applies to the People of Dhimma residing in their own land, then its applying to the People of Dhimma residing in our land is more fitting and more applicable.

[Section: The covenant is annulled by their breaking of their oaths]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and revile your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12].

Allah commanded fighting against one who breaks his oath, that is, his covenant by which he pledged to us to refrain from harming us and from reviling our religion. He made the cause of fighting him that, and He coupled reviling the religion with breaking the covenant and singled it out for mention, to make clear that it is among the strongest causes that necessitate fighting. For this reason, the punishment for its perpetrator is made severe. This was the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): he would make lawful the blood of whoever harmed Allah and His Messenger and reviled the religion, while refraining from others.

If it is said: the verse indicates that whoever breaks his covenant and reviles the religion is to be fought; from where do you derive that whoever reviles the religion without breaking the covenant is not to be fought? It is known that a ruling tied to two attributes does not take effect except by the presence of one of them. The answer comes in several ways:

The first: this is a case of tying a ruling to two mutually entailing attributes, neither of which is separated from the other; whenever one of them is realised, the other is realised too. This is like His saying: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has chosen﴾ [al-Nisa: 115], and His saying: ﴿And do not mix truth with falsehood or conceal the truth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 42], and His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein﴾ [al-Nisa: 14], and its counterparts are very numerous. Thus it is inconceivable that he remains upon the covenant while reviling our religion. Rather, his remaining upon the covenant while still holding to the religion is more likely than his remaining upon the covenant while openly reviling the religion. Indeed, if it is possible for him to remain upon the covenant while openly reviling the religion and the sunnah of Allah and His Messenger, it is possible for him to remain upon it while waging war with his hand and withholding payment of the jizya. This is clear and there is no obscurity in it.

The second answer: each of these two attributes must have its own bearing on the ruling as it is specified; otherwise an attribute with no effect would not be tied to a ruling, and it would not be correct to say: "Whoever eats and commits fornication is flogged." Moreover, each attribute may be independently effective if it stood alone, as when it is said: "This man is to be killed because he is an adulterer and an apostate." Sometimes the whole of the penalty is arranged upon the whole of the attributes, and each attribute has an effect on part of it, as Allah says: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].

These attributes may also be mutually entailing, each of which, if considered in isolation, would be effective independently; so it is mentioned to clarify and explain the cause of the ruling.

Sometimes some of them entail others without the converse, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right﴾ [Aal Imran: 21]. Whatever category this verse is taken to fall under, it serves as evidence; for at most it is said that breaking the covenant is what makes fighting lawful, and reviling the religion reinforces it and necessitates it. We say: if reviling makes fighting one with whom we have no covenant more severe and necessary, then it is all the more necessary to kill one with whom we have a dhimma, who is bound to submit to humiliation. For a muʿahid (treaty partner) may display in his own land whatever he wishes of his religion, whereas a dhimmi is not permitted to display anything of his false religion in the land of Islam.

The third answer: the mere breaking of oaths necessitates fighting even if it is stripped of reviling the religion, and its harm to us is greater than the harm of reviling the religion. So if the lesser of the two matters requires fighting, how much more so the greater of them?

The fourth answer: if a dhimmi openly reviles Allah and the Messenger or disparages Islam, he has broken his oath and reviled our religion. There is no disagreement among the Muslims that he is to be punished for this with what deters him and makes an example of him. It is thus known that this was not part of what we covenanted with him; for if it were a term of the covenant, his punishment for it would not be permissible, just as one is not punished for drinking wine or eating pork and the like. Since we made a covenant with him that he would not revile our religion, and he reviled it, then he has broken his oath after his covenant, and it is obligatory to kill him by the explicit text of the verse.

Our shaykh said: this is a very clear proof, because the opponent concedes to us that he is forbidden from that by the covenant between us and him, but he says: "Not everything he is forbidden from breaks his covenant, such as displaying wine and pork." But the difference is between one who does something the covenant forbids which does not clearly harm us, such as failing to wear the distinguishing belt, drinking wine, or displaying pork, and one who does something the covenant forbids which carries the utmost harm to the Muslims and to the religion. Equating one with the other is invalid.

This is further clarified by the fifth answer: breaking the covenant is violating the agreement. Whenever they violate something they were settled upon, it is a breaking (nakth), derived from the breaking of a rope, which is the undoing of its strands. The breaking of a rope occurs by the undoing of one strand just as it occurs by the undoing of all the strands; but some of its strength may remain by which the rope is still held, and sometimes it is wholly weakened. This violation by a treaty partner may completely nullify the covenant, making him an enemy combatant, or it may loosen the covenant so as to permit punishing them, just as the lack of some conditions in sale, marriage and other contracts may nullify them entirely, or may permit their annulment or continuation.

As for the one who says: "The covenant is broken by every violation," this is evident according to an opinion held by al-Qadi in al-Ta'liq.

Al-Qadi argued that if they displayed something abhorrent in the land of Islam, such as building churches and synagogues in the land of Islam, raising their voices with their books, striking the clappers, extending their buildings over the dwellings of the Muslims, and displaying wine and pork, and likewise what they were required to abandon of imitating the Muslims in their clothing, their mounts, their hairstyles and their kunyas.

He said: The answer is that among our companions are those who consider these things to break the covenant, and this is the apparent meaning of al-Kharaqi's words, for he said: "Whoever breaks the covenant by violating something they were settled upon becomes an enemy combatant." On this basis, we do not concede. And even if we concede it, these things are such that it is clear there is no harm to the Muslims in them; they were only forbidden from doing them because displaying them is abhorrent. This is not the case in our religion, because doing them harms the Muslims; thus the difference is evident. End of his words.

Our shaykh said: On either view, the contract requires that they not display anything of the defects of our religion; and whenever they display it, they have broken the covenant and reviled the religion, and so they fall within the general scope of the verse both in wording and in meaning. Such a general application reaches the level of an explicit text.

[Section: Everyone who reviles our religion is among the leaders of disbelief]

There is another proof in the verse from a different angle, namely His saying: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12]. They are those who broke their oaths after their covenant and reviled our religion. But the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun between the two, on the attribute by which they deserve fighting, like His saying: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer, indeed We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾ [al-A'raf: 170] and its counterparts. This indicates that whoever breaks his oath and reviles our religion is among the leaders of disbelief, and a leader of disbelief is one who calls to it and is followed in it.

He became a leader in disbelief only because of the reviling; otherwise mere breaking of the oath would not necessitate that, and this is clear. For one who reviles the religion disparages it, condemns it and calls to opposing it, and this is the role of a leader. So when a dhimmi reviles the religion, he becomes a leader in disbelief, and it is obligatory to fight him.

His saying: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12] is another reason for fighting them. As for the reading with a kasra (innahum), the verse then contains the mention of what necessitates fighting, namely breaking the covenant and reviling the religion, and the statement that there is no preventive barrier to fighting, namely a protecting faith.

As for the reading with a fatha on the alif (aymanun, plural of yamin), and it is the better of the two readings, since His saying appeared earlier in the verse: ﴿and if they break their oaths﴾ [al-Tawbah: 12]; He informed of the cause of fighting, namely the breaking of oaths and the reviling of the religion, then informed that they have no oaths that would protect them from being killed, because they have broken them.

By "oaths" here are meant covenants, not swearing by Allah; for the Prophet (ﷺ) did not swear an oath to them by Allah at al-Hudaybiyya, but made a covenant with them, and the copy of the document is preserved and contains no oath. This is because each of the two parties to a covenant extends his right hand to the other, and then the mere speech of covenant came to be called a "yamin" (oath/right hand), even if no hand was extended.

It has also been said that the covenant was called a yamin because yamin means strength and firmness, as Allah says: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45]. And since an oath is tied and bound, it is called a yamin. Thus the term yamin encompasses the covenant between the servant and his Lord, even if it is a vow (nadhr), as in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A vow is an oath." It also encompasses the covenant between created beings, as in His saying: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ [al-Nahl: 91]; so the prohibition is against breaking covenants even if no oath is sworn in them. And He said: ﴿And who fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 10], even though there is no oath there. And from this is His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [al-Nisa: 1].

Its meaning: they make a pact with one another and bind themselves by it. The point is that anyone who reviles our religion after we have made a covenant with him, a covenant that requires him not to do so, is a leader of disbelief (imam fi al-kufr) with no oath binding him. For that reason he must be killed, by the explicit text of the verse. This also clarifies the difference between him and the oath-breaker (nakith) who is not a leader of disbelief, meaning one who violates some term that was agreed upon in a treaty by doing something.

[Section: The intention to expel the Messenger makes fighting them obligatory]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 13]. Here He made their resolve to expel the Messenger a reason that makes fighting them obligatory, because of the harm it contains for him.

It is certain that reviling him is a far greater harm to him than merely expelling him from his land. For this reason, on the day of the Conquest (ʿam al-fath), he (ﷺ) pardoned those who had resolved to expel him, but he did not pardon the one who reviled him. Therefore, when a dhimmi (a non-Muslim under the protection of the Muslim state) openly reviles him, he has broken his covenant and done something greater than resolving to expel the Messenger, and he has begun the harm, so fighting him is obligatory.

[Section: The command to fight the oath-breakers who attack the religion]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people, and remove the rage from their hearts﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14–15].

So He commanded the fighting of the oath-breakers who attack the religion, and He attached several results to that: their punishment through your hands, their humiliation, your victory over them, the healing of the believers' breasts, the removal of the rage in their hearts, and His turning (in mercy) to whomever He wills among others. The implication is: if you fight them, these things will come about.

Since these matters are attached to fighting the oath-breaker and the one who attacks the religion, and since they are desired matters, their cause which necessitates them is also desired by the Lawgiver, namely fighting. And since these matters are desired and are achieved through fighting, it is not permissible to suspend the fighting, which is their cause, while the reason for it exists on the part of those who are fought, namely oath-breaking and attacking the religion.

The healing of hearts that results from the pain of oath-breaking and attack on the religion, and the removal of the rage that arises in the believers' breasts because of it, are intended by the Lawgiver and are required to be achieved. There is no doubt that whoever among the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimma) openly reviles the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enrages and pains the believers far more than shedding the blood of some of them or seizing their property. This is because it stirs anger for the sake of Allah and zeal for Him and His Messenger.

This degree of rage does not stir in the heart of a believer any greater than this, and the upright believer does not become angry with such anger except for the sake of Allah and His Messenger. Allah, exalted is He, loves the healing of the believers' breasts and the removal of rage from their hearts, and this is achieved only by killing the reviler, for several reasons:

First: their ta'zir (discretionary punishment) and disciplining would remove the rage in their hearts if he insults one of the Muslims. If ta'zir and discipline removed their rage when he insults the Messenger, their rage at insulting their Prophet would be like their rage at insulting one of themselves. This is definitely false.

Second: insulting him is greater in their eyes than that some of them should shed the blood of others. Moreover, if one of them killed (the reviler), that would not heal their breasts except by his killing. So it is more fitting and more appropriate that their breasts be healed only by killing the reviler.

Third: Allah made their fighting the cause of achieving healing, and the default is the absence of any other cause that would bring it about. Therefore, killing must be what heals the believers' breasts from such a thing.

Fourth: when Mecca was conquered and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to heal the breasts of Khuza'a, who were the believing people, from Banu Bakr, who had fought them, he gave them power over them at midday or later, while he had granted safety (aman) to all the other people. If the healing of their breasts and the removal of rage from their hearts could have been achieved without killing those who had broken oaths or attacked, he would not have done that while granting safety to the people.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim), on surah 9, verses 14–15:

So He commanded fighting against their enemy, and informed them that in it there are six benefits.

Anger pains the heart, and its cure lies in satisfying that anger. If it is satisfied in what is right, one is healed; but if it is satisfied through injustice and falsehood, it increases the sickness from the very direction one thought would cure it. This is like someone who treats the sickness of love (ʿishq) by committing fornication with the beloved: that only increases his illness and brings upon him other sicknesses, more difficult than the sickness of love, as will come, God willing, Exalted is He.

Likewise, distress (ghamm), worry (hamm) and grief (huzn) are sicknesses of the heart, and their cure lies in their opposites: joy and happiness. If that joy is by right, the heart is healed, becomes sound, and is cured of its sickness. If it is by falsehood, that joy vanishes and is concealed, and it does not last, and it leaves behind sicknesses that are more difficult and more dangerous.

Likewise, ignorance (jahl) is a sickness that pains the heart. Some people treat it with knowledge that does not benefit, and believe they have been healed of their sickness by that knowledge, while in reality it only adds sickness to their sickness. But the heart's occupation with it diverts it from perceiving the hidden pain within it, due to its ignorance of beneficial knowledge, which is a condition for its health and cure. The Prophet (ﷺ) said about those who issued fatwas without knowledge, so that the one who asked for their ruling was destroyed:

"They killed him; may God kill them. Why did they not ask when they did not know? The cure for ignorance (ʿiyy) is only asking."

So he made ignorance a sickness, and its cure the questioning of the people of knowledge.

Likewise, the doubter regarding a matter he is uncertain about, his heart is pained until knowledge and certainty are attained for him. Since that causes him burning, it was said of one who attains certainty: "His chest was made firm (thalj ṣadrihi)," and he attained the coolness of certainty. Thus he is constricted by ignorance and error from the path of his guidance, and expands with guidance and knowledge. God, Exalted is He, said:

﴿So whoever God wishes to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whoever He wishes to misguide, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he were climbing up into the sky﴾ [al-Anʿam: 125].

The point is that among the sicknesses of the hearts are those that are removed by natural remedies, and among them are those that are removed only by the legislated, faith-based remedies. The heart has life and death, sickness and cure, and that is greater than what applies to the body.

(Benefit)

As for the effect of jihad in repelling worry and distress, it is a matter known by direct experience: when the soul leaves the assault of falsehood and its onslaught and domination unopposed, its worry, distress, anguish and fear intensify. But when it strives against it for God's sake, God replaces that worry and grief with joy, vigor and strength, as He, Exalted is He, said:

﴿Fight them; God will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people, and remove the rage of their hearts﴾

Nothing removes the burning (jawā) of the heart, its distress, worry and grief, more than jihad. And God is the One sought for help.

Ibn al-Qayyim, Tafsir (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim), on Surah al-Tawbah 9:19–20:

He, glorified and exalted is He, informed that the caretakers of al-Masjid al-Haram, who maintain it through i'tikaf (seclusion in worship), tawaf (circumambulation), and prayer, are not equal in His sight. This is the maintenance of His mosques mentioned in the Qur'an. And the people who provide water for the pilgrims (ahl siqayat al-hajj) are not equal to those who strive in jihad in the way of Allah. He informed that the believing mujahidin are greater in rank in His sight, that they are the triumphant, and that they are the people who receive the good news of mercy, pleasure, and gardens. Thus He negated equality between the mujahidin and the caretakers of al-Masjid al-Haram despite their various forms of worship, while He praised the maintenance of the mosques by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who maintain the mosques of Allah are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none but Allah. It is expected that those will be among the guided.﴾

So these are the caretakers of the mosques, yet despite this, the people of jihad are higher in rank with Allah than them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 24:

Whoever gives precedence to the obedience of any one of these over the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, or to the word of any one of them over the word of Allah and His Messenger, or to the pleasure of any one of them over the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, or to the fear of any one of them, his hope in them, and his reliance upon them over the fear of Allah, His hope, and reliance upon Him, or to the dealings of any one of them over the dealings of Allah, then he is among those for whom Allah and His Messenger are not dearer than all else. Even if he says it with his tongue, it is a lie from him and a report contrary to what is in his heart. Likewise, whoever gives precedence to the ruling of anyone over the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, that one who is given precedence is dearer to him than Allah and His Messenger. However, the matter may be confused for one who gives precedence to the word, ruling, obedience, or pleasure of someone, supposing that this person does not command, judge, or say anything except what the Messenger said. So he obeys him, refers his disputes to him, and receives his sayings on that basis. Such a person is excused if he is unable to do otherwise. But if he is able to reach the Messenger, and he knows that someone other than the one he follows is more deserving of his obedience absolutely or in some matters, yet he does not turn to the Messenger or to the one more deserving of it, then this is the one who is to be feared for, and he falls under the threat. If he considers it lawful to punish whoever opposes him and to humiliate him, and does not agree with him in following his shaykh, then he is among the wrongdoers and transgressors. Allah has indeed appointed a measure for everything.

He said in (the discussion on the question of listening, samā‘ [devotional listening to poetry and song]):

Nothing saves the servant except that Allah and His Messenger be dearer to him than everything. Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is preferred by him over everything. Allah, the Exalted, has not been pleased that His servants' love for Him and His Messenger be like the love for family and wealth. Rather, He is pleased that Allah and His Messenger, and striving in His cause, be dearer to them than their families, their wealth, their dwellings, their trade, and their clans.

The point is that lovers have three foundations by which their love is realized:

The first is sincerity, and singling out their Beloved, may He be blessed and exalted, with love.

The second is striving in His cause, which is what confirms their faith or exposes it as false. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, then did not doubt, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. Those are the truthful.﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 15].

By this, Allah described the people of love in His saying: ﴿They strive in the cause of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54].

(Benefit)

The mention of sons is placed before wealth, as in His saying: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your clan, and the wealth you have acquired...﴾

And His saying: ﴿Adorned for people is the love of desires: women, sons, heaped-up piles of gold and silver...﴾

As for placing them before wealth in these two verses, it is for a wondrous wisdom: Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah) contains a threat against whoever holds those mentioned things dearer than striving in the cause of Allah. It is well known that the striving believer's imagining the separation from his family, children, fathers, and brothers and clan prevents him from leaving them more than separation from his wealth does. If, along with this, he imagines being killed and thereby being separated from them forever, his soul recoils from these even more. At this imagining, the thought of parting from his wealth hardly occurs to him; rather, the parting from loved ones eclipses the parting from wealth. So mentioning this category first was more fitting than mentioning wealth first.

Reflect on this marvelous arrangement, in placing what is placed first and delaying what is delayed, and it will reveal to you the greatness and majesty of this speech. It begins first with mentioning the servant's roots, namely his forefathers, who are first in nature, nobility, and rank. The pride of the people is in their forefathers, and their defense of them is greater than their defense of themselves, their wealth, and even their children. For this reason, their defense of their fathers and their struggle for them have driven them to accept killing and the captivity of their offspring, and they do not testify against their fathers to disbelief or deficiency, nor do they turn away from their religion, because of the disgrace this would bring upon them. Then he mentions the branches, namely the sons, because they follow them in rank, and they are the nearest of relatives to them, most attached to their hearts, and most dear to their livers, more so than brothers and clan. Then he mentions brothers, who are the collateral heirs (kalalah) and the peripheral branches of lineage. Thus he mentions the roots first, then the branches second, then the peers third, then the spouses fourth, because the wife is a stranger to him, and he may be compensated for her by another, and she is desired only for pleasure. As for close relatives, fathers, sons, and brothers, there is no substitute for them, and they are desired for support and defense, and that takes precedence over mere desire. Then he mentions distant kinship fifthly, which is the clan and paternal cousins, since their clans were mostly their paternal cousins, and if they were strangers, they are even more deserving of being placed later. Then he moved after the relatives to mention wealth sixthly, and described it as "acquired," meaning earned, because hearts incline more to what one has earned from wealth, and love it more, and know its value according to the effort and hardship they have undergone for it, unlike wealth that comes effortlessly without earning, by inheritance, gift, or bequest. Its preservation, its safeguarding, and the eagerness to keep it are greater than for the second. The senses witness to this, and that is sufficient. Then he mentions trade seventhly, because the servant's love for wealth is greater than his love for the trade through which he acquires it. Thus trade is for him a means to the acquired wealth, so he placed wealth before trade, as ends are placed before their means. Then he described trade as something whose slump is feared, and this indicates its nobility and importance, and that its worth has reached the point of being feared for slump. Then he mentioned homelands eighthly, the last of the ranks, because the heart's attachment to them is less than its attachment to all that was mentioned before, for homelands resemble one another, and a second homeland may take the place of the first in every respect and be better than it, so there is a substitute for it. As for fathers, sons, relatives, and clans, no substitute can be found for them. Thus, although the heart yearns for its first homeland, its longing for its fathers, sons, and wives is greater. So love of homeland is the last of the ranks. This is the reality, except for an accidental circumstance in which preferring the distant over the near is weighed in his mind. That is a particular case, not a general rule, so no contradiction arises from it. But in the absence of such circumstances, this is the appropriate and actual order.

**[Section: On some of the jurisprudential issues (masa'il fiqhiyya) and wisdoms (nukat hukmiyya) contained in the Battle of Hunayn]**

**[The war with Hawazin served to make manifest the command of Allah]**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had promised His Messenger, and He is the One who keeps His promise, that when Makkah was conquered people would enter his religion in multitudes, and that the Arabs would all submit to him. When the Clear Victory was complete, His wisdom, exalted is He, required that He hold back the hearts of Hawazin and those who followed them from Islam, and that they gather and unite to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, so that the command of Allah would become manifest, His full exaltation of His Messenger and His support of His religion would be shown, their spoils would become a thanksgiving to the people of the conquest, and Allah, glorified is He, would make His Messenger and His servants prevail over this great might, which the Muslims had never encountered the like of, so that after this no one among the Arabs would stand against them. There are other brilliant wisdoms besides these, which shine for the reflective and show themselves to the discerning.

Allah, glorified is He, in His wisdom, made the Muslims first taste the bitterness of defeat and breaking, despite their great numbers and their equipment and the strength of their might, in order to humble heads that had been raised by the conquest. They did not enter His land and His sacred precinct as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had entered it, with his head lowered and bowed upon his mount, so that his chin nearly touched his saddle-bow, in humility before his Lord, submission to His greatness, and submissiveness to His might. Allah made lawful for him His sacred precinct and His land, which was not made lawful for anyone before him or after him. And so that He, glorified is He, might show to those who said, *"We will not be overcome today because of small numbers"*, that victory is only from Him; whoever He supports cannot be overcome, and whoever He forsakes has no supporter other than Him. And that He, glorified is He, is the One who undertook the support of His Messenger and His religion, not your great numbers, which pleased you, for they did not avail you anything, so you turned back retreating. When their hearts were broken, the robes of consolation were sent to them with the messenger of victory: *"Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see"* (Qur'an 9:26). His wisdom also required that the robes and rewards of victory pour out only upon those who have been broken: *"And We wish to bestow favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors, and establish them in the land, and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared"* (Qur'an 28:6).

Among these wisdoms: when Allah, glorified is He, prevented the army from taking the spoils of Makkah, so they did not take from it gold, silver, goods, captives, or land, as Abu Dawud narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "I asked Jabir, 'Did they take any spoils on the Day of the Conquest?' He said, 'No.'" They had conquered it with horses and camels, and they were ten thousand, and they had a need for what an army needs of the means of strength. So Allah, glorified is He, stirred the hearts of the polytheists to fight them, and cast into their hearts the bringing out of their wealth, their camels, their sheep, and their captives with them, as a provision, a hospitality, and an honor for His party and His soldiers. He completed His decree, glorified is He, by making them hope for victory and showing them the first signs of triumph, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was already decreed. When Allah sent down His victory upon His Messenger and his allies, and the spoils were distributed to their owners, and the shares of Allah and His Messenger were applied to them, it was said: "We have no need of your lives, nor of your women and your children." So Allah, glorified is He, inspired in their hearts repentance and turning back, and they came as Muslims. It was then said: "Indeed, among the thanks for your Islam and your coming is that we return to you your women, your sons, and your captives," and *"If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"* (Qur'an 8:70).

Among these wisdoms: Allah, glorified is He, began the Arabs' battles with the Battle of Badr and concluded their battles with the Battle of Hunayn. For this reason these two expeditions (ghazawat, sing. ghazwa, "a military expedition led by the Prophet ﷺ") are mentioned together, and it is said "Badr and Hunayn," even though seven years lay between them. The angels fought alongside the Muslims in person in these two expeditions, and the Prophet (ﷺ) threw pebbles into the faces of the polytheists in both of them. With these two expeditions the flame of the Arabs was extinguished against the expedition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims. The first one frightened them and broke their edge, and the second drained their strength, exhausted their arrows, and humbled their gathering, until they found no choice but to enter the religion of Allah.

Among these wisdoms: Allah, glorified is He, consoled through it the people of Makkah and gladdened them with what they gained of victory and spoils. Thus it was like a remedy for what had befallen them of defeat, and indeed the very essence of their consolation. He also made them recognize the completion of His blessing upon them by turning away from them the evil of Hawazin, for they had no power against them, and they were only helped against them by the Muslims. Had they been left alone with them, their enemy would have devoured them. And other wisdoms besides these, which no one encompasses except Allah, the Exalted.

Among the jurisprudence (fiqh, "the understanding and legal rulings derived from the sources of the Shari'ah") contained in this: the Imam (ruler or leader) should send out scouts and those who infiltrate among his enemy to bring him news of them. When the Imam hears of his enemy's intention to attack him, and his own army has strength and protection, he should not sit waiting for them, but should march toward them, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched toward Hawazin until he met them at Hunayn.

Among these: the Imam may borrow the weapons and equipment of the polytheists to fight his enemy, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) borrowed the armor of Safwan, and he was a polytheist at that time.

Among these: complete trust (tawakkul) in Allah includes using the means that Allah has established as causes for their results, both by decree and by law. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions were the most complete in trust, yet they met their enemy while protected with various kinds of weapons, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah with a helmet on his head, though Allah had revealed to him: *"And Allah will protect you from the people"* (Qur'an 5:67).

Many who lack verification and firm knowledge find this problematic, and they evade the answer with cleverness, sometimes saying that he did this to teach the Ummah, and sometimes that this happened before the verse was revealed. A question was raised in Egypt which one of the rulers asked about, and a hadith was mentioned to him, which Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir narrated in his *Tarikh al-Kabir* (Great History), that after the Jewish woman sent him a poisoned sheep, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not eat any food brought to him until the one who brought it had eaten from it first.

They said: "In this there is a model for kings in this matter." Then someone said: "How can this be reconciled with His saying: *'And Allah will protect you from the people'* (Qur'an 5:67)? If Allah, glorified is He, has guaranteed him protection, then He knows that no path to him is open for any human."

Some answered that this indicates the weakness of the hadith, and some answered that this happened before the verse was revealed, so that when it was revealed he would not have done that afterward. But if these people had reflected that the guarantee of protection from Allah does not contradict taking the means to it, it would have spared them this strain. This guarantee from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, does not contradict his guarding himself from people, nor does it negate it, just as Allah's telling him that He will make His religion prevail over all religion and raise it does not contradict His command to fight, to prepare equipment and strength, to bind horses, to take seriously caution and vigilance against his enemy, and to wage war against him with all kinds of warfare and deception. So when he intended an expedition, he would give the impression of a different destination. This is because this is an announcement from Allah, glorified is He, about the outcome and end of his condition through the means he adopts, which Allah made lead to that and require it. He (ﷺ) knew his Lord best and followed His command most, so he would not neglect the means that Allah, in His wisdom, made to bring about what He promised him of victory, triumph, the manifestation of His religion, and the defeat of his enemy. This is like how He guaranteed him life until he delivers His messages and makes His religion manifest, while he himself pursued the means of life: food, drink, clothing, and shelter. This is a point in which many people err, to the extent that some of them abandoned supplication, claiming there was no benefit in it, because what is asked for, if it has been decreed, will be attained without fail, and if it has not been decreed, it will not be attained. So what benefit is there in occupying oneself with supplication?

Then he evaded the answer cleverly by saying: "Supplication is an act of worship." It is said to this deceived person: there remains for you another division, which is the truth, that He has decreed for him his desired goal through a cause, such that if he takes up that cause, the goal is achieved for him, and if he neglects the cause, he misses the goal. Supplication is among the greatest causes for attaining the goal. The likeness of this deceived person is only like someone who says: "If Allah has decreed that I be satisfied, then I will be satisfied whether I eat or not; and if He has not decreed my satisfaction, I will not be satisfied whether I eat or not. So what is the benefit of eating?" Such are the worthless and false trifles that contradict the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted, and His law. And success is from Allah.

Among these jurisprudential points: it is permissible to hamstring (ʿaqr) the horse or mount of the enemy if that helps to kill him, as ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) hamstrung the camel of the bearer of the unbelievers' banner. This is not the forbidden torturing of animals.

Among them: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pardoned the one who intended to kill him and did not hasten to punish him, but rather invoked blessings for him and wiped his chest until he became as though he were a close, intimate friend.

Among them: what became manifest in this expedition of the miracles of prophethood and the signs of the message: his informing Shayba of what he had concealed in his heart, and his steadfastness when people had turned away from him while he was saying:

*"I am the Prophet, there is no lie;*
*I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib."*

And the battalions of the polytheists were facing him.

Among them: Allah delivered the handful of pebbles that he threw to the eyes of his enemies from a distance, and the blessing in that handful until it filled the eyes of the people; and other miracles in it, like the descent of the angels to fight alongside him, until the enemy saw them plainly and some of the Muslims saw them as well.

Among them: it is permissible for the Imam to delay the distribution of the spoils until the unbelievers embrace Islam and enter obedience, and then he returns to them their spoils and captives. This is evidence for the one who says that spoils become owned only through distribution, not merely by seizing them; for if the Muslims had owned them by mere seizure, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not have delayed the distribution to return them to their owners. Based on this, if one of the participants in the spoils dies before the distribution, or before they are secured in the abode of Islam, his share is returned to the remaining participants, not to his heirs. This is the position of Abu Hanifa: if he dies before seizure, his heirs receive nothing; if he dies after the distribution, his share goes to his heirs.

The jizyah is the tax imposed on the heads of the disbelievers as a humiliation and a debasement, and the meaning is: until they give the tax from their necks.

There is disagreement about its etymology. The judge in *al-Ahkam al-Sultaniyyah* said: its name is derived from *al-jaza'* (recompense), either as a recompense for their disbelief, since it is taken from them in a state of humiliation, or as a recompense for our granting them protection, since it is taken from them gently.

The author of *al-Mughni* said: it is derived from *jazahu*, meaning "he settled it," as in His saying: ﴿Do not let any soul avail another soul anything﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48]. Thus the jizyah would be like the *fidyah* (ransom).

Our shaykh said: the first view is more sound, and this comes back to the point that it is either a punishment or a wage.

As for His saying "an yad" (from a hand), it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (*hal*), meaning: they give it while humbled and subdued. This is the correct interpretation of the verse.

A group said: the meaning is "from hand to hand," i.e., in cash, not deferred.

Another group said: from his hand to the hand of the taker, not sending it through an intermediary, nor appointing an agent to deliver it.

A group said: its meaning is "by way of a favour from you to them," through your permitting them to remain and through your accepting them. The correct view is the first, and it is what the people hold.

Whoever said, "The meaning is: from a hand of theirs, i.e., from a capacity to pay, so it is not taken from one who is unable to pay," went completely astray and did not hit the intended meaning of God. This ruling is sound, but reading the verse as referring to it is false. None of the Companions, the Successors, or the early scholars of this community interpreted it that way; it is merely the cleverness of some later scholars.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29] is another circumstantial clause. The first describes the state of the Muslims when they take the jizyah from them: that they take it by force and from a hand. The second describes the state of the one who pays it: that he pays it while humbled and abased.

The people differed in interpreting *al-sigharu* (humiliation) that they are in at the time of paying the jizyah. 'Ikrimah said: that he pays it standing, while the taker is seated.

A group said: that he comes with it himself on foot, not riding, and his standing is prolonged when he comes to pay it; and he is dragged to the place where it is taken from him with violence, then his hand is pulled and he is degraded.

All of this has no evidence for it, nor is it what the verse requires, nor was it transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ, nor from the Companions, that they did such things.

The correct understanding of the verse is that the humiliation is their acceptance of the application of the rulings of the religion (*millah*) upon them, and their giving of the jizyah; for accepting that is the humiliation.

Imam Ahmad said in the narration of Hanbal: "They used to be dragged by their hands and sealed on their necks if they did not pay the humiliation which God, exalted is He, mentioned: ﴿and they are humbled﴾."

This indicates that when the dhimmi offers what is due from him and accepts the humiliation, there is no need for him to be dragged by his hand and beaten.

He also said, in the narration of Muhanna ibn Yahya: "It is recommended that they be made to suffer in paying the jizyah."

The judge said: he did not intend their torture or imposing on them beyond their capacity; he only intended to belittle them and degrade them.

I say: since the hand of the giver is the upper hand and the hand of the taker is the lower hand, the imams took care that this should not be the case with the jizyah, and they took it in a manner where the hand of the giver is the lower and the hand of the taker is the upper.

Qadi Abu Ya'la said: In this there is an indication that those Christians who take up the work of the ruler, and among whom injustice and domination over the Muslims and the collection of taxes appear, have no dhimmah (protection), and their blood is permitted; because God, exalted is He, described them as giving the jizyah in a state of humiliation and abasement.

What the judge deduced is among the most sound deductions. God, glorified and exalted is He, extended the fighting to an end point, which is the giving of the jizyah together with humiliation. So when the condition of the Christian or others among the people of the jizyah is incompatible with abasement and humiliation, there is no sanctity for his blood or his property, and he has no dhimmah. For this reason the commander of the believers, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, stipulated on them those conditions which contain their humiliation and debasement, and that whenever they deviate from any of them, they have no covenant and no dhimmah; and what is permitted to the Muslims from them is what is permitted from the people of hostility and defiance.

[Section: The jizyah is not a rent for the use of the dwelling]

4 - Section

[The jizyah is not a rent for living in the land]

It has become clear from what we have mentioned that the jizyah was imposed as a humiliation and debasement of the disbelievers, not as a rent for dwelling in the land. We mentioned that if it were a rent, it would be obligatory on women, children, the chronically ill and the blind; and if it were a rent, the Arabs would not have refused it from the Christians of the Banu Taghlib and others, and they would not have agreed to pay double what is taken from the Muslims as zakat on their wealth. And if it were a rent, it would have a fixed term like other leases; and if it were a rent, it would not be obligatory with the attribute of degradation and humiliation; and if it were a rent, it would be determined according to the benefit, for the dwelling in a land may be worth in a year many times the fixed jizyah. And if it were a rent, the dhimmi would not be obliged to pay the rent of a house or land he lives in if he rents it from the public treasury; and if it were a rent, the obligation would be what the lessor and the lessee agree upon.

In summary, the corruption of this view is known from many aspects.

[Section: No jizyah on a child, a woman, or an insane person]

8 - Section

There is no jizyah on a child, a woman, or an insane person.

This is the position of the four imams and their followers.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: "I do not know of any disagreement from others on this."

Abu Muhammad said in *al-Mughni*: "We know of no disagreement among the people of knowledge on this."

Abu 'Ubayd said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Aslam, the freed slave of 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both: that 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, wrote to the commanders of the armies that they should fight in the way of God, and not fight except those who fight them, and not kill women or children, and not kill anyone except those who have reached puberty (*al-mawasi*, those in whom the pubic hair has grown).

[And he wrote to the commanders of the armies: that they should impose the jizyah, and not impose it on women and children, and not impose it except on those who have reached puberty.]

Abu 'Ubayd said: that is, one in whom growth has appeared.

This hadith is the basis regarding who is obligated to pay the jizyah and who is not. Do you not see that he only made it upon the males mentioned, to the exclusion of females and children, and he exempted those who do not deserve killing, namely the offspring?

[Section: From whom the jizyah is taken]

The jurists agreed that the jizyah is taken from the People of the Book and from the Magians.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, had hesitated in taking the jizyah from the Magians until 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf testified that the Messenger of God ﷺ had taken it from the Magians of Hajar, as al-Bukhari mentioned.

al-Shafi'i mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab mentioned the Magians and said: "I do not know what to do regarding their affair." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said to him: "I testify that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Treat them as you treat the People of the Book.'" This is explicit that they are not among the People of the Book. And it is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿lest you say, "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of their study"﴾. God related this about them and did not deny it against them, nor did He call them liars regarding it.

If it is said: the Prophet ﷺ did not take it from any of the idol-worshippers, despite his extensive fighting against them.

It is said: Indeed, and that is because the verse of the jizyah was revealed in the year of Tabuk, in the ninth year after the Hijrah, after the Arabian Peninsula had accepted Islam and no idol-worshipper remained in it. When the verse of the jizyah was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ took it from those who remained upon their disbelief among the Christians and the Magians. For this reason he did not take it from the Jews of Madinah when he arrived in Madinah, nor from the Jews of Khaybar, because he had made a treaty with them before the revelation of the verse of the jizyah.

[The claim of the Jews of Khaybar that the jizyah was removed from them, and the refutation of that]

This doubt is what led the Jews to think that the people of Khaybar are not subject to the jizyah, and that they are exempted from it among the Jews. Then they reinforced the matter by forging a document in which the Messenger of God ﷺ supposedly removed from them the burdens, the forced labour and the jizyah, and they placed in it the testimony of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and others. This document is a lie, fabricated by the consensus of the people of knowledge, for ten reasons:

Among them: that none of the scholars of transmission, biography and campaigns mentioned that this ever happened at all, despite their care in preserving things far less significant than that.

The second: that the jizyah was revealed only after the conquest of Khaybar; so when he made a treaty with the people of Khaybar, the jizyah had not yet been revealed, so that he could remove it from them.

The third: that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan had not yet become Muslim, for he only embraced Islam in the year of the Conquest, after Khaybar.

The fourth: that Sa'd ibn Mu'adh died in the year of the Trench, before the conquest of Khaybar.

The fifth: that there were no burdens or forced labour upon the people of Khaybar in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, so that they could be removed from them.

The sixth: that the people of Khaybar did not have such honour, or such regard for the rights of the Muslims, as would require the removal of the jizyah from them; they were among the most hostile of disbelievers to the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions. So what good came from them to the Muslims that the jizyah should be removed from them, to the exclusion of the rest of the disbelievers?

The seventh: that the document they produced claimed to be in the handwriting of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. This is certainly a lie, and 'Ali's enmity towards the Jews is well known; he was the one who killed Marhab the Jew and inflicted great slaughter upon the Jews on the day of Khaybar, until the conquest came at his hands.

The eighth: that this is known only from the narration of the Jews, and they are the people of slander (*al-buhut*), the most lying of creatures against God and His prophets and messengers. How could they be believed about the Messenger of God ﷺ regarding something that contradicts the Book of God, exalted is He?!
