The ninth: that if this document were authentic, they would have displayed it in the days of the rightly-guided caliphs, and in the days of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-‘Aziz, and in the days of al-Mansur and al-Rashid; and the imams of Islam would have exempted them from those on whom the jizyah is removed, or at least one jurist among the jurists of the Muslims would have mentioned that. It is not permissible for the community to agree in opposing the sunnah of its Prophet. And how could a document from the Messenger of God ﷺ be in the hands of the enemies of God and they not use it as proof every time against those from whom they take the jizyah, and no single scholar among the scholars of the early generations mentions it? And if some who have no knowledge of the biography and transmitted reports among the later generations were deceived by it, their own companions would denounce him, explain his error and warn against his slip.

The tenth: that the imams of hadith and transmission bear witness to the falsehood of this document, and that it is a forgery, a fabricated lie. When the Jews brought it out after the year four hundred, in the time of the hadith master Abu Bakr al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, the vizier Ibn al-Muslimah sent to him and had him examine it. The hadith master said: "This document is a forgery." The vizier said to him: "How do you know this?" He said: "It contains the testimony of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and Sa'd died on the day of the Trench before Khaybar, and Mu'awiyah embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest in the year eight, and Khaybar was in the year seven." This amazed the vizier.

The point is that the Prophet ﷺ did not take the jizyah from any of the idolaters of the Arabs, because the verse of the jizyah was revealed after the year of Tabuk, by which time all the idol-worshipping Arabs had entered Islam. So he took it from those who had not entered Islam among the Jews, the Christians and the Magians.

Those who restricted the jizyah to the People of the Book said: the purpose of sending the messengers and sending down the books is the eradication of disbelief and polytheism from the earth, and that the entire religion should belong to God, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is entirely for God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193], and in another verse: ﴿and the religion will be entirely for God﴾ [al-Anfal: 39]. What this requires is that no disbeliever be allowed to remain in his disbelief. But a text came permitting the People of the Book to remain when they give the jizyah from a hand while humbled. So we limited this to them, and we took the general category of disbelievers under the texts that indicate fighting them until the entire religion belongs to God.

They said: It is not valid to equate the idol-worshippers with the People of the Book, because the disbelief of the polytheists is more severe than the disbelief of the People of the Book. The People of the Book retain some monotheism and some traces of the prophets that the idol-worshippers do not have, and they believe in the Return, the Recompense and the prophethood, unlike the idol-worshippers.

The idol-worshippers have been at war with all the messengers and their nations from the time of Noah until the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers. For this reason, this difference between the two groups has had an effect on the permissibility of their slaughtered animals and on the permissibility of marriage with the People of the Book, but not with the idol-worshippers. This is not refuted by the Magians, for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered that the way of the People of the Book be applied to them (in the matter of the jizya). This indicates that the jizya is taken only from the People of the Book, and that it was imposed specifically for them. Otherwise, if the jizya applied to all disbelievers, the People of the Book would have no greater claim to it than others, and he would have said: "They have the ruling of their likes among the disbelievers: they are to be fought until they embrace Islam or pay the jizya."

As for the prohibition of their slaughtered animals and of marrying their women, it is a consensus of the Companions (may God be pleased with them). For this reason, Imam Ahmad and others denounced Abu Thawr for his rejection of qiyas (analogical reasoning) and his legal opinion permitting their slaughtered animals and marriage with them. Ahmad invoked a curse against him for opposing the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Companions were more knowledgeable, more learned and sounder in analogy and opinion. They ruled regarding blood that it must be preserved, in agreement with the saying and action of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), since he accepted the jizya from them. And they ruled regarding sexual relations and slaughtered animals that they are forbidden, out of caution and in order to keep them on the original principle, and by equating them with the idol-worshippers, since there is no difference in this between the idol-worshippers and the fire-worshippers. The principle regarding blood is that it be preserved, and the principle regarding sexual relations and slaughtered animals is that they be forbidden. So they left each matter on its original principle. This is the height of jurisprudence and the soundest of reasoning.

[The wisdom in keeping the People of the Book among us]

They said: God, exalted is He, has wisdoms in keeping the two kinds of People of the Book among us, for despite their disbelief, they bear witness to the foundations of prophethood, monotheism, the Last Day, Paradise and Hell. Their books contain good tidings of the Prophet (ﷺ), a mention of his description and attributes, and the attributes of his community, which are among the signs of his prophethood and the proofs of his mission, and which testify to the truthfulness of the first and last of the messengers.

This wisdom is specific to the People of the Book and not to the idol-worshippers. Therefore their survival is among the strongest proofs against those who deny prophethood, the Return and monotheism. God, exalted is He, said to those who deny these: ﴿Ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 43]. He mentioned this right after His saying: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed. So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 43]. That is, ask the People of the Book: Did We send before Muhammad men to whom revelation was given, or was Muhammad an innovation among the messengers, with no messenger preceding him, such that his sending would be a strange matter, one that had never come to the world before him?

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45]. The intended meaning of asking them is asking their nations about what their messengers brought them: Did it contain that God prescribed for them to worship another god besides Him?

Al-Farra' said: the intended meaning is asking the people of the Torah and the Gospel, and they will inform him about their books and their prophets.

Ibn Qutaybah said: the implied meaning is: ask those to whom We sent messengers before you, and they are the People of the Book.

Ibn al-Anbari said: the implied meaning is: ask those whom We sent before you.

In every interpretation, the purpose is to establish the matter as a confirmation to the polytheists of Quraysh and others who denied prophethood and monotheism, that God sent a messenger or revealed a book, or forbade the worship of idols.

Thus the testimony of the People of the Book to this is a proof against them, and it is one of the indications of the soundness of his mission (ﷺ), since he came with what his brother messengers who preceded him from the messengers of God, glorified is He, had brought. He was not an innovation among the messengers, nor did he come with the opposite of what they brought. Rather, he reported the same things they reported, without having witnessed them and without being contemporaries with them. This is among the greatest signs of his truthfulness.

[The reason for imposing the jizya]

The matter rests on a basic point: is the jizya imposed as a protection for blood, or as a visible mark of the humiliation of disbelief and the abasement of its people, and is therefore a punishment?

Whoever considers the first meaning says: It does not follow from its being a protection for the blood of those whose disbelief is lighter in comparison to others, namely the People of the Book, that it must be a protection for the blood of those whose disbelief is more severe.

Whoever considers the second meaning says: The purpose is to make manifest the humiliation of disbelief and its people, and to subdue them. This is a matter that is not specific to the People of the Book, but encompasses every disbeliever.

They said: The text has indicated this very meaning in His saying: ﴿until they pay the jizya willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29]. So the jizya is humiliation and abasement, and for this reason it is equivalent to the enslavement.

They said: If it is permissible to allow them to remain in slavery while they are disbelievers, it is all the more permissible to allow them to remain under the jizya, because the punishment of the jizya is greater than the punishment of slavery. For this reason, women and children and others who are not obligated to pay the jizya may be enslaved.

If you say: The individual People of the Book are not enslaved, as is one of the two narrations from Ahmad, then you would be refuted by the Sunnah and the consensus of the Companions. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to enslave the captives of the idol-worshippers, and it was permissible for their masters to have intercourse with them after the completion of their waiting period, as in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may God be pleased with him) concerning the captives of Awtas, which took place at the end of the Arab campaigns after the conquest of Mecca, where he said:

"A pregnant woman is not to be had sexually until she gives birth, nor a non-pregnant one until she has been cleansed by one menstrual cycle."

So he permitted intercourse with them after the cleansing period, and he did not stipulate Islam. Most of the captives of the Companions in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) were from the idol-worshippers, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) allowed them to possess the captives.

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) gave Salama ibn al-Akwa' (may God be pleased with them both) a woman from the captives as a special share (nafl), and she was one of the idol-worshippers.

Umar and his son (may God be pleased with them both) took from the captives of Hawazin, and likewise others among the Companions did.

And this is al-Hanafiyya, the mother of Muhammad ibn Ali, from the captives of Banu Hanifa.

And in the hadith: "Whoever says such-and-such, it is as if he freed four necks from the descendants of Isma'il." They were not People of the Book; most of them were idol-worshippers.

They said: If it is permissible to grant a captive release without ransom and without enslavement, then it is all the more permissible to release him in exchange for a jizya placed upon his neck, which would be a strength for the Muslims. If the jizya is a punishment, then it is more permissible than the punishment of enslavement; and if it is a protection, then it is more permissible than his protection by being granted freedom for nothing. So if it is permissible for him to remain among the Muslims without a jizya, then his remaining among them with a jizya is more permissible and more secure. Otherwise, he would be in a better condition than the People of the Book who do not reside among the Muslims except with a jizya.

If you say: When we grant him release, we send him back to his place of safety, and we do not allow him to reside among the Muslims.

It is said: If it is permissible to send him back to his place of safety, where he becomes a strength for the disbelievers and an aid to them and is poised to wage war against us, without anything in return, then it is all the more permissible to do this in exchange for money taken from him that becomes a strength for the Muslims and a humiliation and abasement of disbelief.

This is clarified by the fact that if it is permissible to make a truce with them for the sake of the public good, without money and without any benefit accruing to the Muslims, then it is all the more permissible to take money from them in a manner of humiliation and abasement, and for the strength of the Muslims. This is clear.

It is further clarified by the fact that if the idol-worshippers were a great nation that cannot be counted, like the people of India and others, where it is not possible to eradicate them by the sword, then subduing and oppressing them through the jizya is closer to the might of Islam and its people and its strength than leaving them without a jizya, so they would be in a better condition than the People of the Book.

The secret of the matter is that the jizya is among the category of punishments, and not that it is a privilege for the People of the Book, so no one else deserves it.

As for those who say that the jizya is a compensation for residing in the land, as the followers of al-Shafi'i say, this view is weak in many respects, which we will address later, God willing.

They said: Killing is required only in exchange for combat, not in exchange for disbelief. For this reason women, children, the disabled, the blind, and monks who do not fight are not killed. Rather, we fight those who fight us.

This was the practice of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the people of the earth: he would fight whoever fought him until he entered his religion, or made a truce with him, or came under his subjugation through the jizya. On this basis, he would command his detachments and armies when they fought their enemies, as has preceded in the hadith of Buraydah. So when the disbelievers abandon fighting the people of Islam, make peace with them, and offer them the jizya "willingly while they are humbled," this is a benefit for the people of Islam and for the polytheists.

As for the benefit to the people of Islam, it is what they take of wealth which becomes a strength for Islam along with the humiliation and abasement of disbelief. This is more beneficial to them than leaving the disbelievers without a jizya.

As for the benefit to the polytheists, it is that in their remaining there is hope that they will embrace Islam when they witness the signs and proofs of Islam, or when news of it reaches them. Some of them will inevitably enter Islam, and this is more beloved to God than killing them.

The aim is only that the word of God be supreme and that the religion be entirely for God. Keeping them under the jizya does not contradict this meaning, just as keeping the People of the Book under the jizya among the Muslims does not contradict the word of God being supreme and the religion being entirely for God. For part of the religion being entirely for God is the humiliation of disbelief and its people, their abasement, the imposition of the jizya upon their heads and enslavement upon their necks. This is part of the religion of God, and nothing contradicts it except leaving the disbelievers in their honor and establishing their religion as they wish, such that they have power and authority. And God knows best.

[A section on the jizya and the kharaj and what they share and differ in]

The kharaj is the jizya of the land, just as the jizya is the kharaj of the persons. They are two rights upon the persons and lands of the disbelievers for the Muslims. They agree in some respects and differ in others.

They agree in that each of them is taken from the disbelievers in a manner of humiliation and abasement; that their expenditure is the expenditure of the fay' (public revenue); that both are due once every year; and that both lapse upon Islam, in detail which we will mention, God willing.

They differ in that the jizya was established by the text, while the kharaj was established by ijtihad (independent juristic reasoning). The jizya, when assessed on the wealthy, does not increase with the increase of his wealth, whereas the kharaj is assessed according to the extent and smallness of the land. The kharaj can coexist with Islam, as we will mention, God willing, while the jizya cannot coexist with it in any way. For this reason, the two may sometimes combine on the person and land of a disbeliever, and sometimes lapse. The jizya is due where there is no kharaj, and the kharaj is due where there is no jizya.

(Fa'idah)

Among the devil's other deceptions toward the Jews: they used to kill the prophets, through whose hands alone guidance could be attained.

They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, the Exalted. They declared things forbidden to them and permitted things for them, and they followed their prohibitions and permissions.

They did not consider whether that prohibition and permission came from Allah, the Exalted, or not.

Adi ibn Hatim said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, and asked him about His saying: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾.

I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they did not worship them.' He said: 'They made lawful for them what was unlawful, and made unlawful for them what was lawful, and they obeyed them. That was their worship of them.'"

Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others.

This is among the greatest of the devil's deceptions toward man: that he kills, or fights, those through whose hands he was guided, and takes as a rival to Allah one whose infallibility is not guaranteed to him, declaring unlawful for him and lawful for him.

[Section: The Distinction Between Following (ittiba') and Blind Imitation (taqlid)]

Abu Umar said in al-Jami': "Chapter on the corruption of taqlid (blind imitation) and its refutation, and the difference between it and ittiba' (following)." Abu Umar said: "Allah, blessed and exalted, has condemned taqlid in more than one place in His Book, saying: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾."

It is narrated from Hudhayfah and others that he said: "They did not worship them besides Allah, but they made lawful for them and unlawful for them, and they followed them."

Adi ibn Hatim said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a cross around my neck, and he said: 'O Adi, throw this idol from your neck.' I came to him while he was reciting Surat Bara'ah, until he reached this verse: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾."

He said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we did not take them as lords.' He said: 'Yes! Do they not make lawful for you what has been made unlawful, so you make it lawful, and make unlawful for you what has been made lawful, so you make it unlawful?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is their worship.'"

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: The hadith is in the Musnad and in al-Tirmidhi, in a longer form.

Abu al-Bakhtari said regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾: "Indeed, if they had commanded them to worship them besides Allah, they would not have obeyed them. But they commanded them, so they made Allah's lawful unlawful and His unlawful lawful, and they obeyed them. That was rububiyyah (lordship)."

Waki' said: Sufyan and al-A'mash both narrated to us from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu Thabit, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: "Hudhayfah was asked about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾: 'Did they worship them?'

He said: 'No, but they made lawful for them what was unlawful, so they made it lawful, and made unlawful for them what was lawful, so they made it unlawful.'"

And Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And thus We did not send before you a warner into any town, but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23] ﴿He said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that upon which you found your fathers?"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 24] So they were prevented, by following their fathers, from accepting guidance, and they said: "Indeed, we reject what you have been sent with." Concerning these and their likes Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿When those who were followed disowned those who followed, and they saw the punishment, and their means of connection were cut off. And those who followed said, "If only we had another return, we would disown them as they have disowned us." Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166-167].

And Allah, Exalted, rebuking and censuring the people of disbelief, says: ﴿What are these statues to which you are devoted?﴾ [al-Anbiya: 52] ﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ [al-Anbiya: 53] And He says: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67] Similar to this in the Qur'an is much censure of imitating fathers and leaders. The scholars have argued with these verses in refuting taqlid, and the disbelief of those people did not prevent them from using these verses as evidence, because the comparison was not made on the basis of one's disbelief or the other's faith. Rather, the comparison was made between imitators who have no proof for their imitation. Like a man who imitates someone and disbelieves, and imitates another and sins, and imitates another in a matter and errs in its ruling: each of them is blameworthy for imitating without proof, because all of that is taqlid, which resembles one another, even if the sins differ. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And Allah would not misguide a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid﴾ [at-Tawbah: 115].

He said: "So when taqlid is nullified by all that we have mentioned, it becomes obligatory to submit to the sources to which submission is obligatory, namely the Book, the Sunnah, and what has the same meaning as them by a comprehensive proof." Then he cited, through the chain of Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Awf, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'I do not fear for my Ummah after me except from three kinds of deeds.' They said: 'And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'I fear for them the slip of a scholar, an unjust ruling, and a followed desire.'" And through this same chain, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "I have left among you two things; you will not go astray as long as you hold fast to them: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ."

I say: The authors of works on the Sunnah combined the corruption of taqlid and its refutation with the explanation of the slip of a scholar, in order to show by that the corruption of taqlid, and that a scholar may inevitably slip, since he is not infallible. So it is not permissible to accept everything he says, or to treat his words as if they were the words of one who is infallible. This is what every scholar on the face of the earth has condemned and prohibited, and they condemned its adherents. It is the root of the affliction and trial of the imitators, for they imitate the scholar in what he erred in and in what he did not err in, and they have no way of distinguishing between them. So they inevitably take the religion with error, making lawful what Allah has forbidden, making unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and legislating what He has not legislated. This is inevitable for them, since infallibility is absent from the one they imitate, and error inevitably occurs from him.

Al-Bayhaqi and others mentioned from the hadith of this Kathir, from his father, from his grandfather, traced back to the Prophet: "Beware of the slip of a scholar, and wait for his return (to the truth)."

(Section)

Then reflect upon the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the rarity of these two currencies, gold and silver, and on the inability of the most skilled people of the world to achieve what they attempted of making them and imitating the creation of them by Allah, despite their intense eagerness, their utmost effort and striving in that matter. They attained nothing but the craft. Had they been enabled to make the like of what Allah created of that, the affairs of the world would have been corrupted, gold and silver would have spread among people until they became like palm-leaves and pottery, the benefit for which they were placed would have been nullified, and their abundance itself would have been the cause of the cessation of benefiting from them, for they would no longer have any value, and their being a measure for precious wealth, transactions, and the provisions of fighters would have been voided. Nor would some people have been subjugated to others, since everyone would become an owner of gold and silver. Had He made all His creatures rich, He would have made them all poor. So who would consent, for himself, to degrade them in the crafts without which the world has no stability?

Glory be to Him who made their preciousness the cause of the order of the world, and did not make them in preciousness like the red sulphur, which cannot be reached, so that the benefit would be entirely lost. Rather, He placed them and caused them to grow in the world in a measure required by His wisdom, His mercy, and the interests of His servants.

I read in the handwriting of the virtuous Jibril ibn Rawh al-Anbari, who said: Some of those who deal in minerals informed me that they went deep in searching for them into some regions of the mountain, and they reached a place where there were mountain-like masses of silver. Beyond that was a valley flowing hard with abundant water, which could not be reached, and there was no way to cross it. So they turned back to where they worked, to prepare what they could cross with. When they had prepared it and returned, they sought the route of the river, but they found no trace of it and did not know where to turn, so they departed in despair. This is one of the things that shows the invalidity of the art of alchemy, and that, upon verification, it is deception and mere dye and nothing else.

We have already mentioned its invalidity and explained its corruption in forty aspects in a separate treatise.

The point is that the wisdom of Allah the Exalted required the preciousness of these two substances and their scarcity in comparison with iron, copper, and lead, for the good of the people. Consider this: when a fine and admired item made by people among their goods appears, it is precious and rare as long as it is scarce and desired; but when it spreads and becomes abundant in people's hands, and both the elite and the common can obtain it, it falls in their estimation and their desire for it decreases.

From this is the saying of the poet:

"The preciousness of a thing is from its rarity."

For this reason, the people most averse to the world are its own people and its neighbours, and the most eager for it are those far away from it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 9, Verse 40:**

(From the notebook of the judge, from a juz' containing explanations of Qur'anic verses, transmitted from Imam Ahmad)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility (sakinah) upon him﴾

He said: "It refers to Abu Bakr, and the Prophet ﷺ had already been sent down tranquility."

I say: Our shaykh Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, held the opposite of this and would say: "The pronoun refers to the Prophet ﷺ and to his companion as a follower of him. It is he (the Prophet ﷺ) upon whom tranquility was sent down, and it is he whom Allah supported with armies, and this extended to his companion." End of quote.

(A subtle point)

Some of the knowers (ʿārifīn) said: "Special closeness to Allah has nothing to do with sorrow."

His saying, may Allah have mercy on him: "The knowledge of Allah, its light has illuminated every darkness, and its joy has revealed every distress." This is a statement of the utmost beauty. For whoever knows Allah loves Him without doubt, and whoever loves Him, the clouds of darkness disperse from him, and worries, griefs and sorrows are cleared from his heart. His heart is filled with delight and joy, and congratulations and glad tidings come to him from every side. There is no sorrow with Allah ever. For this reason Allah, Exalted is He, related of His Prophet ﷺ that he said to his companion Abu Bakr: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40]. This indicates that there is no sorrow with Allah, and that whoever Allah is with, what has he to do with sorrow? Sorrow is entirely for the one who has lost Allah. Whoever has attained Allah, over what would he grieve? And whoever has lost Allah, in what would he rejoice?

Allah said: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice"﴾ [Yunus: 58]. So rejoicing in His bounty and mercy follows from rejoicing in Him, glory be to Him.

So the believer rejoices in his Lord more than anyone rejoices in what they rejoice in: a beloved, a life, wealth, a blessing, or a kingdom.

The believer rejoices in his Lord more than all of this, and the heart does not attain the reality of life until it tastes this joy and delight, so that its happiness appears in the heart and its radiance appears on the face. Thus he attains a state from the states of the people of Paradise, to whom Allah gave radiance and joy.

For the like of this let the workers work, and in it let the competitors compete. This is the knowledge toward which those of high resolve and firm determination strive, and toward which the possessors of distinguished qualities and noble traits race.

A poet said:
"Those are noble qualities, not two bowls of milk
mixed with water; what then remains after its foam?"

(Section)

When the Messenger (ﷺ) pledged allegiance with the people of al-ʿAqabah, he commanded his companions to emigrate to Madinah. Quraysh knew that his companions had increased and that they would protect him, so they applied their minds to devising stratagems. Some proposed imprisonment, some proposed exile, then their opinion settled on killing him. Then the messenger came with the news from the heavens, commanding him to leave his bed. So ʿAli spent the night in his place, and al-Siddiq rose to accompany him on the journey. When they left the houses of Makkah, al-Siddiq's caution intensified: he would mention the watchers and walk ahead, and at times he would mention the pursuers and fall back behind, and at times (he would move) to his right, and at times to his left, until they reached the cave. Al-Siddiq began by entering it so as to be a shield for him, in case there was any harm inside. Allah caused a tree to grow which had not been there before, which darkened the (view of the) pursued and misled the pursuer. A spider came and covered the entrance of the cave, weaving its web in the manner of a curtain, and it made the covering firm, until the tracker who followed the trail was blinded. He also sent two doves, which made a nest there. He placed a veil over the eyes of the seekers. This is more eloquent as a miracle than resisting the people with armies. When the people stood over their heads, and their speech came within hearing of the Messenger and al-Siddiq, al-Siddiq, his anxiety having intensified, said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to look at what is beneath his feet, he would see us beneath his feet." The Messenger said: "O Abu Bakr, what is your opinion of two whom Allah is the third of?"

When the Messenger saw that his (Abu Bakr's) grief had intensified, not for himself but for his companion, he strengthened his heart with the glad tidings of: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾. Thus the secret of this association in companionship became apparent in wording, just as it became apparent in ruling and meaning. For it is said "Messenger of Allah" and "companion of the Messenger of Allah." Then when he died, he was called "Caliph of the Messenger of Allah." Then the attribution of the caliphate ended with his death, and he was called "Commander of the Faithful."

They remained in the cave three nights, then came out of it, while the tongue of destiny was saying: "You will enter it (the journey) such an entry as no one has entered before you, and it is not fitting for anyone after you." When they set out into the desert, Suraqah ibn Malik pursued them. When he was about to succeed, the Messenger sent against him one of the arrows of supplication, and the legs of his horse sank into the earth up to its belly. When he knew that he had no way against them, he began offering wealth to the one who had returned the keys of the treasures, and offering provision to one who was satisfied.

"I spend the night with my Lord, who feeds me and gives me drink." The gift of "the second of two" was reserved for al-Siddiq alone among all. He is the second in Islam, in sacrificing himself, in asceticism, in companionship, in the caliphate, in age, and in the cause of death, for the Messenger died from the effect of poison, and Abu Bakr was poisoned, so he died.

Among the ten promised Paradise, ʿUthman, Talhah, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas embraced Islam at his hands. On the day he embraced Islam he had forty thousand dirhams, and he spent them at the time Islam most needed them. For this reason his expenditure was said to have benefited Islam more than the wealth of anyone else: "No wealth has benefited me as the wealth of Abu Bakr has benefited me." He is better than the believer of the family of Pharaoh, because that man concealed his faith, while al-Siddiq proclaimed it openly. And he is better than the believer of the family of Yasin, because that man strove for an hour, while al-Siddiq strove for years.

A bird of poverty saw the seed of generosity, and it cried out: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?﴾ So he cast to it the seed of wealth upon the meadow of contentment, and he lay down upon the bed of poverty. The bird carried the seed to the crop of multiplication, then rose upon the branches of a tree of truthfulness, singing the arts of praise. Then in the sanctuaries of Islam he recited: ﴿And the most pious will be spared it, who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾.

The verses and the reports have spoken of his virtue, and the Muhajirun and the Ansar agreed upon his pledge. O you who hate him, in your hearts remembrance of him is a fire; every time his virtues are recited, humiliation rises over you. Did the disbelieving Rafidah not hear: ﴿The second of two, when they were in the cave﴾?

He was called to Islam and did not hesitate or refuse; he walked the clear path and did not slip or stumble; he endured in his time against the enemies under the impact of the spears; he increased spending and did not reduce it until his cloak was threadbare. By Allah, he added to the refining of every dinar, every dinar: ﴿The second of two, when they were in the cave﴾.

Whoever was the companion of the Prophet in his youth, who among his companions was foremost to faith, who gave a quick answer in his presence, who was first to pray with him, who was last to pray with him, who lay beside him in his grave after death? Then recognise the right of the neighbour.

On the day of apostasy he rose with understanding and vigilance, and he made clear from the text of the Book a meaning subtle beyond the sharpness of glances. The lover rejoices in his virtues, and the hater is enraged. The Rafidi's grief is that he would flee from the gathering of his remembrance, but where is the escape?!

How many times he protected the Messenger with wealth and self, and he was closest to him in his life, and he is his companion in the grave. His virtues are great and free from any doubt.

O wonder, one who would cover the eye of the sun's light at midday! They entered a cave which no one dwells in, so al-Siddiq became fearful of the calamities. The Messenger said: "What is your opinion of two, when Allah is the third?"

Then tranquility was sent down, and the fear of calamity was removed. Anxiety departed, and the life of the one who remains became pleasant. Then the herald of victory stood calling from the tops of the minarets of the cities: ﴿The second of two, when they were in the cave﴾.

His love, by Allah, is the head of the Hanifiyyah, and his hatred indicates corruption of the heart. He is the best of the Companions and of kin, and the proof for this is strong. Were it not for the correctness of his leadership, it would not have been said "Ibn al-Hanafiyyah."

Gently, gently, for the blood of the Rafidah has boiled. By Allah, we did not love him out of contempt for others, nor do we hold contempt for anyone else; rather, we took the words of ʿAli, and they sufficed us.

"The Messenger of Allah was pleased with you for our religion; should we not be pleased with you for our worldly affairs?"

By Allah, you have taken revenge against the Rafidah. By Allah, the right of al-Siddiq is binding upon us. We judge by his praises, and we are delighted, with the eye of the Sunni being cooled by what we affirm. Whoever is a Rafidi, let him not return to us, and let him make excuses to me.

(Benefit)

The Prophet's ﷺ hiring of ʿAbd Allah ibn Uraiqit al-Dili, who was a disbeliever, as a guide at the time of the emigration is evidence that it is permissible to refer to a disbeliever in medicine, eye-salve, medicines, writing, arithmetic, defects and similar matters, so long as he does not hold a position that requires justice. And it does not follow merely from his being a disbeliever that he cannot be trusted in anything at all, for there is nothing more dangerous than guidance on the road, especially on a road like the road of the emigration.

[Section: The Station of Tranquility]

From the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of tranquility (sakinah).

This station is among the stations of gifts, not among the stations of acquisitions. Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned tranquility in His Book in six places.

The first: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And their Prophet said to them: "Indeed, the sign of His kingship is that there will come to you the chest, within which is tranquility from your Lord"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 248].

The second: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 26].

The third: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When he said to his companion: "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40].

The fourth: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, that they might increase in faith along with their faith; and to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Fath: 4].

The fifth: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Certainly Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest﴾ [al-Fath: 18].

The sixth: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. And the verse.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, when matters grew severe upon him, would recite the verses of tranquility.

And I heard him say, concerning a great event that befell him during his illness, which minds cannot bear, namely a battle against satanic spirits which appeared to him at a time of weakness of strength, that he said: "When the matter grew severe upon me, I said to my relatives and those around me: 'Recite the verses of tranquility.'" He said: "Then that state passed from me, and I sat down, and there was no disturbance left in me."

I too have tried reciting these verses when the heart is agitated by what comes upon it, and I have seen a great effect of them in its calm and reassurance.

The essence of tranquility is reassurance and dignity, and the calm which Allah sends down into the heart of His servant when it is agitated by the intensity of fears, so that after that he is not disturbed by what comes upon him. It necessitates for him an increase in faith, strength of certainty, and steadfastness.

For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, informed of its being sent down upon His Messenger ﷺ and upon the believers in situations of unease and agitation: such as the day of the emigration, when he and his companion were in the cave while the enemy was above their heads; had one of them looked at what was beneath his feet, he would have seen them. And such as the day of Hunayn, when they turned back fleeing because of the severity of the might of the disbelievers, none of them turning towards another. And such as the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when their hearts were agitated by the domination of the disbelievers over them, and their entering under their conditions which souls cannot bear. And consider the weakness of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, in bearing it, though he is ʿUmar, until Allah strengthened him through al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Every tranquility in the Qur'an is reassurance, except the one in Surat al-Baqarah."

In the two Sahihs, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: "I saw the Prophet ﷺ carrying earth from the trench until the dust covered the skin of his belly, and he was reciting a verse of ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him:

"O Allah, had it not been for You, we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity, nor would we have prayed.
So send down tranquility upon us, and make our feet firm if we meet (the enemy).
Indeed the ones before us have rebelled against us, and if they intend a trial, we refuse."

And in the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the earlier books: "I am sending a prophet who is unlettered, who is neither harsh nor coarse, nor shouting in the markets, nor one who adorns himself with obscenity, nor one who speaks evil. I will guide him to every beautiful thing, and grant him every noble character. Then I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner consciousness, wisdom his intellect, truthfulness and fidelity his nature, forgiveness and kindness his character, justice his way, truth his law, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad his name."

(Faa'idah)

Placing a reproach upon an act from God, Exalted is He, does not indicate that the act is forbidden.

God, Exalted is He, reproached His Prophet in five places in His Book: in al-Anfal, in Bara'ah (al-Tawbah), in al-Ahzab, in Surat al-Tahrim, and in Surat 'Abasa. This is contrary to Abu Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Salam, who considered reproach to be among the indications of prohibition.

= Al-Biqa'i said:

﴿God pardon you﴾, i.e., the Possessor of Majesty and Honour pardon you. This is like the custom of the Arabs in addressing their elders, by saying: "May God set right the Amir, and the King," and the like.

Since it is known that he (ﷺ) would only grant permission to what he saw as pleasing to God, such as winning them over and the like, He, glorified is He, made clear that He was not pleased with his leaving off the permission. So He said, as a metaphor for that: ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾, i.e., to stay behind from you, holding to what had preceded of the command to be gentle with them and to pardon them, in agreement with what you were created upon of loving kindness. This was only at the beginning of the matter, out of fear of dispute and strife. But now the religion has risen high and the affair of the believers has become firmly established, so what is commanded is to be firm with the hypocrites. Would that you had not granted them permission ﴿until it becomes clear to you﴾, i.e., with complete clarity, ﴿those who are truthful﴾, i.e., in upholding the commands, by what they acknowledged of the word of monotheism, ﴿and you know the liars﴾, i.e., regarding what they displayed of faith with their tongues. For if you had not granted them permission, they would have stayed behind without permission, not observing their covenant which they pledged to you of obedience in hardship and ease, in eagerness and in reluctance.

Abu Hayyan said: "And ﴿until﴾ is the endpoint of the interrogative," end.

This is because, although it enters upon an affirmative verb, its meaning is negation, i.e., "What is the matter with you that you did not make them go out to battle with you, so that by that carrying out it would become evident who obeys and who disobeys." The conclusion is that what the Prophet (ﷺ) did was good and in agreement with what God commanded him, for he does not speak from whim, but from the command of God, either by a fresh revelation that has just arrived, or by reliance upon a prior revelation already present and ready. And what God, glorified is He, pointed to is the best example, ﴿That God may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2], by way of "the good deeds of the righteous are the misdeeds of those brought near," and by way of elevation from a lofty station to a higher station, as a way of dealing with them justly once it became clear that they were not people of virtue.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 46:

God disliked their acts of obedience, because of the corruption of their hearts and the depravity of their intentions. So He hindered them from them and kept them seated. He hated their nearness to Him and their proximity to Him, because of their inclination toward His enemies. So He drove them away from Him and removed them far. They turned away from His revelation, so He turned away from them. He made them wretched, and how fortunate they were not. He passed upon them a just judgment, such that there is no hope for them in success after it, except that they be among those who repent. Then Almighty God said: ﴿Had they desired to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation. But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 46]

Then He mentioned His wisdom in their hindrance and their being kept seated, and in their being driven away from His door and removed, and that this is from His kindness to His friends and their felicity. He, who is the Most Wise of judges, said: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption, and they would have hurried about among you, seeking to cause you discord, and among you there are those who listen to them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47]

(Fasl)

As for the hindrance (al-tathbit), Almighty God said: ﴿Had they desired to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation. But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit."﴾

And al-tathbit (hindrance) is turning a person back from the thing he is doing. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He means: He forsook them and made them lazy about going out."

And in another narration he said: "He detained them."

Muqatil said: "And He inspired into their hearts: sit with those who sit."

And God, glorified is He, has made clear His wisdom in this hindrance and forsaking, before and after, saying: ﴿Only those seek your permission who do not believe in God and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt, so they are hesitating in their doubt. And had they desired to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation. But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit."﴾

So when they abandoned faith in Him and in meeting Him, and doubted what has no doubt in it, and did not intend to go out in obedience to God, and did not prepare for it nor take up its equipment, God, glorified is He, disliked the dispatch of one whose state is such. For whoever does not raise his head toward Him and His Messenger or His Book, and does not accept His gift which He sent to him by the hand of the dearest of His creation to Him and the most honored of them before Him, and does not recognize the worth of this blessing nor give thanks for it, but rather replaces it with disbelief, then the obedience of such a person and his going out with His Messenger is something God, glorified is He, dislikes. So He hindered him, lest there occur what He dislikes of his going out, and He inspired into his heart, by decree and by existence, that he should sit with those who sit.

[Degrees of Entrusting (Tafwid)]

[The First Degree: that he knows the servant possesses no capacity (istita'ah) before his action]

He said: "It is in three degrees. The first: that he knows the servant possesses no capacity before his action. So he does not feel safe from deception, nor despair of aid, nor rely upon an intention."

That is, he is certain that his capacity is in the hand of God, not in his own hand; He is its owner, not he. For if He does not give him the capacity, he is powerless. He moves only by God, not by himself. So how can he feel safe from deception, when he is one who is moved, not one who moves? He is moved by the One whose movement is in His hand; if He wills, He hinders him and keeps him seated with those who sit.

As He said regarding those whom He denied this success: ﴿But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 46]

This is the deception (makr) of God toward the servant: that He cuts off from him the sources of His success, leaves him between himself and his own self, does not send forth his motives, and does not move him toward what pleases Him and what He loves. This is not a right owed by God, such that He would be a wrongdoer in withholding it—exalted is God above that with a great exaltation. Rather, it is merely His bounty, which is praised when He gives it to whoever He gives it to, and praised when He withholds it from whoever He withholds it from. So to Him is praise for this and for that.

Whoever understands this has understood a great gate of the secret of destiny (qadar), and many difficulties have become clear to him. He, glorified is He, does not will for His servant an act which He performs upon His servant whereby what He loves and is pleased with comes about from him. He withholds from him the act of Himself in him, which is His success, because He dislikes it, and He compels him to perform what displeases Him; rather, He leaves him to his own self, his own power, and his own strength, and forsakes him. This is the deception.

His saying: "nor despair of aid" means: when the one moving him is the Lord, exalted is His majesty, who is most capable of the capable, who alone created and provided, and who is most merciful of the merciful. How, then, would he despair of His aid to him?

His saying: "nor rely upon an intention" means: he does not depend upon his intention and resolve, and trust in them. For his intention and resolve are in the hand of God, Exalted, not in his hand. They belong to God, not to him. So let his trust be in the One in whose hand they are in truth, not in one upon whom they are merely passing by judgment.

(Question)

If you say: How does He be pleased with something for His servant and not help him to it?

I say: Because helping him to it may entail the loss of something beloved to Him greater than the attainment of that obedience which He is pleased with for him. And the occurrence of that obedience from him may include a corruption which is more hateful to Him, glorified is He, than His love for that obedience, such that its occurrence from him entails a dominant corruption and forfeits a dominant benefit. And God, Exalted, has indicated this in His saying: ﴿Had they desired to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation. But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit"—had they gone out among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption, and they would have hurried about among you, seeking to cause you discord, and among you there are those who listen to them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 46-47]

So God, glorified is He, informed that He disliked their being dispatched with His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to the expedition. It is an act of obedience and nearness, and He had commanded them to it; but when He disliked it from them, He held them back from it. Then He mentioned, glorified is He, some of the corruptions that would have followed from their going out had they gone out with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, mischief and evil. ﴿And they would have hurried about among you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, they would have run about between you with corruption and evil. ﴿Seeking to cause you discord, and among you there are those who listen to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, those who accept from them and respond to them. Thus there would arise, from the mingling of these people's striving in corruption and those people's acceptance of them, an evil greater than the benefit of their going out.

So wisdom and mercy required that He prevent them from going out and keep them seated from it.

Take this example as a foundation for this chapter, and measure by it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 9, verse 47:**

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾: that is, those who accept and submit to them.

It has been said: "They are spies and informants." But this is not correct. Spies and informants exist between two opposing groups that are not mixed together, so one needs spies and informants. This verse, however, concerns the hypocrites, who were mixed in among the Companions, so they had no need for spies and informants.

Once this is understood: the hearing of perception (*sam' al-idrak*) takes its object directly, while the hearing of acceptance (*sam' al-qabul*) takes it with the preposition *li-* (لام) at times and with *min* (مِن) at others. This depends on meaning. When the context requires acceptance, it takes *min*; when it requires submission, it takes *li-*.

As for the hearing of response (*sam' al-ijabah*), it takes *li-*, as in "God hears whoever praises Him" (*sami'a Allahu liman hamidah*), because it includes the meaning of "responded to him." There is no omission there; rather, the verb is used in an implied sense. As for the hearing of understanding (*sam' al-fahm*), it takes its object directly, because what it conveys takes its object directly.

**(Section)**

From the hearing of acceptance is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, those who accept from them and respond to them. This is the more correct of the two opinions regarding the verse.

As for the view of those who said, "They are their spies and informants," it is weak. God, glorified be He, informed us of His wisdom in discouraging them from going out, namely that their going out would cause corruption, ruin, and spreading of sedition among the army. Among the army were those who would accept from them and respond to them. So keeping them back was a kindness to them and a mercy, so that they would not fall into the difficulty of accepting from them.

As for the army containing spies and informants of theirs, this has no connection to the wisdom of discouraging and restraining them. It is known that their spies and informants were from among them. And He, glorified be He, has informed us that He restrained them so that they would not spread corruption in the army and would not seek to stir up sedition against them. This sedition is only averted by restraining them and restraining their spies and informants.

Moreover, spies are called "eyes" (*uyun*) in common usage, but they are not called "listeners" (*sammaʿun*).

Furthermore, this is parallel to His saying, may He be exalted, concerning their Jewish brethren: ﴿listeners to falsehood, devourers of the unlawful gain﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 42], that is, accepting of it.

The point is that the hearing of the elite of the elite, the closest ones, is the hearing of the Qur'an in its three aspects: perception, understanding, and reflection, and response. Every hearing in the Qur'an for which God praised His Companions and commended them, and which He commanded His allies to adopt, is this hearing.

It is the hearing of the verses, not the hearing of verses of poetry; the hearing of the Qur'an, not the hearing of the Devil's flutes; the hearing of the words of the Lord of the earth and the heavens, not the hearing of the odes of poets; the hearing of guidance, not the hearing of odes; the hearing of the Prophets and Messengers, not the hearing of singers and merry-makers.

This hearing is a driver that drives the hearts toward the neighbourhood of the Knower of the Unseen, and a guide that leads the souls to the abode of joy, and a mover that stirs what is still in the resolves toward the highest stations and loftiest ranks, and a caller that calls to faith, and a guide that leads the caravan along the path to the Gardens, and a summoner who calls the hearts morning and evening, from the Splitter of the dawn: "Come to prayer, come to success, come to success."

Whoever chooses this hearing is not left without guidance to a proof, insight into a lesson, a reminder of knowledge, reflection on a sign, indication toward right guidance, a refutation of error, direction away from deviation, insight out of blindness, a command to what is good, a prohibition of harm and corruption, guidance to light, a bringing out from darkness, a restraint from desire, an urging toward piety, a clarifying of insight, life for the heart, nourishment, medicine and cure, protection and salvation, the removal of doubt, the clarification of proof, the establishing of truth, and the nullification of falsehood.

**[Section: On the Hearing of Response]**

As for the hearing of response: it is found in such a saying as His, may He be exalted: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47], that is, responding to them. And in His saying: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41], that is, responding to it. This is the intended meaning. And this is the meaning of the worshipper's saying: "God hears whoever praises Him," that is, God responds to the praise of whoever praises Him.

It is this hearing which God, mighty and majestic, denied concerning those in whom He saw no good, in His saying: ﴿And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾ [al-Anfal: 23], that is, He would have made them hear with a hearing of response and submission. It has also been said that the meaning is "He would have made them understand." According to this, the meaning would be "He would have made their hearts hear," for the hearing of the heart includes understanding.

The correct view is that both meanings are intended. If He had known any good in them, He would have made them understand, and would have made them respond to what they heard and understood.

The point is that the hearing of response is the hearing of the submission of the heart, the spirit, and the limbs to what the two ears have heard.

**(Section)**

*Al-khabal* means corruption and disorder. So if they had gone out with the believers, they would have corrupted their affairs and caused disorder and discord among them. Ibn Abbas said: "They would not have increased you except in *khabal*, that is, weakness and cowardice." He meant they would make them cowardly in facing the enemy by exaggerating their affair and magnifying it in their hearts. Then He said: ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾, that is, they would have rushed to enter among you to create division and corruption. Ibn Abbas said: "He means they would weaken your courage, namely by dividing them, so that the word is divided and they become cowardly before the enemy."

Al-Hasan said: "*Lawda'u khilalakum*: they would have spread between you with tale-bearing to corrupt relations between people."

Al-Kalbi said: "They would have gone among you seeking to find fault with you." Labid said:

*"We saw ourselves hastening to the seal of blame,*
*and magic with food and drink."*

That is, hastening. From this is the saying of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a:

*"Ruin upon them, for the recognition, when they recognised me,*
*and they said: 'A man who seeks wrongdoing, who has pressed on,'"*

That is, he hastened until his mount was exhausted. ﴿They seek to cause you sedition, and among you are listeners to them.﴾

Qatadah said: "Among you are those who listen to their speech and obey them."

Ibn Ishaq said: "Among you are people who love them and obey them in what they call them to, because of their nobility among them." According to this view, its meaning is: "Among you are people who listen and obey them, and if these hypocrites accompanied them, they would corrupt them against you." I say: thus "listeners" (*sammaʿun*) includes the meaning of "those who respond."

Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and al-Kalbi said: "The meaning is: among you are spies for them who convey to them what they hear from you," that is, informants. But the first view is the correct one, as God says: ﴿listeners to falsehood﴾, that is, accepting of it. And there were no informants of the hypocrites among the believers, for the hypocrites were mixed with the believers; they would descend with them, travel with them, pray with them, and sit with them, and were not separated from them. They had not sent spies among them to convey their news. This is what one does who has withdrawn from a group and not mixed with it, and has posted spies among them. So the view of Qatadah and Ibn Ishaq is the correct one, and God knows best.

If it is asked: "Their setting out to obey Him is obedience to Him, so how can He dislike it? And if He, glorified be He, dislikes it, He necessarily loves its opposite, for the dislike of one of two opposites entails the love of the other. Then their remaining behind would be beloved to Him, so how does He punish them for it?"

It is said: This is a question of great importance, and it is among the greatest questions in this field. The answers of the sects vary according to their principles. The Jabriyya (the determinist school) answer it by saying that His acts are not to be explained by wisdom and interests, that everything possible is permissible for Him, and that He may punish them for doing what He loves and is pleased with, and for leaving what He hates and is angry at, and that all of this is the same in relation to Him. This group has closed to itself the door of wisdom and causation. The Qadariyya (the free-will school) answer it according to their principles by saying that He, glorified be He, did not truly restrain them or prevent them; rather they prevented themselves and restrained themselves from going out, and they did what He did not want. And since their going out contained the corruption God mentioned, He cast into their souls a dislike of going out with His Messenger. They said: He made the casting of dislike of setting out into their hearts a dislike of will, not that He Himself disliked their setting out, for He commanded them to it. They said: How can He command them to what He dislikes? Yet the one whose insight God has illuminated will not fail to see the corruption of these two answers and their remoteness from the indications of the Qur'an.

The correct answer is that He, glorified be He, commanded them to go out, as obedience to Him and His command, and as following His Messenger (ﷺ), and supporting him and the believers. He loved this for them and was pleased with it as a religion for them. And He knew, glorified be He, that if they went out, it would not occur in this manner; rather their going out would be a going out of abandonment of His Messenger and the believers. So it was a going out that contained what He does not love and is not pleased with, and that entailed the occurrence of what He hates and abhors. So it was hateful to Him in this respect, and beloved to Him in the respect in which His allies went out. He knew that they would not go out except in the hateful manner, so He disliked it, and He punished them for leaving the going out that He loves and is pleased with, not for leaving the going out that He abhors and is angry at. Accordingly, the going out which He disliked from them is not an act of obedience, so that even if they had done it, He would not have rewarded them for it, nor would He have been pleased with it from them. This hateful going out has two opposites: one is the praiseworthy, beloved going out, and this opposite is what He loves.

The second is staying behind from His Messenger and remaining from the campaign with him, and this opposite He also abhors and dislikes. His dislike of going out in the manner they used to go out does not contradict His dislike of this opposite. So one says to the questioner: their remaining behind is hated by Him, but here there are two things hateful to Him, and one of them is more hateful to Him than the other, because it is the greater corruption. For their remaining behind is hateful to Him, and their going out in the manner He mentioned is more hateful to Him. They had no choice but one of the two things hateful to Him, glorified be He, so the greater hateful thing was averted by the lesser hateful thing. For the corruption of their remaining behind is smaller than the corruption of their going out with him, since the corruption of their remaining behind is confined to themselves, while the corruption of their going out would return upon the believers. So reflect on this point.

If you say: "Why did He not guide them to the going out that He loves and is pleased with, which is the going out the believers undertook?" I say: The answer to such a question has been given many times before, and that His wisdom refuses to place guidance in other than its proper place and with other than its people. God knows best where He places His guidance, His success, and His grace, and not every place is fit for that. Placing a thing in other than its place is not befitting His wisdom.

If you say: "Then why did He not make all places fit for it?" I say: His perfect lordship and dominion and the manifestation of the effects of His names and attributes in creation and command would refuse this. Had He done so, it would have been beloved to Him, for He loves to be remembered, thanked, obeyed, affirmed as One, and worshipped. But that would have entailed the loss of what is more beloved to Him: the equal standing of the feet of all creatures in obedience and faith, and His love of making His enemies' armies ready and of taking vengeance on them, and of displaying the worth and nobility of His allies, and singling them out with His grace, and their giving of their souls for Him in opposing those who opposed Him, and the manifestation of His might, power, forcefulness, severity of seizing, and painful punishment. And there are multiples upon multiples of these wisdoms, which creatures have no way, even if they were to reach the utmost in knowledge and understanding, to encompass, and the relation of what they have grasped of them to what remains hidden from them is like a sparrow's peck in the sea.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rarely go out on a military expedition without alluding to it indirectly and concealing it with other matters, except for the expedition of Tabuk, due to the great distance and the severity of the time. So on one day, while he was preparing for it, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Jadd ibn Qays, one of the Banu Salama:

"O Jadd, would you join us this year in fighting the Banu al-Asfar (the Byzantines)?"

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you grant me leave and not tempt me? By Allah, my people know that there is no man more prone to infatuation with women than I am, and I fear that if I see the women of the Banu al-Asfar I will not be able to restrain myself."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him and said: "I have granted you leave." Concerning him the verse was revealed: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me." Unquestionably, they have fallen into temptation.﴾

(Benefit)

Temptation (fitnah) may also be intended to mean disobedience, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 49]. Jadd ibn Qays said this when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him to Tabuk; he said: "Grant me leave to remain behind and do not tempt me by exposing me to the daughters of the Banu al-Asfar, for I cannot restrain myself from them." The Exalted said: ﴿Unquestionably, they have fallen into temptation﴾, meaning they fell into the temptation of hypocrisy and fled into it from the temptation of the daughters of the Banu al-Asfar.

Ibn Zayd said: He means, "Do not tempt me with the beauty of their faces."

Abu al-Aliyah said: "Do not expose me to temptation."

And the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, they have fallen into temptation.﴾

Qatadah said: "What they fell into of temptation by staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and by preferring themselves over him is greater."

So the temptation from which he fled, by his own claim, is the temptation of love for women and his inability to restrain himself from them; and the temptation into which he fell is the temptation of shirk and disbelief in this world, and punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 52:

Among what indicates that the repentance of the zindiq (heretic), after he has been overpowered, does not protect his blood is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Do you await for us aught but one of the two best things (martyrdom or victory), while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, or at our hands?﴾

The salaf (early scholars) said regarding this verse: "﴿or at our hands﴾" means by killing, if you reveal what is in your hearts. And it is as they said, because the punishment for what they conceal of disbelief at the hands of the believers can only be by killing. For if their repentance were accepted after their zandaqah (heresy) had become apparent, the believers would not be able to await for the zanadiqa that Allah afflict them at their hands, because whenever they wanted to punish them for that, they would display Islam, and so they were never afflicted at their hands. The evidences for this are very numerous. At this point, the proponents of this view say: "We are more fortunate with the Revelation and the Sunnah than our opponents in this matter, who denounce us for opposing them," and success is from Allah.

The translation begins with the next sentence, since the passage as given starts mid-argument.

Ibn al-Qayyim: Whoever said that the verse is arranged with an inversion of word order (al-taqdim wa al-ta'khir), as al-Jurjani did, was not correct. He said that His words ﴿in the life of this world﴾ are connected to what comes after a separate clause that is not in its proper place, with the meaning: ﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them by these in the life of this world.﴾

This view is transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father), but the chain is interrupted (munqati'). Qatadah and a group of scholars also adopted it. It seems that they found it difficult to understand how wealth and children could punish people in this world, when those things bring them joy, pleasure and comfort, so they resorted to inversion of word order.

As for those who held that the verse stands in its proper order and wording, they differed about this punishment. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: He punishes them by taking zakat from their wealth and by spending it in jihad. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) adopted this view and explained it, saying: The punishment by these is their being obliged to fulfil the duties and obligations God has imposed on them concerning their wealth, since it is taken from them while they are unwilling, expecting no reward from God, and receiving no thanks or gratitude from the one who takes it, but rather with humiliation and resentment.

This too is a departure from the intended meaning of their being punished in this world by these things, and a failure to grasp the purpose of the verse.

Another group said: Their punishment through these things is that, because of their disbelief, their wealth becomes booty and their children are taken captive, for this is the ruling on the disbeliever, and they are such inwardly. This too is of the same kind as the previous view, for God, glorified is He, confirmed the hypocrites and protected their wealth and children through outward Islam, while He takes charge of their inner states. Had the intended meaning been what these scholars said, His intention, glorified is He, would have been fulfilled, namely that their wealth be seized and their children taken captive. Here the "intention" (irada) is kawniyya (cosmic or creative will, meaning the will of decree), in the sense of His will (mashi'ah). What Allah wills occurs necessarily, and what He does not will does not occur.

The correct view, and Allah knows best, is that their punishment by these things is the observable reality of the punishment suffered by those who seek this world, love it, and prefer it over the Hereafter: through their greed to acquire it, their great exertion in gathering it, and their enduring all kinds of hardships in doing so. You will find no one more exhausted than the person whose greatest concern is this world, and who strives with all his effort to acquire it. Here, punishment (al-'adhab) means pain, hardship and toil, as in the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Travel is a piece of punishment," and his words: "Indeed the dead person is punished by the weeping of his family over him."

That is, he suffers pain and anguish; it does not mean that he is punished for their deeds. Likewise is the one for whom this world is his entire concern or his greatest concern, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the hadith transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and others, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Whoever makes the Hereafter his concern, Allah will place contentment in his heart, gather his affairs for him, and this world will come to him humbled. And whoever makes this world his concern, Allah will place his poverty before his eyes, scatter his affairs for him, and he will receive from this world only what has been decreed for him."

Among the most severe punishments in this world is the scattering of one's affairs, the division of hearts, and poverty being constantly before the servant's eyes, never leaving him. Were it not for the intoxication of the lovers of this world with its love, they would cry out for help from this punishment, though most of them still complain or cry out because of it.

Also in al-Tirmidhi, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said:

"Allah, blessed and exalted, says: 'Son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your heart with richness and close your poverty. If you do not, I will fill your hands with preoccupation and I will not close your poverty.'"

This is also one of the forms of punishment: the preoccupation of the heart and body with bearing the troubles of this world, enduring the hostility of its people, and suffering their enmity. As some of the early generations (salaf) said: Whoever loves this world should prepare himself to bear calamities. The lover of this world is never free of three things: a constant worry, perpetual fatigue, and an endless regret. This is because whoever loves it never attains anything of it except that his soul yearns for what is beyond it, as in the authentic hadith from the Prophet (peace be upon him): "If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would seek a third for them."

'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) compared the lover of this world to a drinker of wine: the more he drinks, the more thirsty he becomes.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya mentioned that al-Hasan al-Basri wrote to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz:

"To proceed: This world is a house of passing, not a house of permanence. Adam (peace be upon him) was sent down into it only as a punishment. So beware of it, O Commander of the Faithful, for provision from it is to leave it, and richness in it is poverty. It has a slain in every age. It humiliates whoever honours it, and makes poor whoever gathers from it. It is like poison that is eaten by one who does not know it, and it is his death. So be in it like one treating his wounds, who endures a little so as to avoid what he dislikes for a long time, and who bears the harshness of the medicine to avoid a long affliction. Beware of this abode that deceives, that cheats, that plots, which has adorned itself with its deceptions, enticed with its delusions, lured with its hopes, and shown itself off to its suitors. It has become like a bride displayed; eyes gaze upon her, hearts are infatuated with her, souls are in love with her, and yet she is a killer to all her husbands. The one who loves her and has obtained his need from her becomes deluded and overbearing, forgets the Return, and busies his mind with her until his foot slips. Then his regret is great, his sorrow multiplies, and the agonies of death and the anguish of loss gather upon him. And the one who loves her and has not attained his desire lives in grief, dies in sorrow, and does not reach what he sought from her, and his soul finds no rest from toil. He departs without provision and arrives without a resting place. So be, when you are most at ease in it, most wary of it, for the companion of this world, whenever he feels secure in its joy, it lifts him toward something hateful. Its ease is joined to affliction, and its remaining is made into an end. Its joy is mixed with sorrow, its hopes are false, its vain desires are untrue, its pure part is turbid, its life is wretched. Had our Lord not informed us of it, nor set forth a parable about it, it would still have awakened the sleeper and alerted the heedless.

How then, when a preacher has come from Allah about it, and a warner has forbidden it? It has no value or weight with Allah, and He has not looked upon it since He created it. Our Prophet (ﷺ) was offered its keys and treasuries, which would not have diminished his standing with Allah by the weight of a gnat's wing, yet he refused to accept them, disliking to love what his Creator hates or to raise what his Lord has lowered. So He withheld it from the righteous by choice, and spread it to His enemies by deception.
