The deluded one, who is able to acquire it, thinks he is honoured by it, forgetting what Allah, mighty and majestic, did to His Messenger (ﷺ) when he tied a stone upon his belly."

Al-Hasan also said: "Some people honoured this world, so it crucified them on wooden planks. Humiliate it, and it becomes most pleasant to you when you humiliate it." This is a broad matter.

The people of this world and its lovers know better what they suffer and the various pains they endure in pursuing it.

Since this world is the greatest concern of one who does not believe in the Hereafter and does not hope to meet his Lord, his punishment through it corresponds to the intensity of his greed for it and the severity of his striving to seek it.

If you wish to know the punishment of its people through it, then reflect on the state of a lover, annihilated in love for his beloved. Whenever he seeks closeness to his beloved, he is pushed away. The beloved is not faithful to him, abandons him, and joins his enemy. He lives in the most wretched state with his beloved, choosing death over him. The beloved is little in fidelity, abundant in estrangement, has many partners, changes swiftly, is great in betrayal, and is constantly changing; his lover cannot feel safe with him regarding his soul or his wealth. Yet the lover has no patience to be without him, and finds no way to a consolation that would relieve him, nor a union that lasts for him. If this lover had no punishment except this immediate one, it would be enough. How much more so when he is cut off from all his pleasures and becomes tormented by the very thing in which he took delight, in proportion to his pleasure in it, which distracted him from his striving for provision and the interests of his Return?

We shall return to the full discussion of this subject in the chapter on treating the heart's sickness through love of this world, if Allah wills. The purpose here is to show that whoever loves something other than Allah, and whose love of it is not for Allah's sake, nor because it helps him obey Allah, will be punished by it in this world before the Day of Resurrection, as it has been said:

"You are slain by everyone you love, so choose carefully for your soul whom you favour in your passion."

When the Day of Return comes, the Just Judge, glorified is He, will cause every lover to be with what he loved in this world. He will be either a bestower of blessings or a punisher to him.

Therefore, the owner of wealth will have his wealth presented to him as a bald, venomous serpent, which seizes him by his two jaws, saying: "I am your wealth, I am your treasure," and plates of fire will be prepared for him, with which his forehead, side and back will be branded.

Likewise, the lover of forms, when he and his beloved gather in disobedience to Allah, Allah will join them in the Fire and each will be punished through the other. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

He, glorified is He, also informed that those who loved one another in this world in association with idolatry will disown one another on the Day of Resurrection, will curse one another, and their refuge will be the Fire, and they will have no helpers.

Thus the lover is with his beloved in this world and in the Hereafter. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, will say to the creation on the Day of Resurrection: "Is it not justice from Me that I make each of you responsible for what he was responsible for in the abode of this world?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "A man is with whom he loves."

(Admonition)

In the hadith of Moses' private conversation with his Lord, which Imam Ahmad transmitted in his book al-Zuhd: "Ismail ibn 'Abd al-Karim ibn Ma'qil narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to us, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih," and he mentioned it, and in it: "Do not let your eyes be captivated by its adornment or by what it has been given to enjoy, nor let your eyes stretch toward it, for it is the flower of the life of this world and the adornment of the affluent. Had I wished to adorn you both with the adornment of this world, such that Pharaoh, when he looked at it, would know that his power could not match what you have been given, I would have done so. But I desire to turn you away from its bliss and withhold it from you, and I do this with My friends. Long ago I have chosen for them in this, for I keep them away from its bliss and ease just as the compassionate shepherd keeps his flock from pastures of ruin. I keep their enjoyment of it and its life far from them, just as the compassionate shepherd keeps his camels away from the lush, blessed pastures. This is not because it is worthless to Me, but so that they may receive their full share of My honour, whole and complete, untouched by this world and not corrupted by desire. Know that the servants have not adorned themselves before Me with any adornment more eloquent than renunciation of this world, for it is the adornment of the God-fearing. Upon them is a garment by which they are recognised, of tranquillity and humility, their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. Those are truly My friends. So when you meet them, lower your wing to them, and humble your heart and tongue before them." And he mentioned the hadith.

Ahmad also said: "Awn ibn Jabir narrated to us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Dawud, from his father, from Wahb, who said: The disciples said: O 'Isa, who are the friends of Allah upon whom there is no fear and who will not grieve?"

He said: "Those who looked into the inner reality of this world when people looked at its immediate appearance. They caused to die within them what they feared would kill them, and they left what they knew would leave them. So their abundance of it became to them insignificance, their remembrance of it became loss, their joy in what they obtained from it became sorrow. Whatever of its gain opposed them, they rejected; whatever of its elevation came to them without right, they lowered. The world was ruined in their eyes, so they do not renew it; it was ruined among them, so they do not rebuild it; it died in their hearts, so they do not revive it. They demolish it and build their Hereafter with it, they sell it and buy with it what will remain for them. They abandoned it, and so they were the joyful ones through it. They looked upon its people fallen in the dust, upon whom the punishments had descended, so they revived the remembrance of death and made the remembrance of life die. They love Allah and love His remembrance, they seek light from His light and give light by it. They have a wondrous report, and with them is the wondrous report. By them the Book stands, and through it they stand; by them the Book speaks, and through it they speak; by them the Book is known, and through it they act. They do not regard gain as gain, even with what they have attained, nor safety as safety, beyond what they hope for, nor fear as fear, beyond what they guard against."

And Rawh narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: It was said to 'Isa ibn Maryam: O Messenger of Allah, would you not take a donkey to ride for your needs?

He said: "I am too honoured before Allah to have anything that would occupy me. And he said: Place your treasures in heaven, for the heart of a man is with his treasure."

And he said: "Beware of the surplus of this world, for the surplus of this world is abomination in the sight of Allah."

And he said: "O Children of Israel, make your houses like the dwellings of guests, for you have no abode in the world except that you are passers-by."

And he said: "O company of the disciples, which of you can build a house upon the waves of the sea?"

They said: "O Spirit of Allah, who could do that?" He said: "Beware of this world, do not take it as a resting place."

And he said: "Eating good bread, drinking sweet water, and sleeping on rubbish heaps with dogs is much for one who wishes to inherit Paradise."

Ahmad said: And Bahz narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Khaythamah, who said: The Messiah said: "How hard it is for the rich to enter Paradise."

And the Messiah said: "The sweetness of this world is the bitterness of the Hereafter, and the bitterness of this world is the sweetness of the Hereafter." And he said: "O Children of Israel, be indifferent to this world and it will be easy for you; humiliate this world and the Hereafter will honour you. Do not honour this world, or the Hereafter will be made light for you, for this world is not worthy of honour, and every day it calls to temptation and loss."

Ishaq ibn Hani' said in his questions: Abu 'Abd Allah (Ahmad) said, while I was leaving his house: "Al-Hasan said: Humiliate this world, for by Allah, it is most pleasant when it is humiliated." And al-Hasan said: "By Allah, I do not care whether it rose or set." He said: Abu 'Abd Allah also said to me: "O Ishaq, how insignificant is this world to Allah, mighty and majestic." And he said: "Its little is repaid, and its much is not repaid."

They said: It has been widely transmitted from the early generations that love of this world is the head of all sins and their root. A hadith has been related about it in a raised form (marfu') that is not authentic, but it is transmitted from the Messiah. 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me from Badil ibn Maysarah, who said: Ja'far ibn Kharfash narrated to me that 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) said: "The head of sin is love of this world; women are the snare of Satan; and wine is the gathering of every evil."

And Imam Ahmad said: Umar ibn Sa'd Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: 'Isa ibn Maryam used to say: "Love of this world is the root of every sin, and wealth has many diseases in it." They asked: "What is its disease?" He said: "One is not safe from pride and vanity." They asked: "And if one is safe?" He said: "Its upkeep will occupy him from the remembrance of Allah, mighty and majestic."

They said: This is known through experience and observation, for its love calls to manifest and hidden sin, especially a sin whose attainment depends upon it. Its lover is intoxicated by its love, so he loses awareness of that sin and its ugliness, and loses his aversion to it and his avoidance of it. Its love leads to doubtful matters, then to what is disliked, then to what is forbidden. It has often led to disbelief. Indeed, all the nations that denied their prophets were driven to their disbelief and destruction only by love of this world, for when the messengers forbade them from polytheism and from the sins through which they earned this world, their love for it drove them to oppose and deny the messengers. So every sin in the world has love of this world at its root. And do not forget the sin of the two parents (Adam and Eve) long ago, for its cause was love of eternal life in this world. And do not forget the sin of Iblis, whose cause was love of leadership, which is more harmful than love of this world. Through it Pharaoh, Haman, their armies, Abu Jahl and his people, and the Jews disbelieved. So love of this world and of leadership is what filled the Fire with its people, and renunciation of this world and of leadership is what filled Paradise with its people. The intoxication of love of this world is far greater than the intoxication of drinking wine, and the one who has this intoxication does not recover from it except in the darkness of the grave. If its veil were lifted from him in this world, he would know the intoxication he was in, and that it is more severe than the intoxication of wine. This world bewitches the intellects with the greatest magic.

Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, who said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar say: "Beware of the sorcery, beware of the sorcery, for it bewitches the hearts of the scholars."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 55 (part 2 of 2):

Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi said: "The world is the wine of Satan. Whoever becomes intoxicated with it does not awaken except in the army of the dead, regretful, among the losers. The least of what comes with loving it is that it diverts one from the love of Allah and His remembrance. Whoever is diverted by his wealth from the remembrance of Allah is among the losers. When the heart is diverted from the remembrance of Allah, Satan takes residence in it and turns it wherever he wills. Among his cunning in evil is that he pleases a person with some acts of good, to show him that he is doing good through them, while his heart has become enslaved to them. How far is what he does of righteousness from his enslavement to them! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the slave of the dinar and the dirham and invoked against him, saying: 'Cursed is the slave of the dinar, cursed is the slave of the dirham. If he is given, he is pleased; if he is denied, he is angry.' This is an explanation from him of their enslavement. The world was presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) in its entirety, and it presented itself to him, but he pushed it away with both hands and turned it back on its heels. Then it was presented after him to his Companions, and it presented itself to them. Some of them followed his way and repelled it, and they were few. Others examined it and said: 'What is in you?' It said: 'In me are the lawful, the doubtful, the disliked and the forbidden.' They said: 'Bring your lawful; we have no need of what is other than it.' So they took its lawful part. Then it presented itself to those after them, and they sought its lawful part but did not find it, so they sought its disliked and doubtful parts. It said: 'The one before you has already taken it.' They said: 'Bring your forbidden,' and they took it. Then those after them sought it, and it said: 'It is in the hands of the oppressors; they have monopolized it over you.' So they schemed to obtain it from them through desire and fear. The one who stretches his hand toward something forbidden finds someone more wicked than him and stronger who has already preceded him to it. All of them are guests, and what is in their hands is a loan, as Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'No one wakes up in this world except as a guest, and his wealth is on loan. The guest departs, and the loan is to be returned.'"

(Section)

They said: The love of this world is the head of all sins and the corrupter of religion, for several reasons:

The first: Loving it entails magnifying it, while it is contemptible in the sight of Allah, and among the greatest sins is magnifying what Allah has belittled.

The second: Allah has cursed it, despised it and hated it, except for what is done for Him in it. Whoever loves what Allah has cursed, despised and hated has exposed himself to trial, to His disdain and His wrath.

The third: When one loves it, he makes it his goal and seeks to reach it through the deeds that Allah has made means to Him and to the Hereafter. So the matter is reversed, wisdom is inverted, his heart is turned upside down, and his journey is reversed backward.

Here there are two matters:
The first: making the means into the goal.
The second: using the deeds of the Hereafter as a means to the world.
This is a corrupt reversal in every respect and a heart overturned to the utmost degree of overturning. This is what fits the saying "exactly like the feather to the feather," namely the words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be shortchanged therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein will come to nothing, and what they used to do is null.﴾ [11:15–16] And the words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the hasty [life], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whomever We wish. Then We have made Hell for him; he will burn in it, censured and rejected.﴾ [17:18] And the words of the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him his tilth, and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him from it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [42:20] These three verses resemble one another and indicate one meaning: whoever directs his deeds toward the world and its adornment, apart from Allah and the Hereafter, will have what he intended, and that is his share; he has no share other than it.

The Prophetic traditions agree with this and explain it, such as the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the three who will be the first to have the Fire kindled with them: "the warrior, the giver of charity, and the reciter, who did all that seeking the world and its reward." It is in Sahih Muslim.

In Sunan al-Nasa'i, from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "A man came to the Prophet and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man fought seeking reward and fame, what does he get?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Nothing for him.' He repeated it three times, and the Messenger of Allah said to him: 'Nothing for him.' Then he said: 'Indeed Allah the Exalted accepts only what is purely for Him and sought with it His face.'" So this one's reward has been nullified and his deed has come to nothing, even though he intended to obtain the reward, because he combined with it the intention of being remembered among people. So his deed was not purely for Allah, and thus all of it was nullified.

In Musnad Imam Ahmad, from Abu Hurayrah: a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man wants to fight in the way of Allah while he seeks the goods of this world." The Messenger of Allah said: "He has no reward." People found this severe and said to the man: "Go back to the Messenger of Allah; perhaps he did not understand." He returned and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man wants to fight in the way of Allah while he seeks the goods of this world." The Messenger of Allah said: "He has no reward." Then he repeated it a third time, and the Messenger of Allah said: "He has no reward."

Also in the Musnad and the Sunan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him), who said that the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever fights in the way of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and in his campaign intends nothing but a rope (of camel-tethering), then he has what he intended."

In the Musnad and the Sunan, from Ya'la ibn Munyah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah used to send me on expeditions. One day he sent me on an expedition, and there was a man who rode a mule. I said to him: 'Mount up, for the Prophet has sent me on an expedition.' He said: 'I will not go out with you until you give me three dinars.' I did so. When I returned from my campaign I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, and the Prophet said: 'He has nothing from this campaign of his, and from his worldly life and his Hereafter except three dinars.'"

In Sunan Abi Dawud, that Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about jihad and raiding." He said: "O Abdullah ibn Umar, if you fight patiently, seeking reward, Allah will raise you up patiently seeking reward; and if you fight showing off and boasting, Allah will raise you up showing off and boasting. O Abdullah ibn Umar, in whatever state you fight or are killed, Allah will raise you in that state."

In the Musnad and the Sunan, from Abu Ayyub (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: "Indeed the cities will be opened to you, and you will strike with armies in them. A man among you will dislike the army (going out), so he will separate from his people and offer himself to the tribes, saying: 'Who will hire me for such-and-such an army?' And that hired man will be (fighting) until the last drop of his blood." So look at what the love of the world has deprived this warrior among warriors of, of reward, and how it corrupted his deed and made him the first of those who enter the Fire.

Fourth: Its love stands between the servant and doing what benefits him in the Hereafter, because he is preoccupied with his beloved. People here have ranks. Some are preoccupied by their beloved from faith and its laws; some from the obligations that are due to Allah and to His creatures, so that he does not fulfill them outwardly or inwardly; some are preoccupied by its love from many obligations; some are preoccupied from an obligation that opposes obtaining it, even if he performs another; some are preoccupied from performing the obligation at its proper time in its proper manner, so he neglects his time and his rights; and some are preoccupied from the enslavement of the heart in the obligation and from devoting it to Allah while performing it, so he performs it outwardly but not inwardly. How far is this from the lovers of the world and its devotees! This is the rarest of them. The least degree of its love is that it diverts one from the happiness of the servant, which is devoting the heart to the love of Allah, the tongue to His remembrance, and gathering one's heart onto one's tongue and one's tongue and heart upon one's Lord. So its lover is infatuated, and his love of it harms his Hereafter without fail, just as the love of the Hereafter harms the world. It has been transmitted in a hadith traced to the Prophet: "Whoever loves his world harms his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter harms his world. So prefer what remains over what perishes."

Section: Fifth: Its love makes it the greatest concern of the servant. It has been transmitted by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has the Hereafter as his greatest concern, Allah will place his richness in his heart, gather his affairs together, and the world will come to him humbled. Whoever has the world as his greatest concern, Allah will place his poverty before his eyes, scatter his affairs, and he will not obtain from the world except what has been decreed for him."

Sixth: The lover of it is the one most tormented by it. He is tormented in its three abodes. He is tormented in the world by seeking it, striving for it and contending with its people; in the intermediate abode (barzakh) by its loss and regret over it, and by being separated from his beloved in a way that he never hopes to be reunited with it, and he finds no other beloved there to replace it. So he is the most tormented of people in his grave. Grief, sorrow, anxiety and regret work upon his spirit as worms and the creatures of the earth work upon his body. As Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to us, Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, that Ezekiel (Hizqil) was among those taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtansar), and he mentioned a long narration concerning him. At its end he said: "While I was sleeping on the bank of the Euphrates, an angel came to me, seized my head and carried me, until he placed me in a field that had been a battlefield. There were ten thousand slain in it, whose flesh the birds and beasts had scattered and whose limbs had been separated. He said to me: 'Indeed a people claim that whoever among them dies or is killed has escaped from Me and my power has gone from him. Call them.' Ezekiel said: 'I called them, and every bone came back to its joint from which it had been severed, so that a man does not know his companion better than the bone knows its joint from which it parted, until some of them were joined to others. Then sinews grew upon them, then flesh grew upon them, then skin was spread over them, while I was watching that. Then he said: "Call their spirits." I called them, and every spirit came back to its body from which it had departed. When they sat up, I asked them: "For what were you (being punished)?" They said: "When we died and departed from life, we met an angel who said: 'Come, bring your deeds and take your rewards; this is our practice regarding you, and regarding those who were before you, and those who will be after you.' He looked at our deeds and found that we used to worship idols. So he sent worms upon our bodies, and the spirits began to suffer from them, and grief was set upon our spirits, and our bodies began to suffer from it. We remained thus, being punished, until you called us." And the lover of the world does not rest.' So their saying 'we used to worship idols' is equivalent to worshipping currency. The worship of wealth and the worship of idols are alike: 'Cursed is the slave of the dinar, cursed is the slave of the dirham.'"

The point is that the lover of the world is punished in his grave and punished on the day he meets his Lord. The Exalted said: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world, and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ [9:55] Some of the early generations said: "He punishes them by gathering it, and their souls depart by loving it, while they are disbelievers by withholding Allah's right in it."

Section: Seventh: The one who loves it and is infatuated with it, who prefers it over the Hereafter, is among the most foolish of creatures and the least intelligent, for he has preferred imagination over reality, dream over waking, a fleeting shadow over lasting bliss, and a perishable abode over the everlasting abode. He has sold eternal life for the most pleasant life, which is nothing but dreams of sleep or a passing shadow. The intelligent person is not deceived by such things. Like the Bedouin who stopped at a people's place, and they served him food. He ate, then rose to the shadow of a tent and slept. They uprooted the tent, and it fell on him. He woke up saying:

"Whoever has his world as his greatest concern,
Is clinging to a rope of delusion."

Some of the early generations used to recite this verse:

"O people of worldly pleasures that have no permanence,
Indeed being deceived by a fleeting shadow is folly."

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la said: "I have not likened the world to anything except a man who slept and saw in his dream what he hated and what he loved, and while he was like that, he woke up."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Abu Ali al-Ta'i narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman al-Bukhari narrated to us, from Layth, who said: "Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him) saw the world in the form of an old woman, wearing every kind of adornment. He said: 'How many times have you married?' She said: 'I cannot count them.' He said: 'Did they all die and leave you, or did they all divorce you?' She said: 'Rather, I killed them all.' Isa said: 'Woe to your remaining husbands! How do they not take warning from your former husbands? You destroy them one by one, and they are not wary of you.'"

I see the wretched of mankind never tire of her,
Though they are naked and hungry in her.
I see her, though she is loved, as
A summer cloud that will soon disperse.

The thing most similar to the world is a shadow. One thinks it has a firm reality, but it is contracting and receding, so one follows it to catch it, but one never reaches it. The thing most similar to it is a mirage, which the thirsty person thinks is water until he reaches it and finds nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full, for Allah is swift in reckoning. The thing most similar to it is a dream, in which the servant sees what he loves and what he hates, and when he wakes up he knows it has no reality. The thing most similar to it is an ugly old woman, hideous in appearance and in what she conceals, treacherous to husbands. She adorns herself for suitors with every adornment and covers every ugliness, so whoever does not look beyond her outward appearance is deceived by her and seeks marriage. She says: "There is no dowry except the cash of the Hereafter, for we are rivals, and our union is neither permitted nor lawful." He prefers the immediate suitor and says: "What harm is there in one who is fond of her?" But when she unveils her face and loosens her garment, behold, every calamity and affliction. Some of her suitors divorce her and find rest; others choose to remain, and their wedding night is not completed except with wailing and screaming.

By Allah, her crier has announced among all creatures: "Come to success," though it is not success. So the diligent and the Muslims rose toward her, continuing their pursuit of her from morning until evening. They traveled through the night, but the people did not praise the night journey at dawn. They flew in pursuit of her prey, and not one of them returned except with a broken wing. They fell into her snare, and she delivered them to the slaughter.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Fudayl ibn Iyad say: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "The world will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a gray-haired old woman, blue-eyed, her fangs showing, her form disfigured. She will look over the creatures, and it will be said: 'Do you recognize this?' They will say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from knowing this.' It will be said: 'This is the world, over which you quarreled, by which you severed the ties of kinship, envied one another, hated one another, and were deceived.' Then she will be thrown into Hell, and she will call out: 'O Lord, where are my followers and my partisans?' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Join her to her followers and partisans.'"

Consider how He made the giving (al-itaʾ) belong to Allah and to His Messenger, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾.

He also made the sufficiency (al-hasb) belong to Him alone. He did not say: "And they said: Allah is sufficient for us and His Messenger," but rather He made it the pure right of Him alone, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, to Allah we turn in hope﴾.

And He did not say: "And to His Messenger," but rather He made the turning in desire (al-raghba) to Him alone, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when you are free, labour, and to your Lord turn with longing﴾.

So the turning in desire (al-raghba), the reliance (al-tawakkul), the returning in repentance (al-inabah), and the sufficiency are for Allah alone, just as worship (al-ibadah), god-fearing piety (al-taqwa), and prostration are for Allah alone, and vowing (al-nadhr) and swearing (al-halif) are only for Allah, glorified is He.

(Benefit)

A servant takes what is forbidden to him only from two directions:

The first: his bad opinion of his Lord, and that if he obeyed Him and preferred Him, He would not give him something better than it that is lawful.

The second: that he knows this, and that whoever leaves something for Allah, Allah compensates him with something better than it, but his desire overcomes his patience, and his whim overcomes his reason. The first arises from weakness of knowledge, and the second from weakness of intellect and insight.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "Whoever has his heart gathered upon Allah in supplication, He does not turn it away."

I say: When his heart is gathered upon Him, his need is genuine, his poverty is true, and his hope is strong, then his supplication is hardly ever rejected.

[Section: The one who opposes Allah and His Messenger has no covenant]

The seventh proof: His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever? That is the great disgrace.﴾

He, glorified is He, mentioned this verse immediately after His saying: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear."﴾ [At-Tawbah: 61]. So He made them harmers of him by their saying, "He is an ear." Then He said: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger...﴾

Thus He made them opposers. And it is known with certainty that whoever openly reviles Allah and His Messenger and attacks their religion is greater in opposition to them both. When it is established that he is an opposer, Almighty and Exalted is He has said: ﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger are among the most humiliated﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 20]. The "most humiliated" (al-adhallu) is more emphatic than "humiliated" (dhalil), and one is not most humiliated until he fears for his own life and his property, because whoever has inviolable blood and property, which may not be violated, is not most humiliated. This is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Humiliation has been decreed upon them wherever they are found, except by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 112]. So He, glorified is He, made clear that wherever they are found, humiliation is upon them, except with a covenant. It is thus known that whoever has a covenant and a rope by which he is secure for his life and property is not under humiliation, even if poverty (maskanah) is upon him, since poverty may exist without humiliation. And He, glorified is He, placed the opposers among the most humiliated, so they cannot have a covenant, since a covenant contradicts humiliation, as the verse indicates. This is evident, for the most humiliated person has no strength by which he can defend himself against one who intends him harm. So if he has a covenant from the Muslims by which it becomes obligatory for them to support and protect him, he is not most humiliated. Thus it is established that the one who opposes Allah and His Messenger does not have a covenant that protects him.

(Section: On the Account of Tabuk)

A group of the hypocrites, among them Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and among them a man from Ashja' who was an ally of Banu Salamah, called Makhshi ibn Humayr, said to one another: "Do you think that the battle of the sons of al-Asfar (the Byzantines) is like the fighting of the Arabs against one another? By Allah, it is as if we see you tomorrow tied together in ropes!" — spreading alarm and intimidation among the believers. Then Makhshi ibn Humayr said: "By Allah, I wish that I could be made to stand trial on condition that each of us be struck a hundred lashes, and that we be spared from a Qur'an being revealed about us because of this saying of yours."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Ammar ibn Yasir: "Go to the people, for they have burned (their words). Ask them what they said, and if they deny it, say: 'Rather, you said such and such.'" So 'Ammar went to them and said that to them. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) making excuses to him. Wadi'ah ibn Thabit said: "We were only plunging in and playing." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 65]

Makhshi ibn Humayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, my name and my father's name have held me back." He was the one pardoned in this verse. He named himself 'Abd al-Rahman, and asked Allah to be killed as a martyr whose place is not known, so he was killed on the day of al-Yamamah and no trace of him was found.

Ibn 'A'idh mentioned in his book "al-Maghazi" that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped at Tabuk at a time when its water was scarce. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) scooped up a handful of water with his hand, rinsed his mouth with it, then spat it back into the spring, and its spring gushed forth until it was full, and it remains so until this hour.

I say: In Sahih Muslim, he said before reaching it: "Tomorrow, God willing, you will come to the spring of Tabuk, and you will not reach it until the afternoon has come. Whoever comes to it, let him not touch any of its water until I arrive." He said: "So we came to it, and two men had already preceded us to it, and the spring was like a thong's latchet, trickling with a little water. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked them: 'Have you touched any of its water?' They said: 'Yes.' So the Prophet (ﷺ) rebuked them and said to them what Allah willed him to say. Then they scooped from the spring little by little until it gathered in something, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) washed his face and hands in it, then returned it to it, and the spring flowed with abundant water until the people had drawn water. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'It is near, O Mu'adh, that if your life is prolonged you will see what is here filled with gardens.'"

(Benefit)

In the Arabic language, forgetting (al-nisyan) may mean deliberate abandonment, or it may be the opposite of remembering. God Most High says: ﴿They forgot God, so He forgot them﴾.

That is, they abandoned obedience to God and faith in what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought, so God abandoned them from His mercy. There is no disagreement over this, and no one with even a little knowledge of the interpretation (ta'wil) of the Qur'an is ignorant of it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 69:

Allah, glory be to Him, has censured those who follow conjecture (al-zann) and what their souls desire. Conjecture refers to doubts (al-shubuhat), and what the souls desire refers to appetites (al-shahawat). These are the two things He mentioned in Surat al-Bara'a (Surah 9) in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Like those before you, who were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged.﴾

He mentioned enjoyment of their portion (al-khalaq), which is the indulgence in appetites, and this is their share which they preferred in this world over their share of the Hereafter.

So the indulging (al-khawd) which they followed involved doubts, and they enjoyed appetites and indulged in doubts. From these two arose the blameworthy division which Allah censured in His Book, and He forbade His believing servants from resembling them, saying: ﴿And do not be like those who divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. For those is a great punishment, on the Day when some faces will be whitened and some faces will be blackened.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 105-106]

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The faces of the People of the Sunnah and unity will be whitened, and the faces of the People of division and discord will be blackened."

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us of the nullification of the deeds of the people of appetites and doubts. He, Exalted, said: ﴿Like those before you, who were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged.﴾

So this enjoyment of the portion is their enjoyment of their share of appetites.

Then He said: ﴿and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged﴾, and this is indulging in falsehood in the religion of Allah, which is the indulgence of the people of doubts.

Then He said: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers.﴾ So He, glory be to Him, linked the nullification of deeds and loss to following appetites, which is the enjoyment of the portion, and to following doubts, which is indulging in falsehood.

(Benefit)

Temptation (al-fitna) is of two kinds: the temptation of doubts, which is the greater of the two, and the temptation of appetites.

Allah, glory be to Him, combined mention of both temptations in His saying: ﴿Like those before you, who were greater than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you enjoyed their portion﴾.

That is, they enjoyed their share of the world and its appetites. Al-khalaq is the allotted portion. Then He said: ﴿and you indulged as they indulged﴾, and this is indulging in falsehood, which is doubts.

Thus Allah, glory be to Him, in this verse points to what brings about corruption of hearts and religions: enjoyment of the portion and indulging in falsehood, because the corruption of religion is either by holding false beliefs and speaking them, or by acting contrary to sound knowledge.

The first is innovation (bid'a) and what is related to it, and the second is corruption of deeds through sin (fisq al-a'mal).

The first is corruption from the side of doubts, and the second from the side of appetites.

For this reason the Salaf used to say: "Beware of two kinds of people: the man of desire whose desire has tempted him, and the man of worldliness whose worldliness has blinded him."

(Section)

There has been disagreement about the grammatical position of this kaf (like) and what it relates to. It was said: it is in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e. "you are like those before you." It was said: it is in the accusative by an omitted verb, its estimate being "you did as those before you did." The comparison according to these two opinions is in their deeds. It was said: the comparison is in the punishment. Then it was said: the governing element is omitted, i.e. "He cursed them and punished them as He cursed those before." It was said: rather, the governing element is what preceded, i.e. "Allah's promise to the hypocrites is like His promise to those before you, and their curse is like their curse, and for them is a lasting punishment like the punishment of those before them." The intent is that He, glory be to Him, joined them with those before them in the threat and made them equal in it, just as they were equal in deeds. Their being greater than them in strength and more abundant in wealth and children is an irrelevant difference. So He attached the ruling to the common effective attribute and disregarded the distinguishing attribute. Then He alerted that their sharing in deeds required their sharing in the recompense, and said: ﴿They enjoyed their portion, and you enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged﴾ [al-Tawba: 69]. This is the effective cause and the common attribute, and His saying ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾ [al-Tawba: 69] is the ruling. Those before are the origin (al-asl), and those addressed are the branch (al-far').

'Abd al-Razzaq said in his Tafsir: Ma'mar informed us from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿they enjoyed their portion﴾, that he said: "For their sin." It is also narrated from Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They enjoyed their portion of the Hereafter in this world." Others said: "Their portion of this world."

The reality of the matter is that al-khalaq is the portion and share, as if it is that which was created for the human being and decreed for him, as one says "his qasm (lot) which was divided for him," and "his nasib (portion) which was set up for him," i.e. established, and "his qit (allotment) which was cut for him," i.e. cut off. From it is His saying: ﴿and he has no khalaq in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Baqara: 200], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Only the one who has no khalaq in the Hereafter wears silk in this world."

The verse encompasses everything the Salaf mentioned, for He said: ﴿who were greater than you in strength﴾. By that strength they were able to work for this world and the Hereafter. Likewise wealth and children. That strength, wealth and children are the khalaq; they enjoyed their strength, wealth and children in this world. The very deeds they performed with this strength are part of the khalaq they enjoyed. Had they intended thereby Allah and the Abode of the Hereafter, they would have had a khalaq in the Hereafter. Their enjoyment of these is taking their hasty shares, and this is the state of one who works only for his worldly life, whether his deed is of the type of acts of worship or otherwise. Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned the state of the branches, saying: ﴿you enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion﴾. This indicates that their ruling is their ruling, and that what befell them will befall them, because the ruling of the like is the ruling of its like.

Then He said: ﴿and you indulged as they indulged﴾. It was said: "alladhi" is an attribute of an omitted verbal noun, i.e. "like the indulgence which they indulged in." It was said: of an omitted noun described, i.e. "like the indulgence of the people who indulged." It was said: "alladhi" is a verbal noun (masdariyya), as in "kama," i.e. "like their indulgence." It was said: it is in the position of "alladhina."

The intent is that He, glory be to Him, combined enjoyment of the khalaq with indulgence in falsehood, because the corruption of religion either occurs through false belief and speaking it, which is indulgence, or occurs in action contrary to truth and correctness, which is enjoyment of the khalaq. The first is innovations (bid'a), and the second is following desire (ittiba' al-hawa). These two are the root of every evil, temptation and trial, and by them the Messengers were denied, the Lord was disobeyed, the Fire was entered, and punishments were incurred. The first is from the side of doubts, the second from the side of appetites. For this reason the Salaf used to say: "Beware of two kinds of people: the man of desire whose temptation is his desire, and the man of worldliness whose worldliness has pleased him."

They also used to say: "Beware of the temptation of the corrupt scholar and the ignorant worshipper, for their temptation is a temptation to every person tempted." The first resembles those upon whom is wrath, who know the truth and act contrary to it, and the second resembles those who go astray, who act without knowledge.

In the description of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him: "How patient he was regarding the world, and how similar he was to those who passed before. Innovations came to him and he rejected them, and the world came to him and he refused it." This is the state of the leaders of the righteous whom Allah described in His Book with His saying: ﴿And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient, and they were certain of Our signs﴾ [al-Sajda: 24]. By patience appetites are abandoned, and by certainty doubts are repelled, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿and they advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 3], and His saying: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision﴾ [Sad: 45].

In some mursal reports: "Indeed Allah loves a discerning sight when doubts arrive, and loves complete intellect when appetites descend."

So His saying ﴿you enjoyed your portion﴾ is an indication of following appetites, which is the disease of the disobedient, and His saying ﴿and you indulged as they indulged﴾ is an indication of doubts, which is the disease of innovators, people of desires and disputes. These two often combine, for you rarely find someone of corrupt belief whose corruption does not appear in his action.

The intent is that Allah informed that in this Ummah there are those who enjoy their khalaq as those before them enjoyed their khalaq, and who indulge as they indulged, and that for them is blame and threat as for those before them. Then He urged them to reflection and consideration of those before them, saying: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ [al-Tawba: 70].

So reflect on the soundness of this analogy and its benefit for whom the ruling is attached to, and that the origin and branch are equal in the meaning on which punishment is attached, and it is reinforced, as mentioned, by a kind of greater reason, namely the intensity of strength and abundance of wealth and children. If it is not impossible for Allah to punish the stronger of them for their sin, how could it be impossible for Him to punish one who is weaker than them?

And consider His words, exalted is He: ﴿God has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden. But the pleasure of God is greater﴾. How He made His pleasure (ridwan) the subject of the sentence, indefinite, and then described it as greater than everything they were promised. The least of His pleasure is greater than the Gardens and the pleasant dwellings in them and all that they contain. For this reason, when He manifests Himself to His friends in the Gardens of Eden and offers them whatever they desire, they say: "Our Lord, what could we desire that is better than what You have given us?" Then the Blessed and Exalted says: "I have something better than that for you: I cause My pleasure to descend upon you, so I will never be displeased with you after this, ever."

(Benefit)

God's being pleased with the servant is greater than the Garden and what is in it. This is because pleasure (al-rida) is an attribute of God, while the Garden is His creation. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿But the pleasure of God is greater﴾ [al-Tawba: 72], after His words: ﴿God has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden. But the pleasure of God is greater. That is the great triumph.﴾

This pleasure is the recompense for their being pleased with Him in this world. And since this recompense is the best of recompenses, its cause is the best of deeds.

When the servant is pleased with Him and with what comes from Him in all circumstances, he does not prefer any request over Him. His contentment with what He allots to him, decrees for him, and does to him makes him independent of such requests. He makes remembrance of Him the place of his asking. Rather, his asking of Him becomes asking for help in remembering Him and for reaching His pleasure. Such a person is given the best thing that a petitioner can be given, as came in the hadith: "Whoever is occupied with remembering Me instead of asking Me, I will give him the best of what I give to those who ask."

Indeed, the petitioners asked Him, and He gave them the grace they asked for. The contented ones were pleased with Him, and He gave them His pleasure with them. Their being pleased does not prevent them from asking Him for the causes of pleasure; rather, His companions are insistent in asking Him for that.

(Another Benefit)

A little of His pleasure, and it is not called "little," is greater than the Gardens and what is in them.

In the hadith of the vision: "By God, God has not given them anything more beloved to them than gazing upon His face." And in another hadith: "When they see Him, glorified is He, they will not turn to anything of the bounties they are in, until He veils Himself from them."

[Section: The Degrees of the Sanctities of God]

[The First Degree: Exalting the Command and the Prohibition]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree: exalting the command and the prohibition, not out of fear of punishment, for that would be a contention against the self, nor out of seeking reward. For then he would be looking for wages, and would not be witnessing anyone. Then he would be adorning himself with showing off. All these attributes are branches of the worship of the self.

This point is frequent in the speech of the people. Among people there are those who exalt it and its adherents, believing that this is the highest degree of servanthood: that one does not worship God and carry out His command and prohibition out of fear of His punishment, nor out of hope for His reward. For this one stands with his own aim and the share of his self. Love refuses this, for the lover has no share with his beloved. So his standing with his share is a flaw in his love. And his hope for reward is an aspiration to the notion that he deserves a wage from God, exalted is He, for his deed. In this there are two afflictions: his aspiration to the wage, and his thinking well of his own deed. For his aspiration to deserving the reward, and his fear of punishment, is a contention against the self, since he never ceases to contend with it when it opposes him. He says: "Do you not fear the Fire, its punishment, and what God has prepared for its people?" So the contention between him and his self never ceases.

From another aspect too: he is like one who contends on behalf of himself, repelling from it an adversary who wants its destruction. This is exactly concern for the self and attention to its portions, contending on its behalf, and seeking what it enjoys.

Nothing frees him from this contention and that aspiration except stripping the performance of the command and the prohibition of every cause. Rather, he performs it exalting the One who commands and forbids, and recognizing that He is worthy to be worshipped and that His sacred limits be honored. He deserves worship, exaltation, and majesty for His very essence, as in the Israelite report: "Had I not created a Garden nor a Fire, would I not still be worthy to be worshipped?"

From this is the saying of the poet:

"Suppose the Resurrection had not come with its messengers, and the blazing fire had not been kindled,
Is it not a due and necessary obligation upon the people of the world to thank the Benefactor?"

So the noble, pure souls worship Him because He is worthy to be worshipped, honored, loved, and exalted. He is deserving of worship for His own essence. They said: The servant should not be like a bad hired hand: if he is given his wage he works, and if he is not given it he does not work. That is the slave of wages, not the slave of love and will.

They said: Workers aim at two stations: the station of the Hereafter, and the station of nearness to the One obeyed. God, exalted is He, said concerning His prophet David: ﴿And indeed for him is nearness to Us and a good return﴾ [Sad: 25]. So nearness (zulfa) is the station of nearness, and a good return (husn al-ma'ab) is the goodness of reward and recompense. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿For those who did good is the best, and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The best (al-husna) is the recompense, and the "more" (al-ziyada) is the station of nearness. For this reason it has been interpreted as gazing upon the Face of God, mighty and majestic is He. These are the two things that Pharaoh promised the sorcerers if they overcame Moses. They said to him: ﴿Indeed for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors.﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near﴾ [al-A'raf: 113]. And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿God has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden. But the pleasure of God is greater﴾ [al-Tawba: 72].

They said: The knowers' deeds are directed toward station and rank, while the workers' deeds are directed toward reward and wage. And how far apart are these two!

(Section)

A second group considers this speech to be among the ecstatic utterances (shatahat) and foolish sayings (ra'unat) of these people. They argue from the conditions of the prophets, messengers, and the truthful ones (siddiqun), from their supplications and their requests, and from their praise for their fear of the Fire and their hope for the Garden. As God, exalted is He, said concerning the chosen servants whom the polytheists worshipped: that they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, as has preceded. And He said concerning His prophets and messengers: ﴿And Zakariya, when he called to his Lord﴾ [al-Anbiya: 89], up to His words: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds, and call upon Us in hope and in fear, and they were humble before Us﴾ [al-Anbiya: 90]. That is, "in hope" of what is with Us, and "in fear" of Our punishment. The pronoun in His words "indeed they" refers, according to the majority of the exegetes (mufassirun), to the prophets mentioned in this surah.

Raghab (hope) and rahab (fear) are, in their view altogether, the hope of mercy and the fear of the Fire.

He, glorified is He, mentioned His servants who are the chosen ones of His creation, and praised them for their best deeds. Among these is their seeking refuge in Him from the Fire. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever adhering. Indeed it is evil as a settlement and residence"﴾ [al-Furqan: 65-66]. He informed of them that they sought a means to Him through their faith that He would save them from the Fire. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who say: "Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 16].

So they made the greatest of their means toward Him the means of faith, and that He would save them from the Fire.

He, exalted is He, informed about the masters of the knowers, the people of understanding, that they used to ask Him for His Garden and seek refuge in Him from His Fire. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for people of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190], through to the end of the verses. There is no disagreement that what was promised through the tongues of His messengers is the Garden that they asked for.

He, exalted is He, said about His intimate friend Ibrahim (ﷺ): ﴿And the one from whom I hope He will forgive my error on the Day of Judgment. My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 82-83], up to His words: ﴿And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected, the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, except one who comes to God with a sound heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 87-89]. So he asked God for the Garden and sought refuge in Him from the Fire, which is the disgrace on the Day of Resurrection.

He, glorified is He, informed us about the Garden: that it was a promise upon Him to be requested (mas'ula), meaning His servants and friends ask Him for it.

The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded his community to ask for him, at the time of answered supplication, after the call to prayer (adhan), the highest station in the Garden. And he informed that whoever asks for it for him, his intercession will be made lawful for him.

Sulaym al-Ansari said to him: "As for me, I ask God for the Garden and seek refuge in Him from the Fire; I do not do well at your murmuring (dandanah), nor the murmuring of Mu'adh." He said: "Mu'adh and I murmur around it."

In the Sahih, in the hadith about the angels who travel and are excellent, who record the deeds of people: God, exalted is He, asks them about His servants, and He is most knowing, blessed and exalted is He. They say: "We came to You from the presence of Your servants who glorify You, declare You free of imperfection, praise You, and extol You." He, mighty and majestic, says: "Have they seen Me?" They say: "No, my Lord, they have not seen You." He, mighty and majestic, says: "How would it be if they saw Me?" They say: "If they saw You, they would be even more intense in extolling You." They say: "My Lord, and they ask You for Your Garden." He says: "Have they seen it?" They say: "No, by Your might, they have not seen it." He says: "How would it be if they saw it?" They say: "If they saw it, they would be even more intense in seeking it." They say: "And they seek refuge in You from the Fire." He, mighty and majestic, says: "Have they seen it?" They say: "No, by Your might, they have not seen it." He says: "How would it be if they saw it?" They say: "If they saw it, they would be even more intense in fleeing from it." He says: "I call you to witness that I have forgiven them, given them what they asked for, and protected them from what they sought refuge from."

The Qur'an and the Sunnah are full of praise for His servants and friends for asking for the Garden and hoping for it, seeking refuge from the Fire, and fearing it.

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Seek refuge in God from the Fire." And he said to one who asked him for companionship in the Garden: "Help me against yourself by increasing prostration."

They said: Working toward seeking the Garden and salvation from the Fire is what the Lawgiver intends from his community, so that they will always remember both and not forget them. And because faith in both is a condition for salvation, and working toward attaining the Garden and salvation from the Fire is the very essence of faith.

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) urged his companions and his community, describing the Garden and making it clear to them so that they would strive for it. He said: "Is there anyone who strives for the Garden? For it, by the Lord of the Ka'ba, is a shining light, a swaying fragrant plant, a beautiful wife, ripe fruit, a lofty palace, and a flowing river..." and the hadith continues. The Companions said: "O Messenger of God, we are those who strive for it." He said: "Say: if God wills."

If we were to mention what is in the Sunnah of his saying: "Whoever does such and such, God will admit him to the Garden," as encouragement to do such deeds, and so that it becomes the motive for knowledge, that would be extremely lengthy. And that is in all deeds.

They said: How then can working for the sake of reward and fear of punishment be considered a flawed motive, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) urges toward it, saying that whoever does such and such, the eight gates of the Garden are opened for him, and whoever "says: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, a palm tree is planted for him in the Garden"? And "whoever clothes a Muslim who is naked, God clothes him with garments of the Garden," and "the one who visits a sick person is in the gathering of fruit of the Garden." The hadith is full of such things. Do you think he urges the believers toward a deficient, flawed aim, and leaves aside the lofty aim, free of the impurities of motives, without urging them toward it?

They said: Also, God, exalted is He, loves that His servants ask Him for His Garden and seek refuge in Him from His Fire, for He loves to be asked. Whoever does not ask Him, He becomes angry with him. The greatest thing asked for is the Garden, and the greatest thing sought refuge from is the Fire.

So working for the pursuit of the Garden is beloved to the Lord and pleasing to Him. And seeking it is servanthood to the Lord. Fulfilling all of His servanthood is better than neglecting part of it.

They said: When the heart is empty of attention to the Garden and the Fire, and of hoping for the one and fleeing from the other, its resolves weaken, its determination becomes feeble, and its motivation diminishes. And the more intense one's pursuit of the Garden and one's work for it, the stronger its motive, the greater its determination, and the more complete its striving. This is a matter known by experience (dhawq).

They said: If this were not something the Lawgiver (al-Shari') desired, He would not have described Paradise to His servants, adorned it for them, and presented it to them. He informed them of the details that their minds can grasp of it, and He described the rest to them in general terms. All of this is to make them long for it and to urge them to strive for it as it should be striven for.

They said: Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has said: ﴿And Allah calls to the Abode of Peace﴾ [Yunus: 25]. This is an urging to answer this call, to hasten to it, and to race to respond.

The truth of the matter is that Paradise (al-Jannah) is not merely the name for trees, fruits, food, drink, dark-eyed companions (al-hur al-'in), rivers, and palaces. Most people err regarding the meaning of Paradise. Paradise is the name for the abode of absolute, complete bliss. Among the greatest of Paradise's bliss is enjoying the sight of the Noble Face of Allah, hearing His speech, and the delight of the eye in nearness to Him and in His pleasure. There is no comparison between the pleasure of what is in it of food, drink, clothing, and forms, and this pleasure, ever. The smallest bit of His pleasure is greater than the gardens and all that is in them of such things, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And the pleasure of Allah is greater﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72].

He mentioned it in indefinite form within an affirmative context, meaning: whatever amount of His pleasure a servant receives, it is greater than Paradise.

A poet said:
"A little from You satisfies me, but
Your little is not called little."

In the sound hadith, the hadith of the vision, it is said: "By Allah, Allah has not given them anything more beloved to them than gazing upon His Face."

In another hadith, that He, glorified is He, "when He manifests Himself to them and they see His Face clearly, they forget what they are in of bliss, and they are absorbed and do not turn to anything else."

There is no doubt that the matter is so. And it is greater than what can occur to the mind or pass through the imagination, especially when those who love succeed there in the company of the Beloved, for a person is with whom he loves. This ruling has no exception; rather it is established both in this world and in the unseen.

What bliss, what delight, what delight of the eye, and what success could approach the bliss of that companionship and its pleasure, and the delight of the eye in it?

Is there anything above the bliss of the delight of the eye in the company of the Beloved, than whom there is nothing greater, more perfect, or more beautiful, that is a delight of the eye at all?

By Allah, this is the knowledge toward which the lovers have strived, and the banner toward which the knowers (al-'arifun) have headed. It is the spirit of the name Paradise and its life. By it Paradise is made good, and upon it it stands.

So how can it be said: "Allah is not worshipped out of desire for His Paradise, nor out of fear of His Fire"?

Likewise the Fire, from which Allah protect us: for its inhabitants there is the torment of being veiled from Allah, His humiliation, His wrath, His displeasure, and distance from Him, which is greater than the burning of the Fire in their bodies and souls. Rather, the burning of this Fire in their hearts is what caused its burning in their bodies, and from it the burning spread to them.

So the seeking of the Prophets, Messengers, truthful ones (al-siddiqin), martyrs, and righteous is Paradise, and their refuge is from the Fire.

Allah is the One sought for help, upon Him is reliance, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah, and Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Guardian.

The aim of these people is that the servant worships his Lord with the true right of servanthood. If a servant asks his master for a wage in return for his service to him, he is foolish and fallen from his master's regard, unless he deserves punishment. For his servanthood requires his service to him. A person serves for wages only when he is not owned in servanthood by the one he serves, either because he is free in himself or because he is the servant of another. As for the creatures, who are truly His servants and His possession in reality, among them there is no one free nor a servant of another; so their service to Him is by the right of servanthood, and therefore their demanding a wage is a departure from pure servanthood.

This is not to be denied absolutely, nor accepted absolutely. It is a matter requiring detail and distinction.

It has already been mentioned at the beginning of this discussion what the ways of people are in this matter, and we explained the path of the people of uprightness (istiqamah).

People in this station are of four categories:

The first: one who neither wants his Lord nor wants His reward. These are truly His enemies, and they are the people of everlasting punishment. Their not wanting His reward is either because they do not believe in it, or because they prefer the immediate over it, even if it entails His displeasure.

The second category: one who wants Him and wants His reward. These are His elite creatures. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 29]. This is His address to the best of the women of the worlds, the wives of His Prophet (ﷺ). Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due striving, while he is a believer, those – their striving will be appreciated﴾ [al-Isra': 19]. So He informed that the appreciated striving is the striving of one who desires the Hereafter. Even more explicit is His saying, addressed to His chosen friends – they being the companions of His Prophet (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with them – on the day of Uhud: ﴿Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152]. So He divided them into these two categories, which have no third.

Someone has erred who says: "Where is the one who desires Allah?" For desiring the Hereafter is an expression for desiring Allah, Exalted, and His reward. Desiring the reward does not contradict desiring Allah.

The third category: one who desires from Allah but does not desire Allah. This one is deficient to the utmost degree. This is the state of the one ignorant of his Lord, who has heard that there is a Paradise and a Fire. There is nothing in his heart but the desire for the created bliss of Paradise, and nothing else ever occurs to his mind. This is also the state of most of the theologians (al-mutakallimun) who deny the vision of Allah, the enjoyment of gazing upon His Face in the Hereafter, hearing His speech, and loving Him, and who denounce those who claim to love Allah. They are the slaves of pure wages. These people do not desire Allah, Exalted.

Among them are those who declare explicitly that desiring Allah is impossible.

They say: "Because desire attaches only to what is temporal (hadith), and the Eternal (qadim) is not desired." These deny the desire for Allah in the extreme. The highest desire in their view is the desire for eating, drinking, marriage, and clothing in Paradise, and what follows from these. These are on one side, and those who said: "We did not worship Him out of desire for His Paradise, nor fleeing from His Fire," are on the other side. These two are opposite extremes, with a distance between them greater than the distance between the two easts. These are among the densest of people in veiling, the coarsest in temperament, the hardest in hearts, and the farthest from the spirit of love and devotion (al-ta'alluh), and from the bliss of spirits and hearts. They denounce the people of love, longing for Allah, and delight in His love, and those who affirm the delight of gazing upon His Face and hearing His speech directly from Him without intermediary.

Those people (the lovers) regard these (the deniers) as human only in form. Their rank in their estimation is close to that of inanimate matter and the brute animal. In their estimation, these are in a thick veil concerning knowledge of their own souls and their perfection, and knowledge of their worshipped One and the secret of their servanthood to Him.

The condition of the two groups is astonishing to whoever comes to know it.

The fourth category – and it is impossible – is one who desires Allah but does not desire from Him. This is the one these people claim to be their goal, and they claim that whoever has not reached it, there is a defect in his journey, and that the knower (al-'arif) arrives at this station: that Allah is his desire and he desires nothing from Him. As is related of Abu Yazid (al-Bistami) that he said: "It was said to me: 'What do you want?' I said: 'I want not to want.'"

In reality this is the very impossibility that is absolutely untenable, by intellect, natural disposition, sense, and law. For desire is among the necessary attributes of the living being. Only the absence of desire occurs to him through being absent from his intellect and senses, such as in intoxication, fainting, and sleep. We do not deny the withdrawal from the desire for other created things that compete with the desire for Him. Is not the possessor of this station desiring nearness to Him, His pleasure, constant watchfulness of Him, and presence with Him? And what desire is above this?

Yes. He has renounced one desire for another desire that is greater and higher than it. Thus he has not departed from desire; he has merely moved from one desire to another, and from one object of desire to another. But his being emptied entirely of the attribute of desire, while his intellect and senses remain present, is impossible.

If someone judges this matter by an overwhelming state of ecstasy (dhawq mustalim) taken from himself, annihilated from its worlds, we do not deny it. But this is a passing state, not permanent, and it is neither the ultimate goal sought by the wayfarers (al-salikin), nor within the capacity of humans, nor something commanded, nor the highest of stations. Rather, one is commanded to acquire its causes.

This is the decisive word on this matter. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 73:

Since jihad is the peak of the hump of Islam and its dome, and the abodes of its people are the highest abodes in Paradise, just as they have elevation in this world, so they are the highest in this world and the Hereafter, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at its highest peak. He mastered all of its types, so he strove for Allah with the rightful striving, with the heart, the inner self, the call, the explanation, the sword, and the spear. His hours were devoted to jihad with his heart, his tongue, and his hand. For this reason he was the most exalted of all the worlds in remembrance, and the greatest of them in rank with Allah.

Allah the Exalted commanded him to engage in jihad from the time of his mission, and said: ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent a warner to every town. So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan: 52]. This is a Meccan surah in which He commanded the striving against the disbelievers through proof, explanation, and conveying the Qur'an. Likewise, the jihad against the hypocrites is only by conveying the proof; otherwise they are under the subjugation of the people of Islam. The Exalted said: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾.

The jihad against the hypocrites is more difficult than the jihad against the disbelievers. It is the jihad of the elite of the Ummah and the heirs of the Messengers. Those who carry it out are few in the world, and those who participate in it and assist in it, even if they are fewer in number, are the greatest in rank with Allah.

Since among the best forms of jihad is speaking the truth in the face of strong opposition, such as speaking it in the presence of one whose power and harm you fear, the Messengers—may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them—had the greatest share of this, and our Prophet—may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him—had the most complete and perfect jihad of it.

Since the jihad against the enemies of Allah outwardly is a branch of the servant's jihad against his own self for the sake of Allah, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «The mujahid is one who strives against his self in obedience to Allah, and the muhajir is one who abandons what Allah has forbidden», the jihad of the self takes precedence over the jihad against the outward enemy, and is its foundation. For as long as he does not first strive against his self, so that it does what it is commanded and leaves what it is forbidden, and wage war against it for Allah, he cannot undertake the jihad against his outward enemy. How can he undertake jihad against his enemy and gain victory over him, when his enemy that is between his two sides dominates him and holds sway over him, and he has not striven against it or waged war against it for Allah? Rather, he cannot even go out against his enemy until he strives against his own self to go out.

These are two enemies with which the servant is tested in striving, and between them is a third enemy whom he cannot strive against except through striving against it. It stands between them, discouraging the servant from striving against them, weakening him, and causing him to waver. It never ceases to make him imagine the hardships of striving against them, the abandonment of pleasures, the loss of delights and desires. He cannot strive against these two enemies except by striving against this third one. So his jihad is the foundation for the jihad against the other two, and it is Satan. The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾ [Fatir: 6]. The command to take him as an enemy is an alert to exerting one's full effort in fighting and striving against him, as if he were an enemy who never slackens or falls short in making war on the servant, to the count of every breath.

These are three enemies, and the servant is commanded to wage war against them and strive against them. He is afflicted with fighting them in this abode, and they are empowered over him as a trial and test from Allah. Allah gives the servant support, equipment, helpers, and weapons for this jihad, and gives his enemies support, equipment, helpers, and weapons. He tests each party by means of the other, and has made some of them a trial for others, so that He may test their reports and examine who among them takes as ally Him and His Messengers, versus those who take as allies Satan and his party. As the Exalted said: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ [al-Furqan: 20].

The Exalted also said: ﴿That, and if Allah had willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them, but [He wills] to test some of you by means of others﴾ [Muhammad: 4], and said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are patient, and We test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. He gave His servants hearing, sight, intellects, and faculties; He sent down His Books to them, sent His Messengers to them, supported them with His angels, and said to them: ﴿Indeed I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. He commanded them, from among His commands, with what is among the greatest assistance to them in fighting their enemy. He informed them that if they comply with what He commanded them, they will continue to be victorious over His enemy and their enemy. And that if He empowers the enemy over them, it is because of their abandonment of some of what they were commanded and their disobedience to Him. Then He did not despair them or make them lose hope, but commanded them to face their situation anew, tend their wounds, and return to confronting their enemy, whereupon He would grant them victory over him and make them triumph over him. He informed them that He is with those among them who are God-fearing, with the good-doers, with the patient, and with the believers, and that He defends His believing servants against what they cannot defend against themselves.
