Your servants other than me are many, and I have no master other than You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I ask You as the poor man asks, I supplicate to You as the humble, abased one supplicates, and I call upon You as the fearful, distressed one calls, the request of one whose neck is bowed to You, whose nose is rubbed in the dust before You, whose eyes overflow for You, and whose heart is humbled before You."

A poet said:
"O You to whom I flee in what I hope for,
and from whom I seek refuge in what I fear,
People cannot mend a bone that You have broken,
and they cannot break a bone that You have mended."

This and similar are among the marks of accepted repentance. Whoever does not find this in his heart should suspect his repentance and return to correcting it. How difficult true repentance is in reality, and how easy it is with the tongue and in claims! The sincere person has never undertaken anything more difficult for himself than pure, sincere repentance. There is no power and no strength except with Allah.

Most people who keep far from gross sins and filth fall into sins similar to them, or greater, or lesser, and it does not occur to their hearts that these are sins from which they should repent. Thus they have—through belittling the people of major sins and looking down on them, the pride of their acts of worship, their boasting over creation through the tongue of their state, and their inner expectation that people honor them for their acts of obedience, an expectation that is obvious to everyone but themselves, and the consequences of that—what is more hateful to Allah and further from His door for them than the major sins of those others. If Allah sets right one of them through a filth or a major sin that causes him to fall into it, in order to break his self, make him know his worth, humble him, and remove the pride of obedience from his heart, then it is a mercy for him. Just as, when He sets right the people of major sins through sincere repentance and their turning of heart to Him, it is a mercy for them. Otherwise, both are in danger.

**(A subtle point)**
If you were to sell a single moment of your turning towards God, weighed against the whole lifespan of Noah in the kingdom of Qarun, you would still be cheated in the transaction.

**(A benefit: on giving precedence to the souls over the wealth)**
Related to this is another kind of precedence that al-Suhayli did not mention: the precedence of wealth over souls in jihad (striving in the way of God). It occurs in the Noble Qur'an in only one place, the saying of God: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for [the price of] that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed.﴾

In all other places, wealth is mentioned first, such as His saying: ﴿and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives﴾, and His saying: ﴿and strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives﴾, and there are many such instances. So what is the wisdom in putting wealth before the soul elsewhere, and in putting it after the soul in this one place alone?

Al-Suhayli, may God have mercy on him, did not address this.

It is said: Firstly, this is evidence that jihad with wealth is obligatory just as jihad with the self is obligatory. So when the enemy attacks, it becomes obligatory on the able-bodied to go forth themselves; if one is incapable, it becomes obligatory on him to hire someone with his wealth. This is one of the two reports from Imam Ahmad, and the evidence for it is too extensive to be mentioned here.

Whoever reflects on the circumstances of the Prophet ﷺ and his conduct with his Companions, and on how he commanded them to bring out their wealth for jihad, will be certain of the soundness of this view. The point of mentioning wealth first is that this indicates a refutation of the one who imagines that if the incapable person is able to campaign with his wealth, nothing is obligatory upon him. Whenever jihad is mentioned, wealth is mentioned first, so how can it be said that it is not obligatory with wealth? Even if it were said that its obligation through wealth is greater and stronger than its obligation through the self, this view would be more sound than the view of the one who says that it is not obligatory with wealth. This is clear. On this basis, the benefit of its being mentioned first becomes apparent.

A second benefit, on the assumption that it is not obligatory, is that wealth is what the soul loves and what it is enamoured with. The soul gives up its very self to acquire it, takes on dangers, and exposes itself to death in its pursuit. This shows that wealth is its beloved and its object of passion. So God, exalted is He, urged those who love Him and strive in His way to give up what they love and cherish for His good pleasure.

The purpose is that God should be the most beloved thing to them, and that there should be nothing in existence more beloved to them than Him. When they give up what they love for His love, He elevates them to a higher and more perfect rank, which is giving up their selves for Him. This is the utmost love, for a person has nothing more beloved to him than his own self. When someone loves something, he gives up for it what he loves, both his self and his wealth. But when the matter comes to giving up his self, he holds on to it and prefers it over what he loves. This is the predominant pattern, and it is what animal and human nature requires. This is why a man defends his wealth, his family and his children, but when he senses that he is overpowered and that harm is reaching his very life and self, he flees and abandons them. God was not satisfied with this from those who love Him; rather, He commanded them to give Him their selves after they had given Him what they loved.

Furthermore, giving up the self is the last of the stages. A servant gives up his wealth first, in order to protect his self with it. When he has no wealth left, he gives up his self. Therefore, putting wealth before the self in jihad corresponds to the reality.

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾, here mentioning the selves first is better, because they are the thing actually purchased. They are the object of the contract, the commodity which its Lord has taken possession of, and He sought to buy it for Himself, making the price of this contract His good pleasure and His Paradise. So they were the very thing intended by the contract of purchase, and wealth follows them. When the buyer possesses them, he possesses their wealth too, for the servant and what he owns belong to his master, and he has no share in it. The true owner, when he owns the selves, owns their wealth and what is connected to them. Thus, putting the selves before the wealth in this verse is a fitting precedence that cannot be improved upon.

**[Section: On the Lord, exalted is He, offering His commodity, Paradise, to His servants, and the price He asked of them, and the contract of exchange concluded between the believers and their Lord]**

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for [the price of] that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have conducted. And that is the great triumph.﴾

Here, He, glory be to Him, made Paradise the price for the souls and wealth of the believers, such that when they give them up in this cause, they deserve the price. He concluded this contract with them and confirmed it with various kinds of emphasis:

First: He informed them, glory and exaltation be to Him, in the form of a statement emphasised by the particle (*inna*).

Second: He informed them of it in the past tense, which indicates that it has occurred, been established, and settled.

Third: He attributed this contract to Himself, and that He is the One who purchased this item.

Fourth: He informed them that He had promised to deliver this price, a promise He will not break or abandon.

Fifth: He used the expression (*ʿalā*), which denotes obligation, to inform His servants that this is a right incumbent upon Him, a right He has imposed upon Himself.

Sixth: He emphasised it by stating that it is a right incumbent upon Him.

Seventh: He informed them of the source of this promise, that it is in the best of His revealed books, which are the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an.

Eighth: He informed His servants by way of a rhetorical question of denial that no one is truer to His covenant than Him, glory be to Him.

Ninth: He, glory and exaltation be to Him, commanded them to rejoice in this contract and to give one another the good news of it, as one gives good news to someone whose contract has been completed and made binding, such that no option of cancellation remains and nothing arises to dissolve it.

Tenth: He informed them with emphatic assertion that this transaction which they have concluded is the great triumph. Here the word "transaction" (*bayʿ*) means the object sold, which they have taken in exchange for this price, namely Paradise.

His saying ﴿which you have conducted﴾ means: the exchange you have engaged in and the bargain you have struck.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned that this contract, which was concluded and completed for them alone and not for others, is for those who repent from what the worshippers dislike, who praise Him for what they love and what they dislike, and who wander (*al-sāʾihūn*). The word "wandering" (*al-siyāḥa*) has been explained as fasting, as travelling in search of knowledge, as jihad, and as the constant maintenance of obedience. The truth about it is that it is the wandering of the heart in the remembrance of God, in His love, in turning to Him in repentance, and in longing for meeting Him. All the actions mentioned follow from this. For this reason, God, glory be to Him, described the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, whom He would have replaced with better ones had he divorced them, as "wanderers". Their wandering was not jihad, nor travel in search of knowledge, nor perpetual fasting. It was rather the wandering of their hearts in the love of God, in fear of Him, in turning to Him, and in remembering Him.

Reflect on how God, glory be to Him, made repentance and worship a pair: the first is abandoning what is disliked, the second is doing what is loved. He made praise and wandering a pair: the first is praise of Him through the attributes of His perfection and the wandering of the tongue in His most excellent remembrance, the second is the wandering of the heart in His love, remembrance and veneration.

Just as He, glory be to Him, made worship and wandering a pair in describing the wives, so: this is the worship of the body, and this is the worship of the heart.

He also made Islam and faith a pair: the first is outward, and the second is in the heart, as in the Musnad from him ﷺ: "Islam is outward and faith is in the heart."

He made obedience (*qunūt*) and repentance a pair: the first is doing what is loved, and the second is abandoning what is disliked.

He made being a previously married woman (*thayyib*) and a virgin a pair: the former has been ridden, tamed, and had her difficulties made docile, while the latter is a pasture untouched, in which no one has yet grazed.

He made bowing and prostration a pair. He made enjoining good and forbidding evil a pair, and placed the conjunction (*wa*) between them, unlike the previous pairs, to inform that neither of them suffices without the other. He linked this with guarding the limits of God: the first is guarding them within oneself, and the second is commanding others to guard them.

The verse conveys the gravity and nobility of the human soul and the greatness of its value. When the worth of a commodity is hidden from you, look at who the buyer is, look at the price offered for it, and look at the contract of sale that has been carried out through his hand. The commodity is the soul, God, glory be to Him, is its buyer, the price is the gardens of bliss, and the envoy in this contract is the best of His creation from among the angels and the most honoured of them before Him, and the best of mankind and the most honoured of them before Him:

*They have prepared you for a matter which, if you were to grasp it,*
*you would keep your self aloof from grazing with the heedless.*

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever fears sets out at night, and whoever sets out at night reaches the destination. Truly, the commodity of God is precious. Truly, the commodity of God is Paradise." He said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

In the Kitab Sifat al-Jannah of Abu Nu'aym, from the hadith of Aban, from Anas, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "What is the price of Paradise?" He said: "La ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but God)." The witnesses to this hadith are very numerous.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: a Bedouin came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, direct me to a deed which, if I do it, will enter me into Paradise." He said: "Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, pay the obligatory zakat, and fast Ramadan." He said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, I will not add anything to this, nor reduce from it." When he turned away, he ﷺ said: "Whoever would like to look at a man of the people of Paradise, let him look at this one."

In Sahih Muslim, from Jabir, who said: al-Nu'man ibn Qawqal came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, what do you think if I perform the obligatory prayer, avoid the forbidden, and make lawful the lawful, will I enter Paradise?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes."

In Sahih Muslim, from Uthman ibn Affan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but God will enter Paradise."

In Sunan Abi Dawud, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: "Whoever's last words are 'La ilaha illa Allah' will enter Paradise."

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Dhar, may God be pleased with him, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "A visitor from my Lord came to me and informed me, or he said, gave me good news, that whoever of your community dies without associating anything with Him will enter Paradise."
I said: "Even if he commits adultery, and even if he steals?"
He said: "Even if he commits adultery, and even if he steals."

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whoever says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, and that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger and His word which He cast to Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true, and that the Fire is true, God will admit him through whichever of the eight gates of Paradise He wills."
In another wording: "God will admit him into Paradise, whatever deeds he had done."

**(An exhortation)**
Whoever has the splendour of the Hereafter's perfection revealed to him, departure from this world becomes easy for him. When the falcon sees its prey, it forgets the familiar hand.

O feet of patience, bear on; only a little remains.

Remembering the sweetness of union makes the bitterness of striving easy for you.

You already know where the destination is; so hasten towards it and you will be glad.

Abu Yazid said: "I kept driving my soul towards God while it wept, until I drove it to Him while it was laughing."

The lofty aspiration belongs to the one whose owner prepares himself for meeting the Beloved, and sends his provisions ahead before the one who meets him, so that he rejoices upon arrival: ﴿And send ahead for yourselves, and fear God, and know that you will meet Him.﴾

Paradise is satisfied from you with the performance of the obligations, the Fire is averted from you by abandoning sins, and love is not content from you with anything less than giving up the spirit: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives.﴾

With the blood of the lover, union is bought; so who will buy at this price?

**(Section)**
Most of creation has forgotten the reality of their own selves, neglected them, and wasted their share from God. They have sold them cheaply, for a paltry price, in a sale of deception. This becomes apparent to them only at death, and it becomes fully apparent on the Day of Mutual Deception, the day when it becomes clear to the servant that he was cheated in the contract he made for himself in this abode, and in the trade he conducted for his return. Every person trades in this world for his Hereafter.

So the losers, who think themselves the people of profit and gain, have bought the life of this world and their portion and pleasures in it with the Hereafter and their portion in it. They have squandered their good things in their worldly life, enjoyed them, were content with them, were at ease with them, and their striving was to attain them. So they bought, sold, and traded, exchanging the deferred for the immediate, credit for cash, and the absent for the present. They said: "This is prudence," and one of them says:

*Take what you see and leave what you have only heard of.*

How, then, should I sell a present cash object which I see in this abode for a deferred absent one in another abode, other than this one? To this is added the weakness of faith, the strength of the call of desire, the love of the hasty, and imitation of those of one's kind. So most of creation is in this losing trade, concerning which God said of its people: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter. So the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 86] And He said of them: ﴿So their trade did not profit them, nor were they guided.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16] So when the Day of Mutual Deception comes, the loss in this trade becomes evident to them, and souls are torn apart by regret.

As for the profitable, they have sold the perishable for the everlasting, the base for the precious, and the petty for the great. They said: "What is the measure of this world from its beginning to its end, that we should sell our share from God, exalted is He, and the Abode of the Hereafter for it? How can a servant obtain from it in this short time, which in reality is like a dozing dream, having no comparison at all with the abode of permanence?" God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognising one another.﴾ [Yunus: 45]

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what are you concerned with mentioning it? To your Lord is its finality. You are only a warner to those who fear it. It will be as if they had not remained except an evening or a morning of it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42–46]

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿It will be as if they had not remained but an hour of a day, a proclamation.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿He will say: "How many years did you remain on the earth?" They will say: "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count." He will say: "You remained but a little, if only you had known."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112–114]

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The day the trumpet is blown, and We gather the criminals that day, blue-eyed, whispering among themselves: "You remained but ten [days]." We know best what they say when their most careful in conduct says: "You remained but a day."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102–104]

This, then, is the reality of this world at the coming of the Day of Resurrection. When they knew how little they remained in it, and that they had another abode other than this one, the abode of life and the abode of permanence, they saw that the greatest deception is to sell the abode of permanence for the abode of extinction. So they traded the trade of the shrewd, and were not deceived by the trade of the foolish among people. Thus, on the Day of Mutual Deception, the profit of their trade and the measure of what they had bought became clear to them. Everyone in this world is a seller, a buyer, and a trader, and every person goes forth in the morning, then sells his soul, and either frees it or destroys it.

﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for [the price of] that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of God, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than God? So rejoice in your transaction which you have conducted. And that is the great triumph.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111]

This is the first installment of the price of this trade. So trade, O bankrupt ones, and you who cannot afford this price. Here is another price. If you are among the people of this trade, then pay this price:

[Section: On the Obligation of Fighting]

Then after that He made fighting obligatory upon them, but only for those who fight against them, not for those who do not fight them. He said: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 190].

Then He made obligatory upon them the fighting of all the polytheists. It had been forbidden, then permitted, then commanded against those who initiated fighting against them, then commanded against all the polytheists. It is either an individual obligation (fard ʿayn) according to one of the two opinions, or a collective obligation (fard kifaya) according to the well-known view.

The verified position is that the category of jihad is an individual obligation, whether by the heart, by the tongue, by wealth, or by the hand. So every Muslim must strive with one of these kinds.

As for jihad with the self (life), it is a collective obligation. As for jihad with wealth, there are two opinions regarding its obligation. The sound view is that it is obligatory, because the command to strive with wealth and with the self in the Qur'an is equal, as the Exalted said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your selves in the way of Allah; that is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [At-Tawbah: 41]. He linked salvation from the Fire, forgiveness of sins, and entry into Paradise to it, saying: ﴿O you who believe, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your selves. That is better for you, if you only knew. He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great triumph﴾ [As-Saff: 10–12].

He informed them that if they did this, He would give them what they love of victory and a near conquest. He said: ﴿And another favor you love: victory from Allah and an imminent conquest﴾, meaning: for you there is another quality you love in jihad, namely: ﴿victory from Allah and an imminent conquest﴾. And He, glorified is He, informed that He ﴿purchased from the believers their selves and their wealth, for that they will have Paradise﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111], and compensated them with Paradise in exchange. He also informed that this contract and promise He deposited in the best of His books sent down from the heaven, namely the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. Then He confirmed this by informing them that none is more faithful to His covenant than Him, blessed and exalted is He. Then He confirmed it further by commanding them to rejoice in their sale, which they had contracted. Then He informed them that this is the great triumph.

So let the contracting party with his Lord reflect upon this transaction, how great and lofty its worth is. For Allah, mighty and majestic, is the Buyer, and the price is the gardens of bliss, the attainment of His pleasure, and the enjoyment of seeing Him there. The one through whose hand this contract was carried out is the most noble of His messengers and the most honored of them before Him among the angels and mankind. Indeed, a commodity of this status has been prepared for a great matter and a momentous affair:

*They have prepared you for a matter, which, if you were perceptive, you would recognize;*
*So guard yourself from grazing with the herd of the heedless.*

The bridal gift of love and Paradise is the giving of one's self and wealth to their Owner, who purchased them from the believers. So what has the coward, the one who turns away, the bankrupt, to do with bidding for this commodity? By Allah, it has not become cheap for the bankrupt to buy it, nor has it become unsaleable so that the insolvent must sell it on credit. It has been placed up for display in the market of whoever desires it, and its Lord did not accept for it any price less than the surrender of souls. So the idlers held back, and the lovers stood up, each waiting to see who would be fit to make his soul the price. The commodity circulated among them and fell into the hands of *"humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers"* [Al-Ma'idah: 54].

When the claimants of love multiplied, they were required to establish proof for the truth of their claim. If people were given according to their claims, the empty-handed would claim the craft of the skilled. So the claimants varied in their witnesses, and it was said: This claim is not established except with evidence: ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 31].

So all of creation held back, and the followers of the Messenger remained steadfast in his deeds, sayings, guidance, and character, so they were required to show the integrity of their evidence.

It was also said: Integrity is not accepted except with a testimony of good standing: ﴿They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54]. So most claimants of love held back, and the strivers stood up. It was said to them: Indeed, the souls and wealth of the lovers are not theirs, so hand over what the contract was made upon, for ﴿Allah has purchased from the believers their selves and their wealth, for that they will have Paradise﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111], and a contract of sale requires delivery from both sides. When the merchants saw the greatness of the Buyer, the value of the price, the exalted rank of the one through whose hand the contract of sale was carried out, and the magnitude of the book in which this contract was recorded, they knew that this commodity has a value and status that no other commodity has. They saw it as clear loss and gross deception to sell it for a base price, a few counted dirhams, whose pleasure passes away while its consequences and regret remain. Whoever does that is counted among the foolish. So they concluded with the Buyer the pledge of good pleasure (bayʿat al-ridwan), by consent and choice, without any reserved option (khiyar). They said: By Allah, we will neither cancel (iqalah) this sale with You nor seek its cancellation (istiqalah). When the contract was completed and they delivered the goods, it was said to them: Your souls and your wealth have now become Ours. And now, We have returned them to you, more than they were, and multiplied your wealth along with them. ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 169]. We did not buy from you your souls and wealth seeking profit over you; rather, so that the effect of generosity and bounty might appear in accepting the defective and giving for it the most exalted price. Then We combined for you the price and the purchased item.

Reflect on the story of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, when he sold his camel to the Prophet (ﷺ), then the Prophet paid him its price in full and added to it, and returned the camel to him. Jabir's father had been killed with the Prophet (ﷺ) at the Battle of Uhud. So this act reminded him of the condition of his father with Allah, and he informed him that "Allah gave him life and spoke to him directly, saying: O My servant, wish of Me."

So glorified is He whose generosity and bounty are too vast for the knowledge of creation to encompass. He gave the commodity and gave the price, and enabled the completion of the contract. He accepted the purchased item despite its defect, and gave for it the most exalted price. He purchased His servant from himself with His own wealth, combined for him the price and the purchased item, praised him, and commended him for this contract. He, glorified is He, is the One who enabled him to it and willed it from him.

*So welcome, if you have resolve, for the yearning driver has urged you, so fold up the stages.*
*And say to the caller of their love and pleasure, when he calls: "At your service," a thousand times over.*
*Do not look at the ruins without them, for if you look at the ruins, they will become barriers.*
*And do not wait for a companion who sits idle on the journey; leave him, for longing is enough to carry you.*
*Take provision from them for your journey to them, and travel on the path of guidance and love, and you will arrive as one who reaches.*
*Revive their memory as your camel's saddle when your mount draws near, for remembrance will return you as one who works.*
*And if you fear weariness, say to her: Ahead of you is the watering place of union, so seek the watering places.*
*And take a brand from their light and travel with it, for their light guides you, not torches.*
*And hasten to the valley of the arak tree and say it there; perhaps you will see them there, if you are speaking.*
*And if not, then in Nuʿman, with me, is one who knows the beloved; so seek them, if you are asking.*
*And if not, then in the gathering on its night; if you miss it, then Mina. Woe to him who was heedless.*
*And hasten to the gardens of Eden, for they are your first abodes, where you had once dwelt.*
*But the enemies captivated you on account of this, and you stood at the ruins weeping over the dwellings.*
*And hasten to the Day of Increase in the Garden of Eternity, so give your soul if you are one who gives.*
*So leave them as worn-out traces, for in them there is no resting place, and pass beyond them, for they are not dwellings.*
*Traces effaced, people frequent them; how many were slain in them, and how many killers of these people in them.*
*And take a turn away from them, on the path which the caravan of the beloved traversed, inhabited.*
*And say, "Help me, O soul, with patience for an hour, for at the meeting this toil will become a thing that passes."*
*For it is but an hour, then it passes, and the one of sorrows becomes joyful and triumphant.*

The one who calls to Allah and to the Abode of Peace has stirred noble souls and lofty resolves. He has made the caller of faith audible to whoever has an attentive ear, and Allah has made audible to whoever is alive. The sound moved him toward the dwellings of the righteous, and drove him onward on the path of his journey. His saddle came to rest only at the abode of permanence. He said: "Allah has undertaken for whoever goes forth in His way, who is moved only by faith in Me and belief in My messengers, that I will return him with whatever reward or spoils he has obtained, or I will admit him to Paradise. Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not have stayed behind any expedition, and I would love to be killed in the way of Allah, then brought to life, then killed, then brought to life, then killed."

And he said: "The likeness of the one who strives in the way of Allah is like the likeness of one who fasts, stands in prayer, and is devoutly obedient to the signs of Allah, never slackening in fasting or prayer, until the one who strives in the way of Allah returns. And Allah guarantees for the one who strives in His way that He will either take his soul and admit him to Paradise, or return him safe with reward or spoils."

And he said: "A morning or an evening in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it."

And he said, relating from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Whichever of My servants goes forth striving in My way, seeking My pleasure, I guarantee for him that if I return him, I will return him with whatever reward or spoils he has obtained, and if I take his soul, I will forgive him, have mercy on him, and admit him to Paradise."

And he said: "Strive in the way of Allah, for jihad in the way of Allah is a gate of the gates of Paradise, by which Allah saves from distress and grief."

And he said: "I am a guarantor, and the guarantor is the surety, for whoever believes in me, submits, and emigrates: a house in the outskirts of Paradise, and a house in the middle of Paradise. And I am a guarantor for whoever believes in me, submits, and strives in the way of Allah: a house in the outskirts of Paradise, a house in the middle of Paradise, and a house in the highest chambers of Paradise. Whoever does that leaves no good sought and no evil fled from; he dies wherever he wishes to die."

And he said: "Whoever fights in the way of Allah, even for the interval between two milkings of a she-camel (fuwaq naqa), for him Paradise is obligatory."

And he said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels which Allah has prepared for those who strive in the way of Allah; between each two levels is as the distance between heaven and earth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth."

He said to Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him): "Whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger, Paradise is obligatory for him." Abu Sa'id was amazed by it and said: "Repeat it to me, O Messenger of Allah." So he did, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And another, by which Allah raises the servant one hundred levels in Paradise, between each two levels as the distance between heaven and earth." He said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah."

And he said: "Whoever spends a pair (of anything) in the way of Allah, the keepers of the gates of Paradise will call him, each keeper of a gate: O so-and-so, come here! So whoever is among the people of prayer will be called from the gate of prayer; whoever is among the people of jihad will be called from the gate of jihad; whoever is among the people of charity will be called from the gate of charity; and whoever is among the people of fasting will be called from the gate of ar-Rayyan." Abu Bakr said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah. There is no harm for one who is called from those gates; but will anyone be called from all of those gates?" He said: "Yes, and I hope you will be among them."

And he said: "Whoever spends an excessive amount (nafaqah fadilah) in the way of Allah, it is multiplied seven hundredfold. Whoever spends on himself and his family, visits a sick person, or removes harm from the road, then the good deed is multiplied tenfold. Fasting is a shield as long as one does not tear it, and whoever Allah tests in his body, it is an expiation for him."

Ibn Majah also related from him (ﷺ): "Whoever sends money for the sake of Allah and remains in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham. Whoever fights in the way of Allah himself and spends in that cause, for him is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And Allah multiplies [the reward] for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261].

He also said: "Whoever helps a warrior in the way of Allah, or a debtor in his debt, or a mukatab (a slave seeking to buy his freedom) in his manumission, Allah will shade him in His shade on a Day when there is no shade but His shade."

He also said: "Whoever has his feet covered in dust in the way of Allah, Allah forbids him to the Fire."

He also said: "Stinginess and faith do not combine in the heart of one man, and dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell do not combine on the face of a servant." In another wording: "in the heart of a servant"; in another: "in the belly of a man"; in another: "in the nostrils of a Muslim."

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, related: "Whoever has his feet covered in dust in the way of Allah for an hour of a day, those two feet are forbidden to the Fire."

It is also mentioned from him that he said: "Allah does not gather in the belly of a man dust in the way of Allah and the smoke of Hell. Whoever has his feet covered in dust in the way of Allah, Allah forbids his whole body to the Fire. Whoever fasts a day in the way of Allah, Allah keeps the Fire away from him a distance of a thousand years' travel for a rider who hastens. Whoever is wounded in the way of Allah is sealed with the seal of the martyrs; for him there will be a light on the Day of Resurrection, its color the color of saffron and its scent the scent of musk, by which the first and the last will recognize him, and they will say: 'So-and-so bears the seal of the martyrs.' Whoever fights in the way of Allah for the duration of a she-camel's milking-pause, Paradise is obligatory for him."

Ibn Majah related from him: "Whoever goes out in the way of Allah in the morning or evening journey, for him there will be musk on the Day of Resurrection equal to the dust that touched him."

Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, related from him: "No dust of the way of Allah (rahaj) mingles with the heart of a man except that Allah forbids the Fire to him."

He also said: "A day of ribat (frontier guard duty) in the way of Allah is better than the world and what is in it."

He also said: "A day and night of ribat is better than a month of fasting and its night prayers. If he dies, his deeds that he used to do continue for him, his provision is continued for him, and he is safe from the tester (al-fattan)."

He also said: "Every dead person's deeds are sealed except one who dies while on ribat in the way of Allah; his deeds continue to grow for him until the Day of Resurrection, and he is secured from the trial of the grave."

He also said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than a thousand days elsewhere."

Ibn Majah related from him: "Whoever stands ribat for a night in the way of Allah, for him it is like a thousand nights of fasting and prayer."

He also said: "The standing of one of you in the way of Allah is better than the worship of one of you in his family for sixty years. Do you not love that Allah forgive you and you enter Paradise? Strive in the way of Allah; whoever fights in the way of Allah for the duration of a she-camel's milking-pause, Paradise is obligatory for him."

Ahmad related from him: "Whoever stands ribat in any of the coasts of the Muslims for three days, it suffices for him as a year of ribat."

It is also mentioned from him: "The guarding of one night in the way of Allah is better than a thousand nights whose nights are spent in prayer and whose days are spent in fasting."

He also said: "The Fire is forbidden to an eye that wept or shed tears out of fear of Allah, and the Fire is forbidden to an eye that stayed awake in the way of Allah."

Ahmad related from him: "Whoever guards behind the Muslims in the way of Allah, voluntarily, not taken by any ruler, will not see the Fire with his eyes except for the fulfillment of an oath, for Allah says: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]."

And he said to a man who guarded the Muslims for a night during their journey, from its beginning until morning, on the back of his horse, not dismounting except for prayer or to relieve himself: "You have made it obligatory (for yourself); there is no blame on you if you do no further deed after it."

He also said: "Whoever reaches (the enemy) with an arrow in the way of Allah, for him there is a degree in Paradise."

He also said: "Whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah, it is equal to freeing a slave, and whoever turns gray (in hair) in the way of Allah, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." In al-Nasa'i's narration, the degree is explained as a hundred years.

He also said: "Indeed Allah admits through a single arrow three into Paradise: its maker who seeks reward in making it, the one who supplies it, and the one who shoots it. Shoot and ride, but that you shoot is more beloved to me than that you ride. Everything a man amuses himself with is vain, except his shooting with his bow, his training of his horse, and his playing with his wife. Whoever Allah has taught archery and then abandons it out of disinterest, it is a blessing he has disbelieved." Narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan. In Ibn Majah: "Whoever learns archery and then abandons it has disobeyed me."

Ahmad related from him that a man said to him: "Advise me." He said: "I advise you to have taqwa (God-consciousness) of Allah, for it is the head of everything. Hold to jihad, for it is the monasticism of Islam. Hold to the remembrance of Allah and the recitation of the Qur'an, for it is your spirit in the heavens and a remembrance of you on earth."

He also said: "The peak of the hump of Islam is jihad."

He also said: "Three have a right upon Allah to help them: the warrior in the way of Allah, the mukatab who wishes to pay (his freedom), and the one who marries seeking chastity."

He also said: "Whoever dies without having fought, and without having ever resolved to do so in his soul, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy."

Abu Dawud related from him: "Whoever does not fight, or does not equip a warrior, or does not look after the family of a warrior with goodness, Allah will strike him with a calamity before the Day of Resurrection."

He also said: "When people grudge the dinar and the dirham, deal in 'inah (a form of usurious sale), follow the tails of cows, and abandon jihad in the way of Allah, Allah will send down a calamity upon them, and He will not lift it from them until they return to their religion."

Ibn Majah related from him: "Whoever meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic, having no trace in the way of Allah, meets Allah with a breach in him."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ [al-Baqarah: 195]. Abu Ayyub al-Ansari interpreted "throwing oneself into destruction" as abandoning jihad. And it is authentically related from him (ﷺ): "Indeed the gates of Paradise are under the shades of swords."

And it is authentically related from him: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah."

And it is authentically related from him: "Indeed the Fire will be kindled first with the scholar, the spender, and the one slain in jihad, if they did that so that it would be said."

And it is authentically related from him: "Whoever strives seeking the goods of this world, there is no reward for him."

And it is authentically related from him that he said to Abdullah ibn Amr: "If you fight patiently seeking reward, Allah will raise you patiently seeking reward; and if you fight showing off and seeking abundance, Allah will raise you showing off and seeking abundance. O Abdullah ibn Amr, in whatever manner you fight or are killed, Allah will raise you in that state."

(Warning)

O dear one, beware the insight of the God-fearing, for he sees the nakedness of your deed from behind a veil.

Beware the insight of the believer. Glory be to Allah: in the self is the pride of Iblis, the envy of Qabil, the arrogance of 'Ad, the tyranny of Thamud, the audacity of Nimrod, the haughtiness of Pharaoh, the insolence of Qarun, the impudence of Haman, the desire of Balaam, the tricks of the people of the Sabbath, the rebelliousness of al-Walid, and the ignorance of Abu Jahl.

And in it are the traits of animals: the greed of the crow, the gluttony of the dog, the vanity of the peacock, the baseness of the dung beetle, the disobedience of the lizard, the spite of the camel, the pouncing of the leopard, the roar of the lion, the wantonness of the mouse, the venom of the snake, the play of the monkey, the hoarding of the ant, the cunning of the fox, the flightiness of the moth, and the sleep of the hyena. However, discipline and striving remove all this. Whoever is carried away by his nature belongs to this army, and his merchandise is not fit for the contract of: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their selves﴾.

What He purchased is only a commodity that faith has refined, so it passed from its nature to a city whose inhabitants are ﴿the repentant, the worshippers﴾.

Deliver the goods before they perish in your hand, for the buyer will not accept them.

The buyer has known the defect of the commodity before buying it, so deliver it and you will have security from its return.

The value of a commodity is known by the value of its buyer, the price offered for it, and the one who advertises it. So if the buyer is great, the price precious, and the advertiser noble, the commodity is precious.

O you who sell your self in a sale of humiliation, if you could reclaim that sale before it passes, you would not be disappointed.

And a seller of a pleasant life that has no worth, for a fleeting life of pains that is plundered.

You have been cheated, by Allah, a gross cheating, and on the Day of Mutual Cheating you will meet the utmost of the defeat.

And one who comes to the pure life, all of which is turbid; before you is the watering-place, truly, not a lie.

And one who gathers firewood in the dark night, standing ready for every calamity that brings near destruction.

You hope for healing with eyes in which is sickness; have you ever heard of a cure that came from destruction?

And one who spends himself after the worst of them, the pure one who is stripped of his beauty by filth.

And one who gives away himself, from one like this, in folly; had you known the worth of the self, you would not have given it away.

Youth has passed, and playfulness has not passed; your time has been wasted between amusement and play.

And the sun of your life has come near to setting, while the shade on the eastern horizon has not set.

He who strove has attained union, and the darkness of night and the clouds have cleared from his horizon.

How long this delay, when the world has departed and the messengers of your Lord have come to you in search.

What is in the abodes, when the caravans of the one you love have departed, for the lover is no pleasure or desire.

So lay your cheek on that dust, and say what the companion of longings and ages said:

"What is the abode of Mayya, surrounded and visited by Ghaylan, more desirable to him than your ruined abode?

Abodes he used to love and be familiar with, in the days when union was near at hand.

Nor the cheeks, even if they bled with crimson, are more desirable to my eye than your ruined abode.

And whenever those abodes are revealed to him, he yearns for them as water flows downhill.

I revive for him longing, remembering the covenants with them; if the heart were called to forgetting, it would not respond.

This, and how many a dwelling on earth he loves, and he has no desire for any other in all time.

In the tents there is no brother, worthy and sincere, who, if I confide to him some matter of love, will keep my secret; so go away.

And I travel by night in the darkness, guided by the fragrance of perfume, not by aloes wood or firewood.

Every coward and weakling has returned, and the one who fights himself does not leave you in the battle.

Take for yourself a light by which you will be guided on the Day when lights are distributed according to rank.

If my patience demands that my compassion be an obligation, because of the evil of my condition, and my body is loosened by the wasting disease.

I have given you my spirit, asking for no price for it except your pleasure, and that is the only price.

I sigh at the edges of the day in longing, and at night desire calls me, and I respond.

And if there must be love, then whoever is incapable of love should love only the beautiful.

If what I strive for were a hasty life, its little part would have sufficed me of what I am in.

But I aspire to an everlasting kingdom, so alas, if I do not meet it."

Mankind is of two kinds: a penitent (tā'ib) and a wrongdoer (ẓālim), and nothing else. As for the penitents, they are ﴿those who worship, who praise, who travel (in the cause of God), who bow, who prostrate, who enjoin what is right, and who forbid what is wrong, and who guard the limits of God﴾ [al-Tawba: 112].

Guarding the limits of God is part of repentance (tawba), and repentance is the sum of all these matters. He was called a penitent (tā'ib) because he returns (rujū') to God's command from His prohibition, and to His obedience from His disobedience, as has already been explained.

Thus repentance is the very reality of the religion of Islam, and the whole of the religion is included within the designation of repentance. For this reason the penitent deserves to be the beloved of God, for God loves the penitent (al-tawwābīn) and loves those who purify themselves (al-mutaṭahhirīn). God only loves the one who does what He commanded and abstains from what He forbade.

[Section: Discussion of (wāw al-thamāniya) – the "wāw of eight"]

Their claim that the wāw (conjunction) comes to denote eight has no sound proof behind it.

They have mentioned this in several places, so we will discuss them one by one:

The first place: the words of the Exalted: ﴿the penitents, the worshippers, the praisers, the travellers, the bowers, the prostrators, those who enjoin what is right and those who forbid what is wrong﴾

It has been said that the wāw in ﴿and those who forbid﴾ is the wāw of eight, because it comes after the seven attributes have been completed.

They have mentioned other explanations for the verse:

Among them: that this is part of the variety of expression (tafannun fi al-kalām), that one part is joined by conjunction and another part is left unjoined.

Among them: that the attributes preceding these two are necessary attributes tied to the agent, whereas these two attributes are transitive and tied to others, so they are separated from what precedes them by conjunction.

Among them: that the intent is to alert that those described by the preceding attributes are the ones who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

All these answers are unsound.

The best that can be said about this: when attributes are mentioned in a context of enumeration, sometimes a conjunction is placed between them because each is distinct in itself, and to indicate that each attribute is to be mentioned on its own.

And sometimes no conjunction is placed between them, because their subject is one and they are inseparable in themselves, and to indicate that in their inseparability they are like a single attribute.

And sometimes the conjunction is placed between some of them and omitted between others, according to these two situations. If the context is one of enumerating attributes without regard to joining or separating, it is good to drop the conjunction.

If the intent is to join the attributes, or to alert to their distinctness, it is good to insert the conjunction.

An example of the first: ﴿the penitents, the worshippers, the praisers﴾, and His saying: ﴿Muslim women, believing women, obedient women, penitent women﴾.

An example of the second is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward﴾.

Consider how both types came together in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book from God, the Mighty, the Knowing, Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty﴾.

Here the wāw is used in the first two attributes and omitted in the last two, because forgiveness of sin and acceptance of repentance might be thought to function as one attribute due to their inseparability, for one who forgives sin would accept repentance.

So joining one to the other shows that they are two distinct acts and two different concepts, each with its own wisdom: one relates to wrongdoing and turning away, which is forgiveness; the other relates to good conduct and turning toward God and returning to Him, which is repentance. Thus that good deed is accepted and that bad deed is forgiven. The joining here is good because of this clear distinction, and whenever the distinction is clearer, the conjunction is better. For this reason the conjunction appears in ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward﴾ and is omitted in ﴿the King, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian﴾.

And His saying: ﴿the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner﴾.

As for ﴿Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty﴾, the conjunction is omitted between them for a wondrous purpose, which is to indicate that these two matters are gathered in His essence, glory be to Him: while He is severe in punishment, He is also the Possessor of bounty, and His bounty does not contradict the severity of His punishment, rather both are combined in Him. This differs from the First and the Last, for priority does not coexist with posteriority. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ explained them by saying:

"You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You."

So His priority is His eternity (azaliyya) and His posteriority is His everlastingness (abadiyya).

If you say: what do you make of His saying ﴿and the Outward and the Inward﴾? His outwardness is established alongside His inwardness, so both outwardness and inwardness are combined in His case. The Prophet ﷺ explained "the Outward" as the One above whom there is nothing, and "the Inward" as the One beneath whom there is nothing. Does this exaltedness and aboveness not coexist with this nearness, proximity and encompassing?

I say: this is a good question. What makes the conjunction appropriate here is that these attributes are opposites, mutually contrasting, and the second of them is conjoined to the first because of the opposition between them. The two latter attributes are like the two former in opposition, and the relation of the Inward to the Outward is like the relation of the Last to the First.

Just as the conjunction is good between the first two, it is good between the latter two. Having understood this, the verse under discussion becomes clear through what we have mentioned regarding the meaning of conjoining and not conjoining. For every attribute not conjoined to what precedes it indicates that in their collectivity they are like a single attribute of a single subject, so no conjunction is needed. But when the enjoining of what is right and the forbidding of what is wrong were mentioned, and they are mutually entailing and derived from one root, the conjunction was appropriate, to make clear that each of them stands on its own and must be specifically intended, not satisfied by the presence of the other: rather, one must clearly enjoin what is right and clearly forbid what is wrong. Furthermore, the conjunction here is appropriate because of the opposition mentioned: since enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong are opposites, one seeking the bringing into existence and the other seeking the removal, they are like two distinct, opposed kinds, and the conjunction is therefore appropriate.

The second place: the words of the Exalted: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submissive, faithful﴾ to His saying: ﴿previously married and virgins﴾

It was said that this is the wāw of eight, because it comes after the seventh attribute. This is not so; the presence of the wāw here is necessary, because the attributes preceding it are intended to be combined in the women, whereas the two attributes of virginity and previous marriage cannot be combined, so the conjunction is necessary, since the intent is that He will give him both types: previously married women and virgins.

The third place: the words of the Exalted: ﴿They will say: "They were three, their fourth was their dog." And they will say: "They were five, their sixth was their dog," conjecturing about the unseen. And they will say: "They were seven, and their eighth was their dog."﴾

It was said that the intent of the wāw here is for the sake of the eight. This admits of two possibilities: first, this; and second, that the wāw here indicates the completion of their statement at their saying "seven," and then the phrase "and their eighth was their dog" begins, which entails affirming their saying "seven," as when someone says to you, "Zayd is a jurist," and you reply, "and a grammarian." This is the view preferred by al-Suhayli, and the discussion of it has already passed, and that this only holds if the phrase "and their eighth was their dog" is not part of what is reported by the speech; the apparent meaning is contrary to this, and God knows best.

The fourth place: the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to the Garden in groups, until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾

The wāw was used because the gates of Paradise are eight, and for the Fire He said ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾ without the wāw, because they are seven. This is extremely far-fetched; the wording contains no indication of eight such that the wāw would enter for its sake. Rather, this is an instance of omitting the response (ḥadhf al-jawāb) for a wondrous purpose, which is that the opening of the gates of Hell occurs upon the arrival of its people, so they are opened in their faces, because that is more emphatic in the surprise of what is disliked. As for Paradise, since it is the abode of honour, which is God's banquet, and since the generous, when he invites his guests to his home, opens its doors for them and then summons them to it with doors already open, the conjunctive wāw is used here, indicating that they arrived after its gates had been opened. The response is omitted to magnify its importance and to exalt its status, in keeping with their customary omission of responses.

We have elaborated on this at length earlier, and God knows best.

[Section: The Sixth Level — the level of general clarification (al-bayan al-'amm)]

This is the clarifying of the truth and its distinction from falsehood through its proofs, its witnesses and its signs, to the extent that it becomes witnessed by the heart, as the eye witnesses visible things.

This level is the proof of Allah against His creation. He does not punish anyone, nor leave anyone astray, except after it has reached them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah would not mislead a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid.﴾

This misguidance is a punishment from Him to them, when He has made things clear to them and they have not accepted what He made clear to them, nor acted upon it. So He punishes them by leading them astray from guidance. Allah the Glorified never led anyone astray except after this clarification.

When you know this, you will know the secret of divine decree (al-qadar), many doubts and dubious claims on this subject will disappear, and you will know the wisdom of Allah in misguiding whomever of His servants He misguides. The Qur'an states this explicitly in more than one place, such as His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], and ﴿and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped," but Allah has sealed them for their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155]. The first is disbelief of obstinacy ('inad), and the second is disbelief of sealing (tab'). And His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. So He punished them for abandoning belief in it when they were certain of it and had verified it, by turning their hearts and their eyes so that they were not guided to it.

So reflect upon this point with true reflection, for it is a great point.

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ [Fussilat: 17]. This is guidance after clarification and indication, and it is a condition, not a cause. For if it is not accompanied by another guidance after it, the perfection of guidance is not achieved through it, and this is the guidance of success (tawfiq) and inspiration (ilham).

This clarification is of two kinds: clarification through the recited, heard signs, and clarification through the witnessed, visible signs. Both are proofs and signs of the Oneness of Allah, His names, His attributes and His perfection, and of the truthfulness of what His messengers reported about Him. For this reason He calls His servants, through His recited signs, to reflect upon His witnessed signs, and urges them to ponder both these and those. This clarification is what the messengers were sent with, and it was entrusted to them and to the scholars after them. After that, Allah misguides whomever He wills. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, to make things clear to them. Then Allah misguides whomever He wills and guides whomever He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Ibrahim: 4]. So the messengers clarify, and it is Allah who misguides whomever He wills and guides whomever He wills, by His might and His wisdom.

(Faʾida)
Repentance (tawba) is the first of the stations (maqamat) and it is also the last; rather, it accompanies every station. For this reason Allah the Exalted made it the last of the stations of His elect. Allah the Exalted said, concerning the Battle of Tabuk, which was the last of the campaigns in which they crossed the valleys, the beginnings, the states and the endings: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a band of them had nearly swerved; then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾
So He made repentance both the beginning and the end of their affair.

(Fasl)
Know now that repentance is the final goal of every knower (ʿarif), and the ultimate aim of every wayfarer (salik). Just as it is a beginning, it is also an end, and the need for it at the end is greater than the need for it at the beginning; rather, at the end it is a matter of absolute necessity.

Listen now to what Allah addressed to His Messenger at the last of the affair, at the point of the end, and how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, at the end of his life, at his most intense and frequent in seeking forgiveness (istighfar). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a band of them had nearly swerved; then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾ [al-Tawba: 117]

This was revealed by Allah, glorified is He, after the Battle of Tabuk, which was the last campaign that he (ﷺ) himself undertook. Allah, glorified is He, made His turning to them a thanks for what had preceded of those deeds and that struggle (jihad). And He said, at the end of what He revealed to His Messenger: ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in multitudes, then glorify the praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ [al-Nasr: 1-3]

In the Sahih it is reported that he (ﷺ) did not pray any prayer, after this surah was revealed to him, except that he said in it: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me." This was at the end of his affair, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. For this reason the scholars among the Companions, such as ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them, understood from it that the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) term (ajal) had been made known to him by Allah, so He commanded him to seek forgiveness at the end of his states and the last of his affair, in accordance with his station and state (ﷺ). The last thing heard from his speech when he came to his Lord was: "O Allah, forgive me, and join me with the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-Aʿla)." He (ﷺ) would also conclude every righteous act with seeking forgiveness, such as fasting, prayer, Hajj and jihad. When he finished from it and came in sight of Madinah, he would say: "Returning, repenting, praising our Lord." He also legislated that a gathering be concluded with seeking forgiveness, even if it was a gathering of goodness and obedience, and he legislated that the servant conclude the deeds of his day with seeking forgiveness, so he says upon sleeping: "I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and I turn to Him in repentance," and that he sleep upon the "master of forgiveness" (sayyid al-istighfar).

The one who knows Allah, His names, attributes and rights, knows that the servant is most in need of repentance at his end, and that he is more in need of repentance than of annihilation (fana'), union (ittisal), gathering of witnessings (jamʿ al-shawahid), gathering of existence (jamʿ al-wujud), and gathering of the eye (jamʿ al-ʿayn). How could these be the highest stations of the wayfarers and the ultimate goal of those brought near, when no mention of them has come in the Qur'an or the Sunnah, and only a rare few of people know them, and most of them cannot conceive them except with difficulty and hardship? Even if most of creation heard them, they would not understand them, nor know their meaning except through translation! So where, in the Book of Allah, or the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), or the words of the Companions, whose relation to the knowledge of those after them is like the relation of their virtue, religion and struggle to theirs, is there anything that indicates this or points to it?

(Faʾida)
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a band of them had nearly swerved; then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾

This is among the greatest things that make the servant aware of the worth of repentance and its virtue with Allah, and that it is the ultimate perfection of the believer. For He, glorified is He, gave them this perfection after the last of the campaigns, after they had fulfilled their vow and offered their souls, their wealth and their homes for Allah, and the final outcome of their affair was that He turned to them. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) made the day of Kaʿb's repentance the best day that had passed over him since his mother bore him until that day. None recognizes this as it truly deserves except one who knows Allah, knows His rights over him, knows what is befitting of his servitude to Him, knows himself, its attributes and its actions, and knows that what he has accomplished of servitude in relation to his Lord's right over him is like a drop in an ocean, and that is if it is free from outward and inward blemishes. Glory be to Him, whom nothing contains of His servants except His pardon, His forgiveness, and His covering them with His forgiveness and mercy. There is nothing but that or destruction. If He were to apply His justice and punish the people of His heavens and earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them; and if He shows them mercy, His mercy is better for them than their deeds, and none of them is saved by his deed.

[Fasl: On the meaning of Allah's repeating the word "repentance" (tawba) in the verse]
Consider His repeating His turning to them twice, at the beginning of the verse and at its end. He turned to them first by enabling them to repent, and when they repented He turned to them a second time by accepting it from them. It is He who enabled them to perform it and graciously accepted it from them. So all good is from Him, through Him, for Him and in His hands. He gives to whom He wills out of kindness and bounty, and withholds from whom He wills out of wisdom and justice.

[Fasl: The servant's repentance lies between two repentances from his Lord]
The servant's repentance to Allah is enveloped by a repentance from Allah toward him before it, and a repentance from Him after it. So the servant's repentance is between two repentances from his Lord, a preceding and a following one. He turned to him first by permission, enablement and inspiration; then the servant repented; then Allah turned to him a second time, by acceptance and reward. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a band of them had nearly swerved; then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them, and to the three who were left behind, until, when the earth was confining for them despite its vastness, and their souls confined them, and they thought there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [al-Tawba: 117-118] So He informed, glorified is He, that His turning to them preceded their turning, and that it was what made them penitent. It was thus the cause that necessitated their repentance. This indicates that they did not repent until Allah, exalted is He, turned to them, and a ruling is negated when its cause is negated.

A parallel to this is His guidance to His servant before the servant is guided: he is guided by His guidance, and that guidance necessitates for him another guidance, by which Allah rewards him with guidance upon his guidance, for among the reward of guidance is guidance after it, just as among the punishment of misguidance is misguidance after it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. So He guided them first and they were guided, then He increased them in guidance a second time. The opposite is the case for the people of deviation, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5]. This second causing to deviate is a punishment for them for their deviation.

This aspect belongs to the mystery of His two names, the First and the Last. He is the One who prepares (al-Muʿidd) and the One who supplies (al-Mumidd), and from Him are the cause and the effect. He is the One who seeks refuge from Himself by Himself, as the one with the greatest knowledge of Him said: "And I seek refuge in You from You." The servant is a penitent (tawwab), and Allah is a Penitent (tawwab). The servant's repentance is his return to his master after fleeing; Allah's repentance is of two kinds: permission and enablement, and acceptance and supply.

[Fasl: The beginning and end of repentance]
Repentance has a beginning and an end. Its beginning is the return to Allah by following His straight path, which He established for His servants, leading to His good pleasure, and He commanded them to follow it by His saying: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways﴾ [al-Anʿam: 153]; and by His saying: ﴿And indeed you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Shura: 52]; and by His saying: ﴿And they were guided to good speech, and were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Hajj: 24].

Its end is the return to Him in the Hereafter and the following of His path, which He established leading to His Garden. Whoever returns to Allah in this abode through repentance, returns to Him in the Hereafter with reward. This is one of the interpretations of His saying: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteousness, then indeed he turns to Allah with a (good) return﴾ [al-Furqan: 71]. Al-Baghawi and others said: "He turns to Allah with a return," i.e., he returns to Him after death, a good return, preferred over others. So the first repentance, which is His saying "whoever repents," is a return from shirk, and the second is a return to Allah for recompense and reward.

The second interpretation: the recompense includes the meaning of commands, and the meaning is: whoever resolves upon repentance and wills it, let him make his repentance to Allah alone, sincerely for His face, not for anything else.

The third interpretation: what is meant is the necessary implication of this meaning, which is informing and notifying the penitent of the One to whom he repents and returns. The meaning: let him know to whom his repentance is directed and to whom his return is made, for it is to Allah and not to anyone else.

A parallel to this, according to one of the two interpretations, is His saying: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 67], meaning: know what follows for one who disobeys His commands and does not convey His message.

The fourth interpretation: repentance occurs first through intention and resolve to perform it, then when the resolve becomes strong and firm, he finds in it the act of repentance. The first repentance is by resolve and intention to perform it, and the second is by the very act of repenting and bringing it into being. The meaning: whoever repents to Allah with intention, purpose and resolve, his repentance to Allah is in deed and action. This is similar to his (ﷺ) saying: "Whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's emigration was for a worldly thing he would obtain, or a woman he would marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for."

[Fasl: The meaning of the word "were left behind" (khullifu) in the verse]
As for His saying: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, Kaʿb has explained it correctly: they were left behind from among those who swore oaths to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and offered excuses from among those who stayed behind. So He left these three behind, and deferred their matter apart from them. This was not their staying behind from the campaign, for if that were what was meant, He would have said "takhallafu" (they stayed behind), as He said: ﴿It was not for the people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them to stay behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Tawba: 120]. That is because they stayed behind of their own accord, unlike their being left behind by the command of others who stayed behind, for Allah, glorified is He, is the One who left them behind from them, and they did not stay behind from Him by themselves. And Allah knows best.

(Fasl)
Allah has divided His creation into two categories with no third: penitents and wrongdoers. He said: ﴿And whoever does not repent, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

Likewise He made them two categories: those punished and those penitent. Whoever does not repent is certainly punished. Allah said: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women, and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and believing women﴾.

He commanded all believers, from the first of them to the last, to repent, and none is excepted from this, and He tied their success to it. Allah said: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you may succeed﴾.

Among the blessings He bestowed upon the best of His creation, the most honored by Him, the most obedient to Him and the most fearful of Him, is that He turned to him and to the special ones among his followers. He said: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a band of them had nearly swerved﴾, then He repeated His turning to them, saying: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾ He put His turning to them before the turning to the three who were left behind. And He, glorified is He, informed that the Garden He promised to its people in the Torah and the Gospel is entered by the penitents. He mentioned the general category of penitents first, then singled out the Prophet, the Emigrants and the Helpers, then singled out the three who were left behind. Thereby it is known that all creation is in need of His turning to them, His forgiveness for them and His pardon of them. And Allah the Exalted has said to the master of the children of Adam and the most beloved of His creation to Him: ﴿Allah pardon you (ʿafa Allahu ʿanka)﴾.

This is a report from Him, and He is the most truthful of speakers, or it is a supplication to His Messenger that He pardon him, and it is a request from his own self.

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in his prostration, when he was closest to his Lord:
"I seek refuge in Your good pleasure from Your anger, and I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot enumerate Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself."

He (ﷺ) also said to Aisha, the most obedient of the women of the Ummah, the best of them and the most virtuous, the Truthful one, daughter of the Truthful (Abu Bakr), when she said to him, "O Messenger of Allah, if I should happen upon the Night of Decree, what should I supplicate?" He said: "Say, 'O Allah, You are Forgiving and You love forgiveness, so pardon me.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith that is hasan sahih" (good and authentic).

Because of His love for pardon and repentance, He (glorified is He) created His creatures with attributes, states and conditions that necessitate their repentance to Him, their seeking forgiveness, and their asking for His pardon and forgiveness. Muslim related in his Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you did not sin, Allah would take you away and bring a people who sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah, and He would forgive them."

Allah, the Exalted, loves those who repent, and repentance is among the acts of obedience most beloved to Him. Sufficient proof of His love for it is His great joy at it, as in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost property in a desert.'" In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Masud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His believing servant than a man in a dangerous, desolate land who has his mount with his food and drink on it.
