Allah, the Exalted, loves those who repent, and repentance is among the acts of obedience most beloved to Him. Sufficient proof of His love for it is His great joy at it, as in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. By Allah, Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his lost property in a desert.'" In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Masud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His believing servant than a man in a dangerous, desolate land who has his mount with his food and drink on it. He falls asleep, then wakes to find it gone. He searches for it until thirst overtakes him, then says, 'I will return to the place where I was and sleep until I die.' He lays his head on his forearm to die, then awakes to find his mount beside him with his provisions, food and drink. Allah is more joyful at the repentance of the believing servant than this man is with his mount and provisions."

In Sahih Muslim, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, traced up to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man who loaded his provisions and water-skin on a camel and set out until he reached a desert. A midday rest overtook him, so he dismounted and lay down under a tree, and sleep overcame him. His camel slipped away. He awoke and ran up a hill, then another, then a third, and saw nothing. He returned to the place where he had been, and while he was sitting there, behold, the camel came walking and placed its halter in his hand." So Allah is more joyful at the repentance of the servant than this man at finding his camel.

Consider His love for this act of obedience, which is the root and foundation of all acts of obedience. Whoever claims that any person can dispense with it, and has no need of it, has ignorance of the right of Lordship and the station of servanthood. He diminishes the One he claims to exalt by claiming that He has made the servant independent of repentance, since he has thereby left Him without this great act of obedience, which is among the greatest of acts and the most noble of devotions. He would be saying, "You are not of the people of this act of obedience, and you have no need of it." So he has not measured Allah with His due measure, nor the servant with his due measure. And he has made some of His servants independent of Allah's forgiveness, pardon and their repentance to Him, claiming that they have no need of their Lord in this.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more joyful at the repentance of His servant when he repents than one of you, a man who was on his mount in a desert wasteland, and it ran off from him with his food and drink on it. He despaired of it, came to a tree and lay down, having given up on his mount. While he was in that state, behold, it was standing right beside him. Then, from the intensity of his joy, he said, 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord!' He erred from the intensity of his joy."

The most complete of creation are the most complete in repentance and the most abundant in seeking forgiveness.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "By Allah, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him more than seventy times a day."

When Abu Hurayra heard this from the Prophet (ﷺ), he would say what Imam Ahmad narrated from him in the Kitab al-Zuhd (Book of Asceticism): "Indeed I seek Allah's forgiveness in a day and a night twelve thousand times, according to the measure of my blood-money (diyya)."

Then he (the narrator) related it through another route, and he said: "according to the measure of his sin."

Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Rashid informed us, from Makhul, from a man, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "I never sat with anyone who sought forgiveness more than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." The man said: "And I never sat with anyone who sought forgiveness more than Abu Hurayra."

In Sahih Muslim, from al-Aghar al-Muzani, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed my heart is veiled, and I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day." In the Sunan and Musnad (collections of hadith), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: "We would count for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in a single sitting, a hundred times: 'My Lord, forgive me and turn to me, You are the Ever-Returning, the Most Merciful.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hadith that is hasan sahih."

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Burda, who said: "I sat with an elder of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the mosque of Kufa, and he related to me, saying: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)' or he said, 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, repent to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and seek His forgiveness, for I turn to Allah and seek His forgiveness a hundred times every day."'"

Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murra, who said: I heard Abu Burda say: I heard al-Aghar relate to Ibn Umar that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O people, repent to your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, for I repent to Him a hundred times a day."

Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama informed us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Aisha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, make me of those who, when they do good, rejoice, and when they do evil, seek forgiveness."

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to supplicate with this supplication: "O Allah, forgive me my error and my ignorance, my excess in my affairs, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and the One who delays, and You are over all things Powerful."

The reality of the matter is that the servant is needy of Allah in every respect and in every consideration. He is needy of Him by virtue of His Lordship over him, His kindness to him, His managing of his welfare and His arranging of his affairs. He is needy of Him by virtue of His Divinity, that He is his God, his Lord, and his supreme beloved, without whom there is no righteousness, no success, no bliss and no joy for him, except by making Allah the most beloved of all things to him, more beloved than himself, his family, his wealth, his father, his child, and all of creation. He is needy of Him by virtue of His protecting him from all kinds of affliction, for if He did not protect him, he would perish by some of them. He is needy of Him by virtue of His pardon of him and His forgiveness of him, for if He does not pardon the servant and forgive him, there is no path to salvation. No one is saved except by Allah's pardon, and no one enters Paradise except by Allah's mercy.

Many people look at the very thing they repent from and see it as a deficiency, and do not look at the complete end achieved through repentance, that the servant after sincere repentance is better than he was before the sin. They do not look at the perfection of Lordship, and that the Lord alone is perfect, and that the properties of humanity are never free from humans, and that repentance is the goal and perfection of every son of Adam, just as it was His goal and perfection. So the servant has no perfection without repentance at all, just as he has no freedom from its cause. He (glorified is He) is the One who alone is independent, the One who alone possesses richness and praise in every respect and every consideration, while the servant is the poor one, needy of Him and dependent on Him in every respect and every consideration. So His mercy to the servant is better for him than his own deeds, for his deeds cannot by themselves bring about his salvation or his happiness. If he were left to his deeds, he would never be saved by them at all. This is part of what relates to his saying (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, if He punished the people of His heavens and the people of His earth, He would punish them, and He would not be unjust to them."

What clarifies this is that His thanks is due from them by virtue of His Lordship over them and their being His servants and slaves. This obliges them to know Him, to exalt Him, to affirm His oneness, and to draw near to Him as a loving servant draws near, one who moves about in His blessings and cannot be independent of Him for an instant. He strives to draw near to Him with all his effort, exhausts his capacity and power in this, does not place anyone equal to Him in anything, and prefers the pleasure of his master over his own will and desire. He has no desire and no will except in what his master wills and loves. This necessitates knowledge, actions, wills and aspirations that nothing else can oppose, and with which he retains no attention to anything else in any way. It is known that what humans are disposed to cannot fulfill this, while what the Exalted Lord deserves by His very essence, and that He is worthy to be worshipped, is greater than what He deserves for His kindness. He is the One who deserves the ultimate worship, humility and submission by His essence and by His kindness and bounty.

In some reports: "If I had not created a Paradise or a Fire, I would still be worthy of being worshipped."

For this reason, the one most devoted to Him among His creatures, the angels, will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Glory be to You, we have not worshipped You with the worship You deserve." So from His generosity, His liberality and His mercy, He is pleased from His servants with a small portion of what ought to be worshipped by them and what He deserves by His essence and His kindness. The actual worship of creatures bears no comparison to what He deserves in any respect, so nothing can contain them except His pardon and His overlooking. He (glorified is He) knows His servants better than they know themselves, so if He punished them, He would be punishing them for what He knows of them, even if they do not comprehend it. And if He had punished them before sending His messengers to them for their deeds, He would not be unjust to them, just as He did not wrong them when He abhorred them for their disbelief, their polytheism and their abominations before sending His Messenger. He (glorified is He) looked at the people of the earth, and He abhorred them, Arab and non-Arab alike, except for remnants of the People of the Book. But He made it binding upon Himself, when He prescribed mercy for Himself, that He would not punish anyone except after the proof of His message had been established against them. The secret of the matter is that since the thanks owed to the Benefactor is according to His worth and according to the measure of His blessings, and no one can fulfill that, His right over every person is binding, and He has the right to demand it. If He does not forgive and show mercy, He would punish. So their need for His forgiveness, His mercy and His pardon is like their need for His protection, His guardianship and His provision. If He does not protect them, they perish; if He does not provide for them, they perish; if He does not forgive them and show mercy to them, they perish and are lost.

For this reason their father Adam and their mother Eve said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers." (Q 7:23)

This is the condition of his offspring after him. Moses, His interlocutor, said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me." (Q 28:16) And he said: "Glory be to You, I have turned to You, and I am the first of the believers." (Q 7:143) And he said: "My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful." (Q 7:151) And he said: "You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of forgivers." (Q 7:155)

His intimate friend Abraham said: "My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants. Our Lord, accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day the account is established." (Q 14:40–41) And he said: "He who created me, it is He who guides me." (Q 26:78) up to his saying: "And He who I hope will forgive me my error on the Day of Judgment." (Q 26:82)

The first of His messengers to the people of the earth said: "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about what I have no knowledge of. And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers." (Q 11:47)

And He said to the most noble of His creation and the most beloved to Him: "Seek forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and women." (Q 47:19) And He said: "Indeed We have sent down to you the Book with truth," up to His saying: "And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." (Q 4:105–106) And He said: "Indeed We have given you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows and complete His favor upon you and guide you to a straight path." (Q 48:1–2)

The hadith of Ibn Abbas has already been mentioned, in his (ﷺ) supplication: "My Lord, help me and do not help against me."

And in it: "My Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sin," and the hadith continues.

[Section on the excuses of those who stayed behind]

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Medina, he began with the mosque, prayed two rak'ahs in it, then sat for the people. Those who had stayed behind came to him and began to make excuses to him and swear oaths to him. They were some eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward profession, pledged allegiance with them, and asked forgiveness for them, and he left their inward states to Allah. Then Ka'b ibn Malik came to him, and when he greeted him, the Prophet smiled the smile of one who is angry, then said to him: "Come here." He said: So I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: "What kept you back? Had you not purchased your mount?" I said: "Yes. By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else among the people of this world, I would have thought to escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have been given eloquence in argument. But by Allah, I know that if I tell you today a false story to win your approval, Allah would soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you a true story, about which you will be upset with me, I truly hope for Allah's pardon for me. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger or more well-off than when I stayed behind from you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for this, he has spoken the truth. Stand up until Allah decides concerning you." So I stood up, and some men from Banu Salama rose and followed me, rebuking me. They said to me: "By Allah, we did not know you to have committed any sin before this. You have failed to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like the excuses the others made. The Messenger of Allah's seeking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin." He said: "By Allah, they continued to rebuke me until I wanted to go back and call myself a liar. Then I said to them: 'Did anyone else meet this same fate with me?' They said: 'Yes, two men said what you said, and they were told what you were told.' I said: 'Who are they?' They said: 'Murara ibn al-Rabi al-Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayya al-Waqifi.' So they mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom there is an example. So I went on when they mentioned them to me."

The Messenger of God ﷺ forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, the three of us, among those who had stayed behind from him. So the people avoided us and changed their attitude toward us, until the earth became strange to me; it was no longer the earth I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they became submissive and stayed in their houses weeping. As for me, I was the youngest of the people and the strongest, so I used to go out and attend the prayer with the Muslims and walk through the markets, but no one spoke to me. I would come to the Messenger of God ﷺ and greet him while he was in his gathering after the prayer, and I would say to myself: "Did he move his lips to return my greeting or not?" Then I would pray near him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer, he would turn toward me, and when I turned toward him, he would turn away from me. When this estrangement from the Muslims had lasted long upon me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of the orchard of Abu Qatada, who was my paternal cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting. I said: "O Abu Qatada, I implore you by God, do you know that I love God and His Messenger ﷺ?" He was silent. I repeated it and implored him, and he was silent. I repeated it and implored him again, and he said: "God and His Messenger know best." My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed back over the wall.

While I was walking through the market of Madina, behold, a Nabatean from the Nabateans of Syria, one of those who had brought food to sell in Madina, was saying: "Who will direct me to Ka'b ibn Malik?" The people began pointing to me, until he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. In it was: "To proceed: it has reached me that your companion has treated you harshly, but God has not made you a dwelling of humiliation or of neglect. So join us, and we will console you." When I read it, I said: "This is also one of the trials." So I took it to the oven and set it on fire.

When forty of the fifty nights had passed, behold, the messenger of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to me and said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ commands you to separate from your wife." I said: "Shall I divorce her, or what?" He said: "No, but separate from her and do not approach her." He sent the same to my two companions. I said to my wife: "Go to your family and stay with them until God decides in this matter." The wife of Hilal ibn Umayya came and said: "O Messenger of God, Hilal ibn Umayya is a feeble old man who has no servant. Do you dislike that I serve him?" He said: "No, but let him not approach you." She said: "By God, he has no inclination toward anything; by God, he has not ceased weeping since the matter that happened to him until this day."

Ka'b said: Some of my family said to me: "If only you had asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about your wife, as he permitted the wife of Hilal ibn Umayya to serve him." I said: "By God, I will not ask the Messenger of God ﷺ about her. What would I know of what the Messenger of God ﷺ would say if I asked him about her, while I am a young man?" I remained after that for ten more nights, until the fifty nights were completed for us since the Messenger of God ﷺ forbade people from speaking to us.

When I had prayed the dawn prayer on the fiftieth morning, on the roof of one of our houses, while I was sitting in the state that God the Exalted described, my soul constricted upon me and the earth constricted upon me despite its vastness, I heard the voice of a crier who had climbed the mountain of Sal' calling out at the top of his voice: "O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!" I fell down prostrate, and I knew that relief had come from God. The Messenger of God ﷺ had announced God's acceptance of our repentance when he prayed the dawn prayer. The people went out to give us good tidings, and bearers of good tidings went toward my two companions. A man raced toward me on a horse, and a runner from the tribe of Aslam ran and climbed the summit of the mountain, and the voice had been faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard came to give me the good tidings, I took off my garments and clothed him with them in return for his good news, by God, I did not own anything besides them. I borrowed two garments and put them on, and I set out to the Messenger of God ﷺ. The people met me in groups, congratulating me on the repentance, saying: "May the acceptance of God's repentance of you bring you joy."

Ka'b said: Until I entered the mosque, and behold, the Messenger of God ﷺ was sitting in the mosque with people around him. Talha ibn Ubayd Allah rose to me, hurrying, until he shook my hand and congratulated me. By God, no man of the Emigrants rose to me besides him, and I will never forget that for Talha. When I greeted the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said, while his face was shining from joy: "Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you." I said: "Is it from you, O Messenger of God, or from God?" He said: "No, rather it is from God." When the Messenger of God ﷺ was pleased, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon, and we used to recognize that in him. When I sat before him, I said: "O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I withdraw from my wealth as a charity to God and to His Messenger." He said: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you." I said: "Then I will keep my share that is at Khaybar." I said: "O Messenger of God, God only saved me by truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will speak only the truth as long as I live." By God, I do not know of any Muslim whom God has tested in truthfulness of speech since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God ﷺ until this day, more than He tested me. By God, I have not intentionally lied since then until this day, and I hope that God will preserve me in what remains.

Then God the Exalted revealed to His Messenger: ﴿Certainly God has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾ [al-Tawba: 117], up to His saying ﴿O you who believe, fear God and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawba: 119]. By God, God has never bestowed upon me a blessing after He guided me to Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness to the Messenger of God ﷺ, that I should not have lied to him and then been destroyed as those who lied were destroyed. For God said about those who lied, when He revealed the revelation, the worst that He said of anyone: ﴿They will swear by God to you when you return to them﴾ [al-Tawba: 95], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is not pleased with the defiant people﴾ [al-Tawba: 96].

Ka'b said: Our staying behind, O three of us, was in the matter of those whose excuses the Messenger of God ﷺ accepted when they swore to him; he accepted their pledge, asked forgiveness for them, and deferred our matter until God decided it. Therefore God said: ﴿And [He also turned in forgiveness to] the three who were left behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 118]. What God mentioned was not that we were left behind from the expedition, but rather His leaving us behind and His deferring our matter, in contrast to those who swore to him, made excuses to him, and he accepted from them.

Ahmad? No; 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins; they mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad﴾ [al-Tawba: 102]. He said: They were ten men who stayed behind from the Messenger of God ﷺ in the expedition of Tabuk. When the Messenger of God ﷺ arrived, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ used to pass by them when he returned to the mosque. When he saw them, he said: "Who are these who have tied themselves to the pillars?" They said: "This is Abu Lubaba and his companions. They stayed behind from you, O Messenger of God, and they tied themselves until the Prophet ﷺ releases them and excuses them." He said: "And I swear by God, I will not release them or excuse them until God is the One who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims." When this reached them, they said: "We too will not release ourselves until God is the One who releases us." So God the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And others who have acknowledged their sins; they mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps God will turn to them in forgiveness﴾. And "perhaps" from God is binding: ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Baqara: 37]. When it was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ sent for them, released them and excused them. They came with their wealth and said: "O Messenger of God, this is our wealth, so give it in charity on our behalf and ask forgiveness for us." He said: "I have not been commanded to take your wealth." So God revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them﴾ [al-Tawba: 103]. He says: ask forgiveness for them, ﴿indeed, your prayer is reassurance for them﴾ [al-Tawba: 103]. So he took the charity from them and asked forgiveness for them. As for three men who had not tied themselves to the pillars, they were deferred, not knowing whether they would be punished or whether God would accept their repentance. Then God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Certainly God has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾ [al-Tawba: 117], up to His saying: ﴿And [He also turned in forgiveness to] the three who were left behind﴾ [al-Tawba: 118], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Tawba: 118]. 'Atiyya ibn Sa'd followed him in this narration.

[Section: On pointing out some of the jurisprudence and benefits contained in this expedition]

Among them: the permissibility of fighting in a sacred month, if its departure was in Rajab, as preserved by what Ibn Ishaq said. But here there is another matter: the People of the Book did not consider the sacred months inviolable, unlike the Arabs, who did. It has already been mentioned that regarding the abrogation of the prohibition of fighting in them there are two opinions, and we mentioned the proofs of both parties.

Among them: the ruler's declaration to the subjects and informing them of a matter whose concealment would harm them, so that they may prepare for it and make ready its equipment; and the permissibility of concealing it from others and alluding to it for the sake of the public interest.

Among them: that when the ruler calls the army to mobilize (nafir), its members are obligated to mobilize, and it is not lawful for anyone to stay behind except with his permission. The obligation of mobilization does not require designating each one individually; rather, whenever the ruler calls the army, each of them is obligated to go out with him. This is one of the three situations in which jihad becomes an individual obligation (fard 'ayn).

The second: when the enemy arrives at the land.

The third: when the enemy appears between the two lines.

Among them: the obligation of jihad with wealth just as it is obligated with the self. This is one of the two narrations from Ahmad, and it is the correct view about which there is no doubt. The command to jihad with wealth is the companion of the command to jihad with the self in the Qur'an, and it is paired with it, indeed it comes before jihad with the self in every passage except one. This indicates that jihad with it is more important and more emphatic than jihad with the self. There is no doubt that it is one of the two forms of jihad, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever equips a fighter has fought." So it is obligatory upon one who is able with wealth just as it is obligatory upon one who is able with the body. Jihad with the body is not complete except by spending, and it is not victorious except by numbers and equipment. If one cannot increase the numbers, it is obligatory upon him to supply with wealth and equipment. If the Hajj is obligatory with wealth upon one who is physically incapable, then the obligation of jihad with wealth is more fitting and more deserving.

Among them: what 'Uthman ibn 'Affan displayed of great expenditure in this expedition, and he surpassed the people with it. So the Prophet ﷺ said: "May God forgive you, O 'Uthman, for what you concealed and what you disclosed, and what you hid and what you revealed." Then he said: "'Uthman will not be harmed by what he does after today." He had spent a thousand dinars and three hundred camels with their equipment, saddle-cloths and packs.

Among them: that the one who is incapable with his wealth is not excused until he exerts his effort and his incapacity is verified. God the Exalted only removed the blame from those incapable after they came to the Messenger of God ﷺ so that he would carry them, and he said: ﴿I cannot find anything to carry you upon﴾ [al-Tawba: 92], so they returned weeping for what they had missed of jihad. These are the incapable upon whom there is no blame.

Among them: the ruler's appointment of a deputy when he travels, from among the subjects, over the weak, the excused, the women and the offspring. His deputy should be from among the fighters, because that is among the greatest help to them. The Messenger of God ﷺ used to appoint Ibn Umm Maktum as his deputy, and he appointed him more than ten times.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verses 117–118 (part 4 of 6):

As for the expedition of Tabuk, it is well known among the people of transmission (ahl al-athar) that he appointed Ali ibn Abi Talib as his deputy, as in the two Sahihs, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, behind during the expedition of Tabuk. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, will you leave me behind with the women and children?' He said: 'Are you not pleased to be to me as Harun (Aaron) was to Musa (Moses), except that there will be no prophet after me.'" But this was a special deputyship over his family (ﷺ). As for the general deputyship, it was for Muhammad ibn Maslamah al-Ansari. Evidence for this is that when the hypocrites spread rumours about him and said, "He left him behind because he found him burdensome," he took his weapon and caught up with the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: "They have lied. Rather, I left you behind for what I left in my charge. Return and be my deputy over my family and your family."

Among the lessons of this episode: the permissibility of estimating (kharş) the dates on the palm trees, that this is part of the Shari'ah, and acting upon the word of the estimator (al-kharis). This has already been mentioned in the expedition of Khaybar, and that the leader (imam) may himself make the estimate, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) estimated the orchard of the woman.

Among them: that the water in the wells of Thamud may not be drunk, nor used for cooking, nor for kneading dough, nor for purification. It is permissible to give it to animals, except the water of the she-camel's well. That well was known and remained until the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then people's knowledge of it continued generation after generation until our time. So riding to a well other than it is not an issue. It is covered, solidly built, and wide in its surroundings, and the marks of the punishment are visible upon it, so it is not confused with any other.

Among them: whoever passes by the dwellings of those who incurred wrath and were punished should not enter them or stay there, but should hasten his pace and cover himself with his garment until he has passed them, and should not enter upon them except weeping and taking heed.

From this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) hastening his pace in the valley of Muhassir between Mina and Arafat, for it is the place where Allah destroyed the elephant and its companions.

Among them: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to combine two prayers during travel. The combining by advancing (jam' al-taqdim) came in this story in the hadith of Mu'adh, as has already been mentioned. We have mentioned the defect (illah) of that hadith and who rejected it. Combining by advancing is not reported from him on any journey other than this one. But it is authentically reported from him that he combined by advancing at Arafat before entering Arafat: he combined the Dhuhr and 'Asr at the time of Dhuhr. It has been said that this was for the sake of the rite (nusuk), as Abu Hanifa said. It has been said that it was because of the long journey, as al-Shafi'i and Ahmad said. And it has been said that it was because of preoccupation (shughl), namely his being occupied with standing at Arafat and continuing until sunset. Ahmad said: "One combines because of preoccupation." This is the view of a group of the early and later scholars. This has already been mentioned.

Among them: the permissibility of tayammum (dry ablution) with sand. The Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions crossed the sands between Medina and Tabuk, and without doubt they did not carry earth with them. Those were waterless deserts in which they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. Certainly they performed tayammum on the ground on which they were encamped. All of this is beyond doubt, along with his saying (ﷺ): "Wherever the prayer overtakes a man of my community, there is his mosque and his purifier (tahur)."

Among them: "He (ﷺ) stayed at Tabuk for twenty days, shortening the prayer." He did not tell the community that a man may not shorten the prayer if he stays longer than that. Rather, his stay happened to last that period. A stay during travel does not leave the ruling of travel, whether it is long or short, so long as one is not settled there and does not resolve to remain in that place.

The early and later scholars have differed greatly on this matter.

Among them: his saying (ﷺ): "It was not I who carried you, but Allah carried you." This may be used by the Jabris (Jabriyya, those who deny human agency), but it has no basis for them. This is rather like his saying: "By Allah, I do not give anyone anything, nor withhold, but I am only a distributor who places things where he is commanded." He is the servant and messenger of Allah; he acts only by command. When his Lord commands him to something, he carries it out. So Allah is the Giver, the Withholder, and the Bearer, and the Messenger executes what he has been commanded. As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17], what is meant is the handful of pebbles with which he threw at the faces of the polytheists, and they reached the eyes of all of them. So Allah attributed the throwing to him in terms of casting and tossing, since he performed it, and negated it from him in terms of its reaching all the polytheists, and that is the act of the Lord, the Exalted, which the power of the servant cannot reach. The word "rama" (throwing) is applied to slinging, which is its beginning, and to reaching the target, which is its end.

[Section: his leaving the killing of the hypocrites]

Section

Among them: his leaving the killing of the hypocrites, although the clear disbelief from them had reached him. Whoever argues from this that a zindiq (heretic who conceals disbelief) is not to be killed if he shows repentance uses it as evidence, because they swore to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they had not said it. This applies when it is not a denial; then it is repentance and abandonment. Our companions and others have said: whoever is testified against for apostasy and then testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, one does not investigate anything further about him. Some jurists said: if he denies apostasy, his denial suffices. Whoever does not accept the repentance of a zindiq says: these were not established by clear evidence (bayyina), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) does not rule against them by his own knowledge. The one who conveyed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) their words did not bring them to him with the required quorum of evidence; rather, only one person testified against them, just as Zayd ibn Arqam alone testified against Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and likewise others, for only one person testified against him.

In this answer there is room for scrutiny. The hypocrisy of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his statements of hypocrisy were very numerous, almost mass-transmitted (mutawatir) from the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. Some of them confessed with their tongues and said: "We were only chatting and playing." One of the Kharijites confronted him to his face, saying: "You have not been just." When it was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Will you not kill them?" he did not say: "There is no clear evidence against them." Rather, he said: "The people must not say that Muhammad kills his companions."

So the correct answer is that in leaving their killing during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ) there was a benefit, which included winning hearts to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and uniting the people's word around him. Killing them would have caused aversion, while Islam was still a stranger. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most eager of all for winning people over, and the most careful of all to avoid what would repel them from entering his obedience. This matter was specific to the time of his life (ﷺ). Likewise, his leaving the killing of the one who criticised his judgment, in the story of al-Zubayr and his adversary, when he said: "Because he is the son of your aunt." And in his distribution, when he said: "This is a distribution by which the face of Allah was not intended," and the other's statement to him: "You have not been just." For this is purely his right: he may claim it, and he may leave it. And after him, the community has no right to abandon claiming his right; rather, pursuing it becomes obligatory upon them, without exception. These matters have another place for their fuller explanation; the purpose here is only to point them out.

[Section: if a dhimmi (protected non-Muslim) commits an act harmful to the Muslims, his covenant is broken]

Section

Among them: that the people of the covenant and protection (ahl al-'ahd wa'l-dhimma, i.e., the dhimmis) — if one of them commits an act harmful to Islam, his covenant is broken regarding his property and his life. If the imam is unable to seize him, his blood and property are forfeit, and they belong to whoever captures him, as he said in the treaty with the people of Ayla: "Whoever among them commits an act, his property does not shield his life, and it belongs to whoever takes it from the people." This is because by such acts he becomes a combatant, and his ruling is the ruling of the people of war.

[Section: the permissibility of burial at night]

Section

Among them: the permissibility of burial at night, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) buried Dhu'l-Bijadayn at night.

Ahmad was asked about this and said: "There is no harm in it." He said: "Abu Bakr was buried at night, and Ali buried Fatima at night," and 'A'isha said: "We heard the sound of the spades in the last part of the night at the burial of the Prophet (ﷺ)." End of quote. Uthman, 'A'isha and Ibn Mas'ud were also buried at night.

In al-Tirmidhi, from Ibn Abbas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered a grave at night, and a lamp was lit for him, and he took him from the direction of the qibla, and said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, for you were truly a man who grieved much and recited the Qur'an much.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan hadith."

In al-Bukhari: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked about a man, and said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'So-and-so, who was buried last night,' and he prayed over him."

If it is said: "What do you say about what Muslim reported in his Sahih: 'The Prophet (ﷺ) once gave a sermon in which he mentioned a man of his companions who had died, who was shrouded in an inadequate shroud and buried at night, so the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that a man be buried at night before he is prayed over, unless a person is compelled to it.'" Imam Ahmad said: "This is what I follow."

It is said: We affirm both hadiths, praise be to Allah, and we do not reject one by the other. So we dislike burial at night, and we forbid it, except in cases of necessity or a stronger benefit, such as a dead person who died with travellers at night, and they would be harmed by staying with him until day, or when the body is feared to burst, and similar reasons which make burial at night preferable. And success is from Allah.

[Section: the reward of one who is kept back by an excuse]

Section

Among them: his saying (ﷺ): "There are people in Medina who did not march any march nor crossed any valley except that they were with you." This companionship is with their hearts and their resolve, not as some ignorant people think, that they were with them in body. That is impossible, because they said to him: "And they are in Medina?" He said: "And they are in Medina; the excuse has kept them back." They were with him in spirit, and in the House of the Hijra in their bodily forms. This is jihad by the heart, which is one of its four levels: the heart, the tongue, wealth, and the body. And in the hadith: "Strive against the polytheists with your tongues, your hearts, and your wealth."

[Section: burning and demolishing places of disobedience]

Section

Among them: the burning and demolishing of places where Allah and His Messenger are disobeyed, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burned the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar) and ordered its demolition. It was a mosque in which prayer was performed and the name of Allah was mentioned, but since its building was for harm and to divide the believers, and a refuge for the hypocrites, and every place of this kind must be rendered inoperative by the imam, either by demolition and burning, or by changing its form and removing it from the purpose for which it was built. If this is the case of the Mosque of Harm, then shrines of polytheism, whose custodians call those within them to take them as rivals besides Allah, are more deserving of demolition and more obligatory. Likewise, places of sin and immorality, such as taverns, the houses of wine-sellers, and those who engage in forbidden practices.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab burned an entire village in which wine was sold. He burned the shop of Ruwaysh al-Thaqafi and called him "the fasiq (wicked one)." He burned the palace of Sa'd when he secluded himself in it from the subjects. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also intended to burn the houses of those who abandoned attendance at the congregation and the Friday prayer.

Among them: the permissibility of reciting poetry to an arriving person out of joy and happiness at him, so long as there is no forbidden amusement with it, such as the flute, the shabbaba (a type of flute), or the lute, and it is not singing that includes the enticement to immorality and what Allah has forbidden. This no one forbids. The attempt of the practitioners of immoral listening to use it as evidence is like the attempt of one who permits drinking intoxicating wine by analogy to eating grapes and drinking juice that does not intoxicate, and similar analogies resembling the analogy of those who said: ﴿Trade is only like usury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275].

Among them: the Prophet's (ﷺ) listening to the praise of those who praised him and his leaving off rebuking them. The analogy of others to him in this is not valid, because of the differences between the one who praises and the one who is praised. He also said: "Throw dust in the faces of the flatterers."

Among the lessons and benefits of the story of the three who were left behind are many wisdoms, and we will point out some of them:

Among them: the permissibility of a man reporting his own negligence and shortcoming in obeying Allah and His Messenger, and its cause, and what its outcome was. In that there is warning, advice, and explanation of the paths of good and evil and what follows from them, which is among the most important matters.

Among them: the permissibility of a person praising himself for the good that is in him, so long as it is not by way of boasting and haughtiness.

Among them: a person consoling himself for the good that was not decreed for him by what was decreed for him of a similar kind, or something better than it.

The first point is that the Pledge of al-'Aqaba (bay'at al-'Aqaba) was among the most excellent of the battles and occasions of the Companions (ṣaḥāba), to the extent that Ka'b did not regard any other occasion as superior to the event of Badr.

Another point is that when the imam sees the benefit in concealing from his subjects some of what he intends and aims at against the enemy, and in speaking in a veiled manner about it, such concealment is recommended for him, or it becomes obligatory according to the benefit involved.

Another point is that concealment and secrecy are not permissible when they entail corruption (mafsada).

Another point is that during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ the army had no register (dīwān), and the first to establish the register (dīwān) was 'Umar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (raḍiya Allāhu 'anhu). This is from his Sunnah, which the Prophet ﷺ commanded people to follow, and its benefit and the need of the Muslims for it became evident.

Another point is that when a person is presented with an opportunity for nearness to God and obedience, the utmost resolve lies in seizing it and hastening to it, while weakness lies in delaying it and postponing it, especially when he is not confident of his ability and capacity to attain the means of achieving it. Resolutions and aspirations are quickly undone and rarely remain firm. God, glorified is He, punishes the one to whom He opened a door of good but who did not seize it, by coming between his heart and his will, so that he is no longer able to will it, as a punishment for him. Whoever does not respond to God and His Messenger when they call him, God comes between him and his heart and his will, so that he is no longer able to respond afterwards. The Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that God intervenes between a man and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. God, glorified is He, has made this explicit in His saying: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 110]. The Exalted also said: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], and He said: ﴿And God would not mislead a people after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Tawbah: 115]. This occurs frequently in the Qur'an.

Another point is that none of the men lagged behind the Messenger of God ﷺ except one of three: either one who was accused of hypocrisy (nifāq), or a man of excuse, or one whom the Messenger of God ﷺ left behind and appointed over Madina, or one whom he left behind for a benefit.

Another point is that the imam and the one who is obeyed should not neglect those who lag behind him in some matters, but should remind them so that they return to obedience and repent. The Prophet ﷺ said at Tabuk: "What did Ka'b do?" and did not mention anyone else among those who stayed behind, in order to reform him and show consideration, and to neglect the hypocrite people.

Another point is the permissibility of criticising a man with what prevails upon the judgement of the critic out of zeal or in defence of God and His Messenger. From this is the criticism of the people of hadith of those narrators whom they criticised, and from this is the criticism of the heirs of the prophets and the people of the Sunnah of the people of desires and innovations, for the sake of God and not for their own shares and purposes.

Another point is the permissibility of responding to the critic when the responder's assessment is that it is a mistake and an error, as Mu'adh said to the one who criticised Ka'b: "What a bad thing you said! By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing about him except good." The Messenger of God ﷺ did not denounce either of them.

Another point is that the Sunnah for one returning from a journey is to enter the town in a state of wudu' and to begin with the House of God before his own house, praying two rak'ahs in it, then sitting to receive the greetings of the Muslims, then leaving for his family.

Another point is that the Messenger of God ﷺ would accept the outward profession of those hypocrites who showed Islam, leave their inner state to God, apply to them the ruling of the outward, and not punish them for what he did not know of their secret.

Another point is that the imam and the judge refrain from returning the greeting of one who has committed an offence, as a discipline for him and a deterrent to others. It is not reported that the Prophet ﷺ returned the greeting to Ka'b; rather, he met his greeting with the smile of one who is angry.

Another point is that smiling may come from anger, just as it may come from wonder or joy, for each of them causes the blood of the heart to expand and surge. For this reason redness appears on the face because of the swift surge of blood in it; joy arises from this, while anger is a form of wonder that is followed by laughter and smiling. So the one who is deceived should not be deceived by the laughter of one who has power over him, especially at the time of reproach, as it has been said:

*When you see the fangs of the lion bared,*
*do not think that the lion is smiling.*

Another point is the reproach of the imam and the one who is obeyed to his companions and to those who are dear and honoured to him. He reproached the three and not the rest of those who lagged behind him. People have greatly praised the reproach of loved ones, finding sweetness in it and taking pleasure in it. How much more so is the reproach of the one most beloved of all creation to the one being reproached! How sweet that reproach was, how great its fruit, and how lofty its benefit! How much delight and sweetness of contentment and robes of acceptance the three attained through it!

Another point is God's granting success to Ka'b and his two companions in what they brought of truthfulness. He did not forsake them, whereas those who lied and offered excuses without truth had their immediate state made good but their final outcome utterly corrupted. The truthful ones suffered some hardship in the immediate life, but it brought them a good outcome and complete success. Upon this the world and the Hereafter stand: the bitterness of beginnings becomes sweetness in outcomes, and the sweetness of beginnings becomes bitterness in outcomes. The saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ka'b: "As for this one, he has spoken the truth" is clear evidence for holding to the principle of the implied meaning of the title (mafhūm al-laqab) when there is an indicator requiring that the mentioned subject be specifically assigned the ruling, as in His saying: ﴿And David and Solomon, when they gave judgement concerning the field when the sheep of a people had grazed in it by night; and We were witness to their judgement. And We caused Solomon to understand it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 78-79], and His saying ﷺ: "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and its dust a purifier," and his saying in this hadith: "As for this one, he has spoken the truth." No listener doubts that the speaker intended to specify the ruling for him.

As for Ka'b's saying: "Has anyone met with this same fate as I?" They said: "Yes, Murara ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayya." In this is the point that a man should ward off the heat of a calamity with the spirit of solace from those who have suffered the same as he has. God, the Exalted, directed to this in His saying: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you are suffering, but you hope from God that for which they do not hope﴾ [al-Nisa': 104]. This is the same comfort that God, glorified is He, denies to the people of the Fire in His saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 39]. And his saying: "They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom I have an example."

This point is among what has been counted as errors of al-Zuhri, for it is not preserved from anyone among the people of the campaigns and biographies (ahl al-maghazi wa-l-siyar) at all that these two men are mentioned among the people of Badr: not Ibn Ishaq, nor Musa ibn 'Uqba, nor al-Umawi, nor al-Waqidi, nor anyone who enumerated the people of Badr. Likewise, they should not be among the people of Badr, for the Prophet ﷺ did not boycott Hatib, nor punish him, though he had spied, and he said to 'Umar when he intended to kill him: "What makes you know that God looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you?" And where is the sin of lagging behind compared with the sin of spying?

Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi said: I was always eager to uncover and verify this until I saw that Abu Bakr al-Athram had mentioned al-Zuhri, mentioned his excellence, his memorization and his precision, and that hardly any error is preserved against him except in this place. For he said that Murara ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayya witnessed Badr, and no one other than him said this, and a mistake is not immune from any human being.

[Section on the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of speaking to these three as a discipline for them being evidence of their truthfulness]

Section

In the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of speaking to these three, among all who lagged behind him, is evidence of their truthfulness and the falsehood of the rest. He intended to boycott the truthful and discipline them for this sin. As for the hypocrites, their crime is too great to be met with boycott, and the remedy for this disease does not work on the disease of hypocrisy, nor is there any benefit in it. Likewise the Lord, glorified is He, deals with His servants in punishing their crimes: He disciplines His believing servant whom He loves and who is honoured in His sight with the slightest slip and lapse, so he remains ever alert and cautious. But whoever has fallen from His sight and become despised before Him, He leaves him to his sins, and whenever he commits a sin, He grants him a blessing. The deceived one thinks that this is from His honour toward him, not knowing that it is the very essence of humiliation, and that He intends by it the severe punishment and the chastisement that has no end. As in the well-known hadith: "When God wills good for a servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when He wills evil for a servant, He withholds his punishment in this world, until he comes on the Day of Resurrection with his sins."

In it there is also evidence for the imam, the scholar and the one who is obeyed boycotting one who has done what deserves reproach, and his boycott being a remedy for him, such that it does not weaken him from attaining healing through it, nor exceed in quantity or quality so as to destroy him, since the aim is his discipline, not his destruction.

As for his saying: "until the earth became strange to me, so it was not the earth I knew," this strangeness is felt by the fearful, the sorrowful and the anxious in the earth and in trees and plants, even in people who do not know his state. The sinner and the disobedient also feel it according to the magnitude of his offence, even in the character of his wife and child, his servant and his animal, and he feels it within himself as well, so that his own self becomes strange to him, as though it were not him, nor his family and companions, nor those who are compassionate to him, whom he knows. This is a secret from God that is hidden except from one whose heart is dead; and according to the life of the heart, the perception of this strangeness and loneliness occurs.

*And a wound does not feel pain when it is dead.*

It is well known that this strangeness and loneliness were far greater for the people of hypocrisy, but because their hearts were dead they did not feel it. Likewise, when the heart's disease becomes entrenched and its pain intensifies through sins and crimes, it no longer finds this loneliness and strangeness, nor senses it. This is the sign of wretchedness, and that one has despaired of the health of this disease, and the physicians have been unable to cure it. Fear and anxiety accompany suspicion, while security and joy accompany freedom from sin.

*There is nothing on earth braver than the innocent,*
*and nothing on earth more fearful than the doubtful.*

This measure may benefit the discerning believer when he is tested with it and then returns to God, for he benefits from it greatly in countless ways. Even if there were nothing in it except that he derives from it the signs of prophethood, and tastes directly what the Messenger reported, so that his belief becomes self-evident to him, and what he receives of evil through his sins and of good through his obedience becomes proofs of the truth of prophethood, known by direct experience and not open to doubt. This is like one who informs you that on this path there are such-and-such dangers and fears in detail; you disregard him and take it, and you see exactly what he told you, so you witness his truthfulness precisely in your opposition to him. But if you take the path of safety alone and find none of those fears, then although you may bear witness to the truth of the informant regarding the good and the success you have gained in detail, your knowledge of those things remains general.

The letter of the king of Ghassan to Ka'b ibn Malik inviting him to come to him was a trial from God, the Exalted, and a test of his faith and his love for God and His Messenger, and a demonstration to the Companions that he was not one whose faith had weakened through the Prophet's ﷺ and the Muslims' boycott of him, nor one whom the desire for status and kingship, together with the Messenger's and the believers' boycott of him, would move to abandon his religion. In this there is part of God's clearing him of hypocrisy, the display of the strength of his faith and his truthfulness to His Messenger and the Muslims, which is part of the completion of God's favour upon him, His kindness to him, and His mending of his brokenness. This trial reveals a man's core and secret and what he conceals within, for it is like the furnace that separates the bad from the good.

So the precedence of goodness refused to let him turn away from the Messenger of God ﷺ and his religion.

[Section on prostration of gratitude being a habit of the Companions]

Section

And in Ka'b's prostration when he heard the voice of the bearer of good news, there is clear evidence that this was the custom of the Companions: the prostration of gratitude at renewed blessings and averted calamities. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq prostrated when he received news of the killing of Musaylima al-Kadhdhab. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib prostrated when he found Dhu al-Thudayya killed among the Kharijites. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrated when Jibril gave him the good news that whoever sends blessings upon him once, Allah sends blessings upon him tenfold. He prostrated when he interceded for his Ummah and Allah granted his intercession for them three times. A messenger came to him with the good news of victory for a force of his over their enemy, while his head was in the lap of 'Aisha, and he rose and fell prostrate. Abu Bakra said: "When something that pleased the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him, he would fall prostrate to Allah." These are sound reports with no flaw in them.

In the racing of the horseman and the runner towards Sala' to give Ka'b the good news, there is evidence of the people's eagerness for good and their hastening towards it, and their competing to bring joy to one another.

In Ka'b's removing his two garments and giving them to the bearer of good news, there is evidence that giving to bearers of good news is among the noble characteristics and the custom of the honourable. Al-'Abbas freed his slave when the slave gave him the good news that Hajjaj ibn 'Ilat had information from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that would please him.

In it there is also evidence for the permissibility of giving a bearer of good news all of one's garments.

In it there is evidence for the recommendation (istihbab) of congratulating one to whom a religious blessing has renewed, of standing up for him when he approaches, and of shaking his hand. This is a recommended sunnah (the prophetic practice). It is also permissible for one to whom a worldly blessing has renewed, and the better course is to say to him: "May what Allah has given you bring you joy, and what Allah has bestowed upon you," and similar words, for in this is the attribution of the blessing to its Lord and a supplication for the one who has attained it, that he may rejoice in it.

In it there is evidence that the best and most excellent of a servant's days, absolutely, is the day of his repentance to Allah and Allah's acceptance of his repentance, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you." If it is said: how can this day be better than the day of his Islam?

It is said: it completes his day of Islam and is part of its perfection. The day of his Islam is the beginning of his happiness, and the day of his repentance is its completion and perfection. And Allah is the One sought for help.

In the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) joy at this, his delight in it, and the brightening of his face, there is evidence of the perfect compassion, mercy and tenderness that Allah placed in him towards the Ummah, to the point that his joy may have been greater than the joy of Ka'b and his two companions.

Ka'b's saying: "O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I should strip myself of my wealth," is evidence for the recommendation of giving charity upon repentance with whatever wealth one is able to.

The saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you," is evidence that whoever vows to give away all his wealth in charity is not obliged to give away all of it, but may keep a remainder for himself. The reports differ on this. In al-Sahihayn (the two Sahih collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Keep some of your wealth for yourself," without specifying an amount; he left it unrestricted and entrusted it to his own judgment regarding the sufficiency needed. This is the correct view, for what falls short of his sufficiency and that of his household is not permissible for him to give in charity, so his vow in that case is not an act of obedience and does not have to be fulfilled. What exceeds his sufficiency and need, its giving and donating is more excellent, and so it must be given if he vowed it. This is the analogy of the school and what the principles of the Shari'ah require. For this reason, a man's own sufficiency and that of his household take precedence over the discharge of financial obligations, whether they are a right of Allah, such as expiations and Hajj, or a right of the children of Adam, such as repaying debts. For we leave the insolvent debtor what he cannot do without: a dwelling, a servant, clothing, the tools of his trade, or what he trades with for his livelihood if he lacks a trade, and the creditors' right is in what remains.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 119 (part 1 of 2):

Many of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: "They are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ)." There is no doubt that they are the leaders of the truthful, and every truthful person after them follows them in his truthfulness. Indeed, the true reality of one's truthfulness is following them and being with them. It is known that whoever opposes them in something, even if he agrees with them in other things, is not with them in what he opposes them in. In that case, it is correct to say of him that he is not with them, so the absolute companionship (al-ma'iyya al-mutlaqa) is negated from him, even though he has a share of companionship in what he agrees with them about. It is not correct to say of him that he is with them by this share. This is like the way Allah and His Messenger negated complete faith (al-iman al-mutlaq) from the adulterer, the drinker, the thief, and the plunderer, to the point that he does not deserve the name "believer," though the general name that makes it correct to say "he has some faith" is not negated from him. It is also like the name "jurist" (faqih) and "scholar" (alim) when used without qualification: it is not said of someone who has one or two issues of jurisprudence or knowledge, although it may be said that "he has some knowledge." So there is a difference between absolute companionship and companionship in general. It is known that what is commanded is the first, not the second. Allah, exalted is He, did not intend that we be with them in some things only, or that we attain from companionship only what the name applies to. This is a great error in understanding the intent of the Lord, exalted is He, in His commands. When He commands us to piety, righteousness, truthfulness, chastity, enjoining good, forbidding evil, jihad, and the like, He does not intend that we perform the least amount to which the name applies, namely the bare essence of what is commanded, such that we are obedient to His command when we do that. The full establishment of this point is the same as what was established earlier regarding the command to follow them.

[Section: On the greatness of truthfulness, and the linking of the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, and salvation from their evil, to it]

Allah did not save anyone He saved except through truthfulness, and He did not destroy anyone He destroyed except through lying. Allah, glorified is He, commanded His believing servants to be with the truthful, saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawba: 119].

He, glorified is He, divided creation into two categories: the happy (su'ada') and the miserable (ashqiya'). He made the happy the people of truthfulness and affirmation (al-tasdiq), and the miserable the people of lying and denial (al-takdhib). This is a division that is comprehensive, consistent, and reciprocal. Happiness revolves around truthfulness and affirmation, and misery revolves around lying and denial.

Allah, exalted is He, informed that on the Day of Resurrection only one's truthfulness will benefit the servants. He made the mark (alam) by which the hypocrites are distinguished the lying in their words and actions. So everything He reproached them for has as its root lying in speech and deed. Truthfulness is the herald of faith, its guide, its mount, its driver, its leader, its adornment, and its garment; indeed, it is its core and its spirit. Lying is the herald of disbelief and hypocrisy, its guide, its mount, its driver, its leader, its adornment, its garment, and its core. The opposition of lying to faith is like the opposition of polytheism to monotheism. Lying and faith do not come together except that one of them drives out the other and takes its place. Allah, glorified is He, saved the three [who stayed behind] through their truthfulness and destroyed the others among those who stayed behind through their lying. Allah has bestowed upon no servant, after Islam, a blessing better than truthfulness, which is the nourishment and life of Islam, nor has He tested him with a trial greater than lying, which is the sickness and corruption of Islam. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

(Benefit)
A student asked his teacher to praise him in a letter to a man and to exaggerate his praise beyond his rank.
The teacher said: "If I did that, then in the eyes of the one to whom the letter is written I would be either deficient in understanding, since I gave you more than your due, or accused of false reporting, and so I would be a liar.
Both matters would harm you, because I am your witness, and when the witness is discredited, the right of the one he testifies for is nullified."

[Section: The station of truthfulness]

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5] is the station of truthfulness (manzilat al-sidq), which is the greatest station of the people. From it all the stations of the travelers (al-salikin) arise, and it is the straightest path. Whoever does not walk upon it is among those who are cut off and destroyed. By it the people of hypocrisy are distinguished from the people of faith, and the dwellers of Paradise from the people of the Fire. It is the sword of Allah on His earth, which is never placed upon anything without cutting it, and never confronts falsehood without throwing it down and felling it. Whoever charges with it, his charge is not repelled, and whoever speaks by it, his word prevails over his opponents. It is the spirit of deeds, the touchstone of states, the impetus to face terrors, and the gate through which those who arrive enter the presence of the Majestic Lord. It is the foundation of the building of religion and the pillar of the tent of certainty. Its rank follows the rank of prophethood, which is the highest rank of all beings. Among its dwellings in the Gardens, rivers flow to the dwellings of the truthful (al-siddiqin). Just as there was, between their hearts in this world, a continuous and abundant flow of support.

Allah, glorified is He, commanded the people of faith to be with the truthful, and singled out those upon whom He bestowed favor: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [al-Tawba: 119]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. They are "the highest companions," ﴿and excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. Allah continues to supply them with His favors, His kindness, and His increase, out of His generosity and success. For them is the rank of companionship with Allah, for Allah is with the truthful, and for them is the station of nearness to Him, since their rank with Him is the second rank after the prophets.

He, exalted is He, informed that whoever is truthful to Him, it is better for him. He said: ﴿But when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them﴾ [Muhammad: 21].

He, exalted is He, spoke of the people of righteousness (ahl al-birr) and praised them for their best deeds: faith, Islam, charity, and patience, and that they are the people of truthfulness. He said: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Scripture, and the prophets, and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing slaves; and [one who] establishes prayer and gives zakah; and those who fulfill their promise when they promise; and the patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and those are the righteous﴾ [al-Baqara: 177]. This is explicit that truthfulness is in outward and inward deeds, and that truthfulness is the station of Islam and faith.

Allah, glorified is He, divided people into the truthful and the hypocrite. He said: ﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or turn to them in forgiveness﴾ [al-Ahzab: 24].

Faith is founded on truthfulness, and hypocrisy is founded on lying. Lying and faith do not come together except that one of them wars against the other.

He, glorified is He, informed that on the Day of Resurrection, nothing will benefit the servant or save him from His punishment except his truthfulness. He said: ﴿This is a day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 119]. He said: ﴿And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it, those are the righteous﴾ [al-Zumar: 33]. "The one who brought the truth" means that truthfulness is a characteristic of his speech, his deed, and his state. Truthfulness is in these three things.

Truthfulness in speech is the tongue's being straight in its statements, like the ear of grain standing upright on its stalk. Truthfulness in deeds is the actions' being straight according to the command and the following of the Sunnah, like the head's being upright on the body. Truthfulness in states is the straightness of the actions of the heart and the limbs upon sincerity (ikhlas), the exertion of effort, and the expending of strength. By this the servant becomes among those who "brought the truth." According to the completeness of these matters in him and their establishment in him, his being a siddiq (truthful one) is determined. For this reason, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him and make him pleased, had the peak of the hump of siddiqiyya (the station of being a siddiq). He was called "al-Siddiq" without qualification. And al-siddiq is more emphatic than al-sadduq, and al-sadduq is more emphatic than al-sadiq.

So the highest levels of truthfulness are the rank of siddiqiyya, which is the perfection of submission to the Messenger (ﷺ) together with the perfection of sincerity toward the One who sent him.

Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Messenger to ask Him to make his entering and exiting upon truthfulness. He said: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause my entry to be of truth and my exit to be of truth, and grant me from Yourself an authority to help me"﴾ [al-Isra': 80]. He informed about His intimate friend Ibrahim (ﷺ), that he asked Him to grant him a tongue of truthfulness among later generations. He said: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truth among later generations﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 84]. He gave good news to His servants that for them with Him is a foot of truthfulness and a seat of truthfulness. He said: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a foot of sincerity with their Lord﴾ [Yunus: 2]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be within gardens and a river, in a seat of truth, near a Sovereign, Able﴾ [al-Qamar: 54-55].

So these are five things: the entrance of truthfulness, the exit of truthfulness, the tongue of truthfulness, the foot of truthfulness, and the seat of truthfulness.

The reality of truthfulness in these matters is the established truth, connected to Allah, leading to Allah, and it is what was done for His sake and for what belongs to Him, of words and deeds. Its recompense is in this world and the Hereafter.

So the entrance of truthfulness and the exit of truthfulness: that one's entering and exiting be a truth established by Allah and in pursuit of His pleasure, through attaining the aim and reaching the sought goal. This is the opposite of the exit and entrance of lying, which has no end to reach and no firm leg to stand upon. Like the exit of his enemies on the day of Badr. The exit of truthfulness is like his exit (ﷺ) and that of his Companions in that expedition.

Likewise, his (ﷺ) entrance into Madina was an entrance of truthfulness: by Allah, for Allah, and seeking the pleasure of Allah. Thus support, victory, help, and the attainment of what he sought in this world and the Hereafter were connected to it. This contrasts with the entrance of lying, which his enemies intended to enter Madina with on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), for it was not by Allah nor for Allah. Rather it was opposition to Allah and His Messenger, so only humiliation and ruin were connected to it.

Likewise is the entrance of the Jews who fought the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) into the fortress of Banu Qurayza. When it was an entrance of lying, what befell them with it befell them as well.

Thus every entrance and exit that is by Allah and for Allah, its doer is a guarantee upon Allah. It is an entrance of truthfulness and an exit of truthfulness.

Some of the early scholars, when they left their house, would raise their head to the sky and say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from going out on an exit in which I am not a guarantee upon You."

He means: that the exit should not be other than an exit of truthfulness. For this reason, the entrance of truthfulness and its exit were interpreted as his (ﷺ) going out from Makka and entering Madina. There is no doubt that this is by way of example, since this entrance and exit are among the most noble of his entrances and exits (ﷺ). Otherwise all his entrances are entrances of truthfulness and all his exits are exits of truthfulness, since they are for Allah, by Allah, by His command, and seeking His pleasure.

Whenever anyone leaves his house and enters his market, or another place, it is only with truthfulness or with lying. The exit and entrance of each person do not go beyond truthfulness or lying. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

As for the tongue of truthfulness: it is the good praise of him (ﷺ) from all the nations, with truthfulness, not praise by lying. Just as He said about Ibrahim and his descendants among the prophets and messengers, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truth, elevated﴾ [Maryam: 50]. The meaning of "tongue" here is good praise. Since truthfulness is with the tongue, and it is its locus, Allah, glorified is He, made the tongues of His servants speak praise of the truthful, as a recompense in kind, and expressed it by that.

The word "tongue" (lisan) is used for three meanings: this one, language, and the organ itself. For language, as in His saying: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people to make [the message] clear for them﴾ [Ibrahim: 4], and His saying: ﴿And the difference of your languages and your colors﴾ [al-Rum: 22], and His saying: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103]. For the organ itself, as in His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ [al-Qiyama: 16].

As for the foot of truthfulness: it has been interpreted as Paradise, as Muhammad (ﷺ), and as righteous deeds.

The true meaning of "qadam" (footing) is what they sent forward (*qaddamū*), and what they will come upon on the Day of Resurrection. They sent forward their deeds and their faith in Muhammad (ﷺ), and they will come upon (*yaqdamūna ʿalayhi*) Paradise, which is the reward for that.

Whoever interprets it as Paradise means: "what they will come upon." Whoever interprets it as deeds and the Prophet (ﷺ) means: "because they sent them forward," and they sent forward faith in him ahead of them. So the three (deeds, faith, and the Prophet) are a "footing of truthfulness" (*qadam ṣidq*). As for "a seat of truthfulness" (*maqʿad al-ṣidq*), it is Paradise in the presence of the Lord, blessed and exalted.

Describing all of this as "truthful" (*ṣidq*) necessitates its being established and firm, that it is true, that it lasts, that it is beneficial, and that its benefit is complete. It is connected to the Truth (al-Ḥaqq), glorified is He, existing through Him and for Him. So it is truthful and not false, true and not void, lasting and not perishing, beneficial and not harmful.
