Falsehood and its associated matters have no path or entry to it.

Among the signs of truthfulness is the heart's tranquility (*ṭumaʾnīna*) in it, and among the signs of falsehood is the arising of doubt (*rība*). This is as in al-Tirmidhi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) by way of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Truthfulness is tranquility, and falsehood is doubt." In the two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from the narration of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to speak the truth until he is written before Allah as a truthful one (*ṣiddīq*). Falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie until he is written before Allah as a great liar." Thus he made truthfulness the key to and beginning of *al-ṣiddīqiyya* (the station of being a supremely truthful one), and it is its ultimate goal. No liar ever attains its rank, whether in his speech, his deeds, or his state. This is especially so for one who lies about Allah regarding His names and attributes, denying what He has affirmed or affirming what He has negated about Himself. Among such people there will never be a *ṣiddīq*.

Likewise, lying about Him in His religion and law, by making lawful what He has forbidden, forbidding what He has not forbidden, dropping what He has made obligatory, making obligatory what He has not made obligatory, disliking what He loves, and recommending what He does not love. All of this is incompatible with *al-ṣiddīqiyya*.

Likewise, lying to Him in deeds, by adorning oneself with the adornment of the truthful, the sincere, the ascetic, and the trusting (*mutawakkilīn*), while not truly being among them.

Therefore *al-ṣiddīqiyya* is the perfection of sincerity, submission, and following the report and the command, outwardly and inwardly, to the extent that the truthfulness of two parties to a sale brings blessing to their sale, while their lying erases its blessing. This is as in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (to cancel) so long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and clarify, their sale will be blessed for them. If they lie and conceal, the blessing of their sale will be erased."

[Section on sayings about the reality of truthfulness]

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd said: Truthfulness is fidelity to Allah through action.

It has also been said: It is the agreement of the inner state with the speech.

It has also been said: It is the equality of the inner and the outer. This means that the liar's outward appearance is better than his inner reality, like the hypocrite whose outward is better than his inward.

It has also been said: Truthfulness is speaking the truth in places of destruction.

It has also been said: It is a word of truth before one whom you fear and hope in.

Al-Junayd said: The truthful person changes forty times a day, while the hypocrite (*murāʾī*) remains in one state for forty years.

This statement needs explanation, and its opposite may come to mind, namely that the liar is changeable, since lying has many colors, so he changes with its changing, whereas the truthful person is steady in one state. Truthfulness is one in itself, and its possessor does not change or alter.

But the intended meaning of Shaykh Abu al-Qasim (al-Junayd) is correct and differs from this. The trials and inspirations that come upon the truthful person do not come upon the lying hypocrite. Rather, he is empty of them. Indeed, the inspirations from the Truth that come upon the truthful do not come upon liars and hypocrites, and Satan does not oppose them as he opposes the truthful. For he has no interest in a ruin with nothing in it. These inspirations cause the truthful person to change according to their variety and diversity. So you see him only fleeing from place to place, from deed to deed, from state to state, and from cause to cause, because he fears in every state in which he finds tranquility, and every place and cause, that it will cut him off from what he seeks.

He does not settle in any state or thing short of his goal. He is like one who wanders the horizons seeking a wealth that surpasses that of the rich. Circumstances and causes turn him about, raising him and seating him, moving him and stilling him, until he finds in them what helps him toward his goal, and this is rare among them. So his heart is in constant turning and intense movement, in proportion to the vastness of his goal, its greatness, and his resolve, which is too high to stop short of his aim at a mark or state, or to settle in anything other than it. He is like the true lover whose aim is to search for his beloved. Likewise is the state of the truthful seeker of knowledge, and the state of the truthful seeker of worldly things. Every truthful person seeking something finds no settled resting place and does not remain in one state.

Also: the truthful person's aim is the pleasure of his Lord, the execution of His commands, and the pursuit of what He loves. So he moves within these, going wherever their mounts go, and settling wherever their camps settle. So while he is in prayer, you see him in remembrance, then in holy warfare, then in pilgrimage, then in doing good to creation by teaching and other kinds of benefit, then in commanding good or forbidding evil, or in undertaking a matter that builds up religion and the world, then in visiting the sick, or accompanying a funeral, or supporting the oppressed where possible, and other kinds of nearness to Allah and benefits.

So he is constantly dispersing for Allah and gathered upon Allah. No outward form, custom, or fixed situation possesses him. He is not bound by any restriction or gesture, nor by a specific place where he prays and will not pray elsewhere, nor a specific garment that he will not wear instead, nor a specific worship to which he pays no attention, even though other worship is better than it or higher in rank. The distance between these is like the distance between heaven and earth.

For trials, calamities, showing off, affectation, worship of the self, preferring its desires, and drawing attention to it, all of these exist in these conditions, customs, restrictions, and bonds, which have imprisoned their owners from journeying to their hearts, let alone journeying from their hearts to Allah, exalted is He. So if one of them departs from his custom, condition, garb, restriction, or gesture, even toward something better, he finds it shameful, sees it as a deficiency, a fall in the eyes of people, and a lowering of his rank among them. Yet he has already been lowered and has fallen from the sight of Allah.

One of them may sense this within himself and in his state, yet his customs, conditions, garb, and restrictions do not allow him to stop trying to repair and reform it. This is the way of the lying hypocrite who shows people the opposite of what Allah knows of his inner self, working to build his own self and rank. This is hypocrisy itself. Had he been acting toward what Allah intends from him, and in truthfulness with Allah, those restrictions would have weighed him down, those customs would have held him back, and he would have seen standing by them and with them as the cutting-off from Allah rather than the reaching toward Him. He would not care what garment he wore or what deed he performed, so long as it was in accordance with what Allah intends from the servant.

So the words of Abu al-Qasim al-Junayd are true, words of one firmly rooted in truthfulness, knowledgeable of its details, its afflictions, and the points where it resembles falsehood.

Also, bearing truthfulness is like bearing the firm mountains. Only the people of resolve can bear it, and they turn beneath it like one carrying a heavy load. Showing off and lying are light like a feather, and their possessor finds no weight in them at all. He carries them in any place without fatigue, hardship, or burden. So he does not turn beneath his load, and does not feel its weight.

Some of them said: A servant who flatters his soul or others will never smell the scent of truthfulness.

Some of them said: The truthful one is one who is prepared to die and not feel shame at his secret being revealed. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Baqara: 94].

Ibrahim al-Khawwas said: You will never see the truthful person except in an obligation he is fulfilling or a virtue he is performing.

Al-Junayd said: The reality of truthfulness is that you are truthful in a situation from which only lying would save you.

It has been said: Three things do not miss the truthful person: sweetness, comeliness, and awe.

In a divine report: "Whoever is truthful with Me in his secret, I will be truthful to him in his public before My creation."

Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah said: The first betrayal of the *ṣiddīqīn* (the truthful ones) is their discourse with their own selves.

Yusuf ibn Asbāṭ said: To spend a night dealing with Allah in truthfulness is dearer to me than to strike with my sword in the cause of Allah.

Al-Ḥārith al-Muḥāsibī said: The truthful one is the one who does not mind if every measure of his standing in the hearts of creation departs, for the sake of the soundness of his heart. He does not love that people should see even the weight of an ant-atom of his good deeds, and he does not dislike that people should see the bad of his deeds. For his dislike of that is evidence that he loves to be increased in their estimation, and this is not one of the signs of the *ṣiddīqīn*.

I say: There is room to examine this. For his disliking that people see the faults of his deeds is of the same kind as his disliking beatings, illness, and all other pains. This is a natural, innate matter, and its possessor does not leave truthfulness because of it, especially if he is a model to be followed. Indeed, his disliking that is one of the signs of his truthfulness, because in it are two harms: the harm of abandoning emulation of him, and his being followed in good and implementing it; and the harm of the ignorant emulating him in faults. So his disliking that they see the faults of his deeds does not contradict his truthfulness, and may even be one of its signs.

Yes, what contradicts truthfulness is that a person has no aim other than building his standing among them and dwelling in their hearts with reverence for him. If his aim is the execution of Allah's command, the spreading of His religion, commanding good, forbidding evil, and calling to Allah, then this is the truly truthful person. Allah knows the secrets of hearts and their intentions.

I think this is what al-Muḥāsibī meant by his words: "and he does not dislike that people see the bad of his deeds," for they desire that out of excess and interference in what does not concern them. May Allah be pleased with Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, when he said: "I will certainly fight whoever separates prayer from zakat. By Allah, if they withhold from me a young goat or a cord, which they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I will fight them over it." So this and similar things people count and see as bad deeds among the common folk and the ignorant.

Some of them said: Whoever does not fulfill the constant obligation, his temporary obligation will not be accepted from him.

It was asked: What is the constant obligation? He said: Truthfulness.

It has been said: Whoever seeks Allah with truthfulness, He gives him a mirror in which he sees truth and falsehood.

It has been said: Hold to truthfulness where you fear it will harm you, for it will benefit you. And leave lying where you think it will benefit you, for it will harm you. It has also been said: No truthful merchant has ever become destitute.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 120:

It is related in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one has been given a gift better and more expansive than patience."

It is related in some of the Musnads from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: When I afflict one of My servants with a calamity in his body, his wealth, or his children, and he then meets that with beautiful patience, I am ashamed before him on the Day of Resurrection to set up a scale for him or unroll a record for him."

In the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from him: "When Allah loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is content, for him is contentment, and whoever is discontent, for him is discontent."

In some of the Musnads, from him, raised (marfu'): "When Allah wills good for a servant, He pours trials upon him in abundance."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon a woman and said: "What is wrong with you, trembling?" She said: "The fever; may Allah not bless it." He said: "Do not curse the fever, for it removes the sins of the children of Adam as the furnace removes the impurity of iron."

It is mentioned from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever has a fever for a night, and is patient and content with Allah, the Exalted, comes out of his sins like the day his mother bore him."

Al-Hasan said: "Indeed, a servant's sins are all expiated by one night of fever."

In the Musnad and others, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) while he had a fever, and I placed my hand upon him over the quilt, and I found the heat of the fever. I said: "How intense is your fever, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: "So it is with us, O company of prophets; our pain is doubled so that our reward may be doubled." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, who among people is most severely tested?" He said: "The prophets." I said: "Then who?" He said: "The righteous. A man may be tested with poverty until he finds nothing but a cloak, which he rips and wears; and a man may be tested with lice until they kill him, and that was more beloved to them than gifts are to you."

Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no deed except that it is sealed upon. When the believer falls ill, the angels say: 'O our Lord, Your servant so-and-so has been kept from his deed?'

The Lord, the Exalted, says: 'Seal for him the like of his deed until he recovers or dies.'"

Abu Hurairah said: "When a Muslim servant falls ill, the one on the right is called: 'Record for My servant what he used to do while he was healthy,' and it is said to the one on the left: 'Refrain from My servant as long as he is in My bond.'"

A man said in the presence of Abu Hurairah: "Would that I were never free of lying ill!"

Abu Hurairah said: "The servant hates sins."

Mentioned by Ibn Abi al-Dunya.

Also mentioned from Hilal ibn Bassaq, who said: We were sitting with Ammar ibn Yasir, and they mentioned ailments. A Bedouin said: "I have never been ill at all." Ammar said: "Are you not one of us, or are you not one of us?!" Indeed, the Muslim is tested with a trial, and his sins are removed from him as leaves are shed from a tree. But the disbeliever, or he said the wicked person, is tested with a calamity, and his likeness is that of a camel: if it is released, it does not know why it was released, and if it is tied, it does not know why it was tied.

It is mentioned from Abu Ma'mar al-Azdi, who said: Whenever we heard from Ibn Mas'ud something we disliked, we would keep silent until he explained it to us. One day he said to us: "Indeed, sickness is not recorded as a reward for anyone." This troubled us and weighed heavily on us. He said: "But it expiates sin by it." This pleased us and we were delighted.

This is from the completeness of his knowledge and understanding (may Allah be pleased with him), for reward is only given for voluntary deeds and what is produced from them, as Allah, glorified is He, mentioned both types at the end of Surah al-Tawbah in His saying concerning the direct act of spending and crossing a valley: ﴿except that it is written for them﴾.

And concerning what is produced from thirst, fatigue, and hunger in His way, and the enraging of the disbelievers: ﴿except that there is written for them thereby a righteous deed﴾. So reward is tied to these two types.

As for illnesses and calamities, their reward is the expiation of sins, and therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever calamity befalls you is because of what your hands have earned﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) only said regarding calamities: "Allah expiates by it some of his sins," as the wording of his statements has already been mentioned.

Likewise his saying: "Sickness is an expiation." So acts of obedience raise degrees, and calamities remove misdeeds. Therefore he said: "Whoever Allah wills good for, He afflicts with it," and he said: "Whoever Allah wills good for, He grants him understanding in the religion." So this raises, and that expiates sins.

Yazid ibn Maysarah said: Indeed a servant falls ill while he has no good deed with Allah, so Allah, glorified is He, reminds him of some of his past sins, and there comes from his eye like the head of a fly of tears out of fear of Allah. Then Allah raises him, if He raises him, purified, or takes him, if He takes him, purified.

This is not contradicted by the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the reward of one whose child and the fruit of whose heart Allah has taken, that He builds for him a house in Paradise and names it the House of Praise.

[Section: The Effects of Love]

Love has effects, consequences, necessary implications, and rulings, whether it is praiseworthy or blameworthy, beneficial or harmful: from ecstasy, taste, sweetness, longing, intimacy, connection with the Beloved and nearness to Him, separation from Him and distance from Him, aversion and estrangement, joy and happiness, weeping and sorrow, and other of its rulings and necessary implications.

Praiseworthy love is the beneficial love which brings to its possessor what benefits him in his worldly life and his Hereafter, and this love is the sign of happiness. Harmful love is that which brings to its possessor what harms him in his worldly life and his Hereafter, and it is the sign of wretchedness.

It is known that the sound, rational living being does not choose love for what harms him and makes him wretched; such choice arises only from ignorance and wrongdoing. The soul may desire what harms it and does not benefit it, and this is the wronging of a person to himself: either by the soul being ignorant of the state of its beloved, so that it desires a thing and loves it without knowing the harm in loving it, and this is the state of one who follows his desire without knowledge; or by the soul knowing the harm in loving it, but preferring its desire over its knowledge. Its love may be composed of two matters: corrupt belief, which is blameworthy, and this is the state of one who follows conjecture and what souls desire. So corrupt love arises only from ignorance, or corrupt belief, or overpowering desire, or what is composed of these, such that some aid others. So doubt and lust combine: a doubt by which truth is confused with falsehood and the matter of the beloved is made attractive to him, and a lust which calls him to obtain it. Thus the army of doubt and lust assists one another against the army of intellect and faith, and victory belongs to the stronger of the two.

When this is understood, the consequences of every kind of love take the ruling of what they follow. Praiseworthy beneficial love, which is the sign of the servant's happiness, and all its consequences are beneficial to him; so their ruling is the ruling of what they follow. If he weeps, it benefits him; if he grieves, it benefits him; if he rejoices, it benefits him; if he is constricted, it benefits him; if he is expanded, it benefits him. He moves through the stations of love and its rulings in increase, gain and strength.

Harmful blameworthy love: all its consequences and effects are harmful to its possessor, distancing him from his Lord, however he turns through its effects and descends through its stations, he is in loss and distance.

This is the case with every act that arises from obedience or disobedience. Whatever arises from obedience is an increase and nearness for its possessor, and whatever arises from disobedience is loss and distance for its possessor. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is because they do not suffer thirst or fatigue or hunger in the way of Allah, nor do they tread a path that enrages the disbelievers, nor do they inflict on an enemy any injury, except that a righteous deed is written for them thereby. Indeed, Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good. And they spend no expenditure, small or large, nor do they cross a valley, except that it is written for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [At-Tawbah: 120-121].

So in the first verse Allah, glorified is He, informed that what arises from their obedience and actions is recorded for them as a righteous deed, and in the second He informed that their righteous deeds which they directly performed are recorded for them in themselves. The difference between them: the first is not their own act, but arose from it, so there is recorded for them thereby a righteous deed; the second is the very deed itself, so it is recorded for them.

Let the one slain by love ponder this section with true pondering, so that he may know what is for him and what is against him.

Poet:
"He will know on the Day of Presentation what merchandise he lost, and what he had gained at the weighing."

God, Exalted is He, urged the believers to seek understanding of the religion (tafaqquh, meaning to learn it) and to warn their people when they return to them (tanbih, meaning to teach).

There is a difference of opinion about the verse. It was said that the meaning is: the believers should not all go forth to seek understanding and learning. Rather, from each group among them, a party should go forth to gain understanding, and then return to teach those who stayed behind. On this reading, the going forth (nafir) is a going forth for learning. The word ṭā'ifa (party) is applied to one person or more, and they said this is evidence for accepting the report of a single narrator (khabar al-wāḥid). Al-Shāfi'ī and a group of scholars interpreted it this way.

Another group said: the meaning is that the believers should not all go forth to jihad. Rather, a party should go forth for jihad, and another group should remain behind to gain understanding of the religion. When the party that went forth comes back, those who stayed behind should instruct them in what was revealed of the religion, the lawful and the unlawful. On this reading, the words ﴿liyatafaqqahū﴾ (that they may gain understanding) and ﴿liyundhirū﴾ (that they may warn) refer to the group from which a party went forth.

This is the view of most scholars. On this reading, the going forth is a going forth for jihad according to its original meaning, since wherever the word is used, jihad is what is understood from it. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives﴾.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no migration after the Conquest, but there is jihad and intention. And when you are called to go forth, then go forth."

This is the well-known meaning of this term. On both views, the verse encourages seeking understanding of the religion, learning it, and teaching it, for that is equal to jihad, and may even be better than it.

(Benefit)

When a past-tense verb follows the particle of urging (ḥarf al-taḥḍīḍ, the particle expressing urging or reproach), it may also be used for either past or future meaning, as in God's words: ﴿Why did not a party from every group among them go forth, that they might gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them?﴾

The correct view is that the past tense here remains in its original form and does not change, as in God's words: ﴿Why were there not, among the generations before you, people of virtue?﴾

It is as if one were saying: "Why did you not fear God in what you did?" The verse was revealed concerning the Battle of Tabuk, in the context of blaming those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So God informed that the believers had not been going to go forth all together, then He rebuked them with a rebuke that contains an exhortation that some of them should go forth and some should remain behind.

The more correct of the two views is that a party from among them goes forth in the raids (sarāyā) and expeditions (ba'ūth), while another party remains behind to gain understanding of the religion, then warns those who stayed behind the party that went forth when they return to them, and informs them of what was revealed after them of the lawful, the unlawful, and the rulings. This is for several reasons:

First: the verse is in the context of going forth for jihad and rebuking those who stay behind from it.

Second: going forth (nafir) is only for a raid, and one does not say of someone who travels to seek knowledge that he has gone forth or been called forth, nor is such travel called nafir.

Third: the verse includes a statement of the ruling on those who go forth and those who remain, and of their partnership in jihad and knowledge. The ones who go forth are the people of jihad, and the ones who remain are the people of understanding, and the religion is only complete through jihad and knowledge. When one party is occupied with jihad and another with understanding of the religion, and then the people of understanding teach the fighters when they return to them, the benefit is achieved through both knowledge and jihad. This is more fitting to the verse and more complete for its meaning.

As for the view that makes the going forth in it a going forth for seeking knowledge, then there is no reference to jihad in it, and the going forth is removed from its place.

What led those who claim that the going forth is for seeking knowledge to this view is that they saw that the pronoun refers to the nearest previous noun: the ones who warn are the ones who go forth, and they are the ones who gain understanding.

The answer to this is that the pronoun returns to the nearest antecedent when there is no obstacle that requires a more distant one. We have shown that the context requires that the one who remains is the one who gains understanding and warns the one who goes forth and returns.

The point is that the verb nafara in the verse is in the past tense, and it is understood as referring to the future only because the particle of urging indicates this. The precise view on this point is that the words lawlā (why not) and hallā (why not) if used purely for rebuke, the past tense does not change from its form. If they are used purely for urging, the verb changes to refer to the future. If it is a rebuke that carries the sense of urging, it is suitable for both meanings. If it comes after kullamā (whenever), it may be intended for the past, as in God's words: ﴿Every time a messenger came to a nation, they denied him﴾.

It may also be intended for the future, as in His words: ﴿Whenever their skins are roasted, We will replace them with other skins﴾.

The author of al-Tashīl (Ibn Mālik) thought that when a verb follows a relative pronoun (ṣila), it may refer to the future, arguing from God's words: ﴿except those who repent before you have power over them; so know that God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

This is an error on his part, may God have mercy on him. The verb is past in both form and meaning, and what is intended is: except those whose repentance came before you gained power over them, so you let them go. The future sense he saw comes from the conditional meaning contained in the sentence. The meaning is: "whoever repents before you gain power over him, so you let him go." This meaning does not come from the relative clause itself. If the relative clause were stripped of the conditional sense, the verb would be only past in both form and meaning, as in God's words: ﴿those to whom people said﴾.

[Section: The Meaning of God's Requirement to Accept the Warning of One Who Goes Forth to Gain Understanding of the Religion]

[What is meant by God's requirement to accept the warning of one who goes forth to gain understanding of the religion]

The fifty-seventh point: your saying: "God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Why did not a party from every group among them go forth, that they might gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them?﴾ So He made it obligatory to accept their warning, and that is taqlid (blind following) of them." The answer to this comes in several ways:

One: God, glorified is He, only made it obligatory to accept what they warned them of from the revelation that descends in their absence from the Prophet (ﷺ) during jihad. Where, then, in this is proof for the party of taqlid (blind following) in preferring the opinions of men over revelation?

Two: the verse is a clear proof against them, for He, glorified is He, divided their worship and their upholding of His command into two kinds: one is going forth for jihad, and the second is gaining understanding of the religion. He made the upholding of the religion through these two groups, namely the rulers and the scholars, the people of jihad and the people of knowledge. So the ones who go forth fight on behalf of those who remain, and those who remain preserve knowledge for those who go forth. When they return from their going forth, they make up for what they missed of knowledge by the reports of those who heard it from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Here there are two views among people about the verse:

One: the meaning is: "Why did not a party from every group go forth to gain understanding and warn those who remain?" Then the meaning concerns seeking knowledge. This is the view of al-Shāfi'ī and a group of exegetes, and they used it as an argument for accepting the report of a single narrator, since the ṭā'ifa (party) need not be the number required for mass transmission (tawātur).

The second: the meaning is: "Why did not a party from every group go forth to fight, so that those who remain may gain understanding and warn those who went forth for jihad when they return to them and inform them of what was revealed after them." This is the view of most scholars, and it is the correct one, because going forth is only going out for jihad, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And when you are called to go forth, then go forth."

Also, the word "believers" is general, including those who stayed with the Prophet (ﷺ) and those who were absent from him, and those who stayed are certainly intended, for they are the leaders of the believers. How, then, would the word not include them? On the view of those scholars, "believers" would be restricted to those absent from him only. The meaning would be: "The believers should not all go forth to him, so why did not a party from every group go forth to him?"

This goes against the apparent meaning of the word "believers," and removes the word "going forth" from its meaning in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. On both views, there is nothing in the verse that requires the validity of blind following that is condemned. Rather, it is proof against its corruption and invalidity. For warning is only established by proof. Whoever is not confronted by proof has not been warned, just as the warner is one who establishes proof. Whoever does not bring proof is not a warner. If you call that taqlid, then the matter is not about names. We do not deny taqlid in this sense, so call it whatever you wish. What we deny is setting up a particular man whose word is made the measure over the Qur'an and the Sunnahs: what agrees with his word is accepted and what contradicts it is not accepted. His word is accepted without proof, and the word of his equal, or one more knowledgeable than him, whose proof is with him, is rejected. This is what we reject, and every scholar on the face of the earth openly declares his rejection of it and condemns it and its adherents.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 9, verse 124–125:

If it is said: a thing may be attributed to another thing because it accompanies it, even if the latter has no effect on it, as in the words of God Most High: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, among them are some who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾.

It is known that the surah did not cause them any increase in uncleanness; rather, the increase in their uncleanness coincided with its descent, so it was attributed to it?

It is said: The matter is not confined to these two things you have mentioned, namely that the surah caused the uncleanness, and the second, that it coincided with its descent. Rather, there is a third matter: when the surah was sent down, its descent required belief in it, affirmation, submission to its commands and prohibitions, and acting upon what it contains. The believers prepared themselves for this, and so their faith increased through it; hence the increase in faith was attributed to it, since it was the cause of that increase. The disbelievers denied it, rejected it, denied the one who brought it, and prepared themselves to oppose and reject what it contained; thereby their uncleanness increased, and it was attributed to it, since its descent and its reaching them was the cause of that increase. How does this compare with the attribution of foul acts to God, which you deem impermissible, when they are called to faith and to reflect upon His signs? Their foul acts are not attributed to God the Exalted; they are attributed to them. What is attributed to Him, glory be to Him, are His good and beautiful acts, which contain praiseworthy ends and sought-after wisdoms. Sealing, stamping, locking, and misguidance are good acts from God, which He placed in the most fitting places for them, since nothing other than them is suitable for that wicked place. Shirk, disbelief, sins, and injustice are their foul acts, which are not attributed to God as an act, though they are attributed to Him as creation: their creation is other than them, and the creation is other than the created, the act other than the acted upon, the decree other than the decreed, and the measure other than the measured. This question will come to you fully, God willing, in the chapter on the combination of contentment with the decree and displeasure with disbelief, sinfulness and disobedience, God willing.

The Qadariyya said: When they reached such a level of disbelief that no path to faith remained for them except through compulsion and coercion, and His wisdom did not require that He compel them to faith (lest the wisdom of obligation be nullified), He expressed the abandonment of compulsion and coercion with sealing and stamping, to inform them that they had gone so far in disbelief and aversion that they would desist only through coercion. That is the ultimate description of their obstinacy and persistence in disbelief.

The People of the Sunnah said: This statement is false. He, glory be to Him, is able to create in them the will, desire, and love of faith, so that they believe without coercion or compulsion, but with voluntary faith and obedience, as God Most High said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on the earth would have believed, all of them together﴾. Faith under coercion and compulsion is not called faith; for this reason all people will believe on the Day of Resurrection, yet that is not called faith, because it comes from compulsion and necessity. God Most High said: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾. What is attained by the souls of knowledge and affirmation through compulsion, necessity, and coercion is not called guidance. Likewise His words: ﴿Have not those who believed despaired that, if God willed, He would have guided all mankind?﴾

Your statement that no path to faith remained except through coercion is therefore false, for there remained for their faith a path that God did not show them, namely His will, His grace, His inspiration, and His inclining of their hearts toward guidance and keeping them upon the straight path. That is a matter the Lord of everything and its Sovereign is not incapable of; rather, He is able to do it, just as He is able to create their essences, attributes, and forelocks. But He withheld that for His wisdom and justice concerning them, and because they did not merit or deserve that it be granted to them, just as lowness is denied the qualities of height, heat is denied the qualities of cold, and the wicked is denied the qualities of the good. It should not be said: "Why did He do this?" For that is among the requirements of His dominion and lordship, and among the implications of His names and attributes. Is it fitting for His wisdom to equate the good and the wicked, the beautiful and the ugly, the excellent and the inferior? Among the requirements of lordship is the creation of pairs and the diversification and varieties of created beings.

So the saying of one who asks, "Why did He create the inferior, the wicked, and the base?" is the question of one ignorant of His names, attributes, dominion, and lordship. He, glory be to Him, distinguished between His creatures with the greatest distinction, and this is from the perfection of His power and lordship. He made some of them receive every perfection that is possible, and some of them receive none of it, and between these are varying degrees that none can enumerate except the All-Creating, the All-Knowing. He guides every soul to attain what it is capable of. The receiver, the received, and the receptivity are all His creation, the effect of His act and His creating. This is what the Jabriyya and the Qadariyya departed from, and did not come to know. And success is from God.

And as for *al-sarf* (turning away), God Most High says: ﴿When a surah is revealed, some of them look at others, [asking], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. God has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ He informs us of their action, which is turning away, and of His action toward them, which is turning their hearts away from the Qur'an and from reflecting upon it, because they are not fit for it. The place (the heart) is therefore neither suitable nor receptive.

The suitability of the place depends on two things: sound understanding and sound intention.

These people's hearts do not understand, and their intentions are corrupt. God Most High has stated this explicitly in His words: ﴿Had God known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And had He made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.﴾ Thus He informs us that faith is not receptive in them, and that there is no good in them through which faith could enter their hearts. He did not make them hear with the kind of hearing that yields understanding and benefit. Even if they heard it in the sense that the proof is established against them, the kind of understanding-hearing through which the believers heard was not attained by them. Then He informs us of another barrier that is present in their hearts and prevents them from faith even if He had made them hear. This is the special kind of hearing, namely arrogance, turning away, and aversion. The first is a barrier to understanding; the second is a barrier to submission and yielding.

Their understanding is corrupt, their intentions are base, and this is the mark of misguidance and the sign of wretchedness, just as the mark of guidance and the sign of happiness are sound understanding and righteous intention. And God is the One sought for help.

Consider His words: ﴿Then they turned away; God turned their hearts away﴾, and how He made this second clause, whether it is a statement or a repetition, a punishment for their turning away. He punished them for it with a turning away other than the first one. Their turning away was due to His not willing and not intending to turn them toward Him, because there was no suitability or acceptance in them. So they did not attain the turning toward Him and submission, and their hearts turned away from the Qur'an because of the ignorance and wrongdoing within them. Therefore He recompensed them with a turning other than the first, just as He recompensed the deviation of their hearts from guidance with a deviation other than the first deviation, as He said: ﴿So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate.﴾ Likewise, when a servant turns away from his Lord, Glorified is He, He recompenses him by turning away from him, so that He does not enable him to turn toward Him. Let the story of Iblis be a reminder from which you benefit most fully. When he disobeyed his Lord, Exalted is He, and did not submit to His command, and persisted in that, He punished him by making him one who calls to every act of disobedience. He punished him for his first disobedience by making him a caller to every act of disobedience and its branches, minor and major. This turning away and disbelief became a punishment for that earlier turning away and disbelief. So among the punishments for an evil deed is an evil deed following it, just as among the rewards for a good deed is a good deed following it.

If it is said: How does His denial to them of turning away and aversion from Him fit with His saying: ﴿So where are you turned?﴾ and ﴿How are they deluded?﴾ and His saying: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder?﴾ If He is the One who turned them away and made them averse and deluded, how can He blame them for that?

It is said: They are caught between His justice and His proof against them. He enabled them, opened the door for them, laid out the path for them, and prepared the means for them. He sent His messengers to them, sent down His books to them, and called them through the tongues of His messengers. He gave them minds to distinguish between good and evil, between what benefits and what harms, and between the causes of ruin and the causes of success. He gave them hearing and sight. But they preferred desire over piety, chose blindness over guidance, and said: "Your disobedience is dearer to us than your obedience, polytheism is more beloved to us than your monotheism, and worshipping other than you is more beneficial to us in our worldly life than worshipping you." Thus their hearts turned away from their Lord, their Creator, and their Sovereign, and turned away from obeying Him and loving Him. This is His justice toward them, and that is His proof against them. They closed the door of guidance upon themselves by their own will and choice, so He closed it upon them by necessity. He left them to what they chose for themselves, entrusted them with what they abandoned, empowered them in what they approved, and admitted them through the door they rushed toward. And He closed off from them the door from which they turned away, while they were averse. There is nothing more ugly than their action, and nothing more beautiful than His action. Had He willed, He would have created them with other attributes and brought them into being in another state. But He, Glorified is He, is the Creator of the high and the low, the light and the darkness, the beneficial and the harmful, the good and the wicked, the angels and the devils, the women and the flies, and the Giver of their instruments, attributes, powers, and actions, and the One who employs them for what they were created. Some of them act by their natures, and some by their will and volition. All of that proceeds according to His wisdom; it necessitates His praise and demands His holy perfection and His absolute dominion. What creatures know of this bears no comparison to what remains hidden from them in any way. It is no more than the amount a sparrow takes from the sea.

Ibn al-Qayyim's Commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 9, verses 128–129:

[A note: The thirty-fifth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ), after the prayers]

al-Hafiz Abu Musa and others mentioned it, and they cited nothing about this except an account that Abu Musa al-Madini related through the route of Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Hasib say: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar told me: I was with Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid when al-Shibli came. Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid stood up for him, embraced him, and kissed him between his eyes. I said to him: "O my master, do you do this to al-Shibli, when you and everyone in Baghdad consider him to be insane?"

He said to me: "I did with him what I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) doing with him. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a dream when al-Shibli approached, and he stood up for him and kissed him between his eyes. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you do this to al-Shibli?' He said: 'He recites after his prayer: ﴿Certainly there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves...﴾ to its end, and follows it with blessings upon me.'"

In another narration, [it is said] that he did not perform an obligatory prayer without reciting after it ﴿Certainly there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to the end of the surah, and saying three times: "May Allah bless you, O Muhammad."

He said: When al-Shibli entered, I asked him about what he recites after the prayer, and he mentioned the same.
